name: 24 (Stern 2009)
desc:
Jack Bauer is back, but this time in Stern Pinball's new 24 pinball machine.

Stern Pinball takes FOX's hit television show and turns it into one fast-paced pinball machine that will excite both operators and homeowners.

desc: 250 cc is a pinball table with the theme of motorcycle sport, developed and published by the spanish INDER, which was released in Europe in 1992.

name: 300 (Gottlieb 1975)
desc: The two outlanes on the playfield of production games each have their text description of "Adds Bonus" appearing above their rollover switches and inside an area painted blue. In contrast, the playfield in the manufacturer's flyer shows these blue areas appearing below the rollover switches and, unfortunately, the text they contain are obscured from view. The flyer game may be a Sample game or an Early Production game.

name: 301 Bullseye (Grand Products 1986)
desc: 301/Bullseye is a pub darts themed pinball machine from 1986, manufactured by Grand Products Inc. It was designed as a retrofit for all electronic 4 player games except the wide body styled ones and included all the glass, decals and a new drop in playfield and sound and lamp modules.

name: 4 Aces (Williams 1970)
desc:
4 Aces was produced by Williams Electronic in 1970.

Notable Features: Flippers (4), Slingshots (2), Hanging targets (7), Standup targets (2), Stop magnets (2), Spinning posts, Left and right dual outlanes. Player presses button on lockdown bar to shoot ball into play from between the flippers. Pressing the flipper buttons triggers the upper flippers first then the lower ones. Ball hitting either of two hanging targets when lit for Bonus is stopped by an electromagnet and released after bonus points are scored. Lighting the playing cards along the top of backglass awards Special and is a carry-over feature. Cabinet measures 24 1/4 inches wide.

Design by: Steve Kordek

name: 4 Queens (Bally 1970)
desc:
This pretty lady themed pinball has Skill-Shot Special Center Top Rollover scores special when 3* Queens are lit. (*Adjustable)
Features:
Kickout Hole scores 3000 when mystery lit. Also "spots" next letter.
Kickout Bonus scores up to 5000. Bonus advance on mystery basis.
-2 Extra "Spot" Letter Targets
Hit bumpers A, B, C in rotation to light bumper D. Hit bumper D when lit to light next Queen.
Sudden Special when 4 Queens are lit.
Flipper-Zipper-closes flipper gap, keeps ball busy on playfield.
4 QUEENS packed with action to pack the coin box!

name: 4 Square (Gottlieb 1971)
desc: 4 Square is a pinball machine designed by Ed Krynski and produced by Gottlieb in 1971. 4 Square is an electro-mechanical pinball machine and there were 2,200 units produced. 4 Square features 2 flippers, 3 pop bumpers, 2 slingshots and 8 standup targets. The maximum point score displayed is only 9,999 points.

name: 4x4 (Atari 1983)
desc: The 4x4 was a prototype pinball machine designed by Atari in 1983. Only two machines were ever produced, making it a very rare machine.

id: Charlie Brown Christmas, A (Original 2023)/Charlie Brown Christmas, A (Original 2023) 1.2.vpx
name: A Charlie Brown Christmas (Original 2023)
desc:
Find the real meaning of Christmas in A Charlie Brown Christmas Pinball! Join the Peanuts crew in putting on a play and decorating the most perfect tree there is.
Table features:
- Snowflakes fall on the playfield, shoot the ball to eat them before they melt
- Feed Snoopy a snack by shooting his bowl
- Choose the perfect Christmas tree by shooting the right lanes
- Decorate Snoopy's house in Multiball to win the Lights and Display contest
- Direct the play in the Wizard mode and bring the Peanuts crew together to celebrate!

id: Aaron Spelling (Data East 1992)/Aaron Spinlling (Data East 1992) v1.02.vpx
name: Aaron Spelling (Data East 1992)
desc:
The Aaron Spelling pinball machine is one of the rarest and most exclusive pinball machines ever created. Produced by Data East in February 1992, it was never intended for public sale.

The machine was commissioned by Spelling's wife, Candy Spelling, as a personalized gift for his birthday, and only 3 units were ever manufactured. Reports suggest the commissioning cost was approximately $170,000.

It is a modified version of the Lethal Weapon 3 table. The backglass and playfield feature various TV shows produced by Spelling, including Dynasty, Charlie's Angels, The Love Boat, and Beverly Hills, 90210.

name: ABBA (Original 2020)
desc:
The Abba Visual Pinball v2.0, released in 2020, is a digital pinball table dedicated to the iconic Swedish pop group ABBA. Created by Gray Ghost with contributions from JPSalas and STAT, this table is notable for its attention to detail and its homage to the legendary music group known for hits during the 70s and 80s. The game is built on the platform of "Vortex," a game originally by Taito in 1981, ensuring that it has a strong foundation in pinball gameplay mechanics.
One of the unique aspects of this table is its approach to incorporating ABBA's music. Due to copyright restrictions, the game itself doesn't come with ABBA's songs pre-installed. Instead, players are encouraged to add their music by downloading MP3 files and adjusting the game's script to include them, which allows for a personalized soundtrack that respects copyright laws​​​​.
The table is appreciated for its nice graphics and engaging playfield, which features various targets and obstacles that resonate with ABBA's musical journey. Players have lauded its design and the overall gaming experience it offers, with some viewing it as a valuable addition to their digital pinball collection​​​​.

name: Abra Ca Dabra
desc:
With its mysterious magic and sorcery theme and unique layout, Abra Ca Dabra is one of the most beloved games released by Gottlieb in the mid-1970s.
The game features a moving lit drop target that will score an indicated bonus value, a value which is increased by completing the rollover sequence or hitting the centre target after collecting all the drop targets. The same layout appeared in Gottlieb's soccer themed games Team One and Kicker.

id: AC-DC LUCI Premium (Stern 2013)/AC-DC LUCI Premium VR (Stern 2013) v1.1.3.vpx
name: AC/DC LUCI Premium (Stern 2013)
desc:
Because of AC/DC's tremendous success for both us and Stern, Stern Pinball is introducing another Premium model. The AC/DC Luci Premium (short for Lucifer) has new cabinet, translight and mini-playfield art. These do not do justice to the this stunning game. When you see Luci in person, you will be as excited as I everyone will be.
The art features a drawing of Luci reminiscent of pinball art “back in the day” – an artist rendition of a hot pinball lady. She is drawn over a bright red and black background adapted from AC/DC album art. Luci game play and rules remain the same that Steve Ritchie, Lyman Sheats and their team created for AC/DC Premium and Limited Edition. And Luci has the 12 great AC/DC hits from the Stern AC/DC games.

name: Ace Of Speed
desc: A homebrew mod of Bally's 1989 table "Mousin' Around!" for Visual Pinball X themed around American cars, tattoos and pin-ups.

id: Adventures Of Rocky And Bullwinkle and Friends 1993 (Data East)/Adventures of Rocky & Bullwinkle And Friends 1.06.vpx
name: Adventures of Rocky & Bullwinkle And Friends
desc:
Adventures of Rocky and Bullwinkle and Friends was a pinball machine released by Data East in 1993. It  brought the wacky world of Rocky, Bullwinkle, and their foes to life on the pinball table.
Based on the classic cartoon "The Adventures of Rocky and Bullwinkle and Friends"
The table features various ramps, spinners, and targets that correspond to different characters and events from the show. Players can rack up points by hitting these targets and completing specific objectives.
The playfield artwork depicts iconic locations from the cartoon like Frostbite Falls and Pottsylvania.  It also features  recognizable characters like Boris Badenov, Natasha Fatale, and Fearless Leader.

name: Aerosmith (Original 2019)
desc:
Aerosmith is a original pinball table released in 2019.
The game is themed around the famous rock group of the same name – specifically, it's touted as "reflect(ing) the high-energy and excitement that accompanies the experience of a live Aerosmith concert." As the band plays on, the player must get through nine modes based on their songs, including "Rats in the Cellar", "Dude Looks Like a Lady", "Sweet Emotion", "Walk This Way", "Last Child", "Same Old Song and Dance", and "Back in the Saddle".

name: Aerosmith (Stern 2017)
desc: Stern Pinball's Aerosmith machines reflect the high-energy and excitement that accompanies the experience of a live Aerosmith concert. Players will rock to nine famous Aerosmith hits in the concert arena playfield and embark on an exhilarating pinball experience. Players score points and finish game objectives to raise the audience's levels of energy, thrill and enjoyment. Higher scores amplify the experience–the higher the energy level, the bigger and louder the show–resulting in an Aerosmith pinball experience that cannot be matched.

name: Agents 777
desc: Agents 777, released by Game Plan Inc. in October 1984, is a solid-state pinball machine with a unique cartoonish gangster theme. Designed by Ed Cebula with artwork by Larry M. Blazek, the game features three flippers, three pop bumpers, a spinner, and three drop targets.

name: Airborne
desc:
Visual Pinball Airborne is a digital recreation of a pinball machine originally released by Capcom in 1996. It's not an official product, but rather a fan-made table created for the Visual Pinball X (VPX) pinball simulator software.
Simulates the play of the physical Airborne pinball machine.
Aims to be as accurate as possible in terms of table layout, graphics, sounds, and physics.
Offers the same challenges and scoring opportunities as the original game.

id: Al's Garage Band Goes On a Wold Tour 1992 (Alvin G.)/Al's Garage Band Goes On A World Tour (AlvinG 1992) v2.5.2.vpx
name: Al's Garage Band Goes On A World Tour
desc:
Al's Garage Band Goes on a World Tour is a virtual pinball table based on a 1992 pinball machine of the same name by Alvin G.
Classic pinball mechanics with flippers, slingshots, pop bumpers, and ramps.
Hitting targets and completing objectives progresses the band's world tour, represented on the playfield and backglass.
Different tour locations offer unique scoring opportunities and challenges.

name: Aladdin (Original 2026) Tombg
desc:
Here's a brand new creation, made entirely from scratch, on which I spent quite a bit of time (around 7-8 months)... I'll probably update it based on your feedback, but only if it's relevant. I probably won't respond to minor personal issues, sorry. It's a table that's both complex in terms of gameplay (you need to spend some time to get a decent score) and in terms of code, so please don't be too negative in your comments. I was mainly inspired by my Super Nintendo console games and the 1992 Disney animated film to set the mood.
Like in my childhood games, this game had a cheat mode that allowed you to skip levels to progress in adventure mode. So I added a similar progression option to the F12 menu. I recommend using it to jump straight to mode 1 when this mode (collecting the magic lamp to make wishes) starts to feel too repetitive. Each story progression mode takes place in the underground mode!

Table requirements:

- VPX 64-bit version 10.8.0 (or higher)
- Pinup: Version 1.5.2 (or higher) Please do not message me if you are not using Pinup or if your system is not up to date. This table is designed exclusively for use with the latest generation PupDmd.
- DoF: needs updating

Thanks to two of my best friends in the SuperTilted community for their help:
- @Burger for the Nfozzy sounds for the table and his daily support
- @Gman for the PupPack videos (this guy needs to be limited, he's such a video fanatic, lol)
- For everything else, thanks to myself 😊
Happy gaming everyone.

name: Aladdin's Castle (Bally 1976)
desc: Aladdin's Castle, released by Bally in June 1976, features a fantasy theme centered around Aladdin and his magical adventures. Designed by Greg Kmiec and illustrated by Christian Marche, this electro-mechanical pinball machine incorporates a colorful and engaging playfield with three flippers, three pop bumpers, two standup targets, and a unique horseshoe lane.

name: Algar (Williams 1980)
desc: The Algar pinball machine, produced by Williams in 1980, is a solid-state game with a wide-body cabinet and digital display, designed for up to four players. It features two flippers and no ramps or multiball options, reflecting a classic pinball style from the early 80s. With only 349 units produced, Algar is a rare find in the pinball community. The game's design was led by Tony Kraemer, with distinctive artwork by Constantino and Jeanine Mitchell.

name: Ali (Stern 1980)
desc:
Ali is a Licensed Pinball Table that pays tribute to the legendary boxer Muhammad Ali. It was designed by famed pinball designer Harry Williams and released in 1980 by Stern Electronics. Like Muhammad Ali himself, this is a fast, bombastic game that never lets players forget who they're up against.
The table is festooned with famous Ali-isms, such as "I am the Greatest", "Three-Time Champ", "Ali Shuffle" and "Rope-A-Dope", all drawn with comic-style pop lettering. The center of the playfield has a portrait of Ali pointing at the player along with a facsimile of his signature, while the backglass features the boxer's face surrounded by his form in the ring. The game also supported the then-new Susan B. Anthony dollar coin, and gave players an extra game for using one.

name: Alien Poker
desc: This multiball game has some crazy fantasy alien gambling artwork. The 5 Bank Drop targets right in the middle of the playfield are the major targets for this game. You need to hit them in order to maximize the Royal Flush Value. You can also hit the 4 kings across the top of the playfield to multiply the royal flush value. There are other things to shoot for but the center drops with the top lane multipliers are you main shots. This particular machine is a beautiful example of this game.

name: Alien Star (Gottlieb 1984)
desc:
Alien Star is a pinball machine from June 1984, manufactured by D. Gottlieb & Co.

Journey to an Alien Star, for a pinball battle in space. Multiball, skill shots and plenty of fast action bring this fantasy world alive for your players.

name: Aliens (Original 2005)
desc:
Recaptures the events of the highly-acclaimed 1986 film and sequel to Alien, where Ellen Ripley joins a squad of galactic marines to investigate a colony for Xenomorphs and are all drawn into a deadly struggle to eradicate them all.

This table was released as part of Zen Studio's Alien vs. Pinball mini collection. All three tables were available simultaneously on April 26, 2016, coinciding with what is known as "Alien Day" (due to the month and day numbers forming the code number of the colony where Aliens takes place in, LV-426) and marking the 30th anniversary of Aliens.

The tables can be purchased separately as DLC in the games Zen Pinball 2, Pinball FX 2 and Pinball FX 3, as well as in the Zen Pinball mobile app.

The three tables are also free-to-play in the downloadable Aliens vs. Pinball mobile app. An Internet connection is required to play any of the three tables, and only Alien vs. Predator is available from the start. To unlock the other two tables, the player must complete three challenges each on the unlocked tables. Advertisements will play at the beginning of a new session, but they can be removed for a particular table (or for all tables), along with the need for online connectivity through an in-app purchase.

Since most Alien media involve graphic violence and strong language that would not be appropriate for children, Zen Studios has omitted such content from the pinball adaptations, allowing only milder swear words like "damn" and "bastard" and brief splashes of alien goo when Xenomorph eggs are destroyed in the Alien vs. Predator table. This allows the overall Everyone 10+ ESRB rating to be maintained across all Zen Pinball titles, but results in a higher Teen rating for the Android version of the Aliens vs. Pinball app, as well as a 12+ rating on the App Store for its iOS version.

name: Amazon Hunt (Gottlieb 1983)
desc: Amazon Hunt is a pinball machine released by D. Gottlieb & Co. in September 1983. It has a jungle adventure theme with two flippers, no ramps, and no multiball. Designed by Ed Krynski with artwork by Larry Day, it is part of the Gottlieb System 80A series and had a production run of 1,515 units.

id: America's Most Haunted 2014 (Spooky Pinball)/America's Most Haunted (Spooky Pinball 2014)_Bigus(MOD)2.0.vpx
name: America's Most Haunted
desc:
America's Most Haunted is unique for being the first pinball game inspired by a podcast.
The genesis of this game came when Charlie Emery, creator and host of the Spooky Pinball podcast, hooked up with Video Game-console modder and internet celebrity Benjamin Heckendorn, a.k.a. Ben Heck. Heck, already (in)famous for building his own Bill Paxton pinball table, became inspired to develop a game combining Emery's love of pinball and all things paranormal. Emery, in turn, was inspired to start his own company to manufacture and sell it to collectors of boutique pinballs.
The game itself is about the wacky antics of four amateur Reality Show ghost hunters as they search for evidence of ghosts in various haunted venues. Visit places like the Abandoned Hospital, the Historic Theater, and the Haunted Bar, take photos of sneaky spectres, consult the Spirit Guide, then Complete Investigations for a chance to battle the six different Ghost Bosses. While the Ghost Minion on the playfield follows your ball, jump across the Theater Balcony, push open the Morgue Door, manipulate the haunted Hellivator to summon the Hotel Ghost, then use the high-tech and psychic powers of your team to clear each haunt. Color-changing LEDs and over a thousand comical quips keep things lively, but only the best will be able to Battle the Demon behind all the haunted happenings.

name: Andromeda (Game Plan 1985)
desc: Andromeda, released by Game Plan Inc. in September 1985, is a solid-state pinball machine known for its challenging gameplay and striking artwork by Paul Faris. Designed by Ed Cebula and Mike Kubin, it features two flippers, four pop bumpers, a bank of six drop targets, and a single spinning target.

id: Animal Crossing Pinball (Original 2021)/Animal Crossing Pinball (Original 2021) v1.1.vpx
name: Animal Crossing Pinball (Original 2021)
desc: Homebrew table for Visual Pinball X based on Nintendo's popular villiage-living social simulator.

name: Apache! (Playmatic 1975)
desc: Apache is an electro-mechanical table channeling a gritty underworld vibe (the term “apache” referred to Parisian gangsters), it features classic EM design with two flippers, pop bumpers, and mechanical scoring reels. Digitally recreated in VPX with authentic artwork restoration and optional VR/backglass support.

name: Apollo 13
desc:
Apollo 13 is a 1995 pinball game designed by Joe Balcer and Joe Kaminkow, released by Sega Pinball, based on the film of the same name. Kevin Bacon (Jack Swigert), Bill Paxton (Fred Haise), and Gary Sinise (Ken Mattingly) provided custom speech for this game.
This is a very dense pinball table; playfield toys include an elevating Saturn V rocket, a lunar LEM module, a countdown LED, and a rotating Moon. Collect orbits around the table to Advance the Spacecraft around the Moon and return to Earth, and perform various Apollo Missions along the way — perform a manual burn to straighten the orbiter, fix the Life Support systems, fix the CO2 scrubbers, and take care of the Master Alarm. For more points, shoot the Saturn and load up for multiball, or use gravitynote  to slingshot pinballs over the Moon. Even with all these features, the biggest appeal of the game is its 13 Ball Blastoff Multiball, where thirteen balls are unloaded onto the playfield. Up to six people can play at once, either individually or in teams, and the game offers "Novice" and "Wizard" difficulty settings for players.

name: Aqualand (Juegos Populares 1986)
desc: Aqualand is a solid-state pinball machine released by Juegos Populares, a Spanish manufacturer, in 1986. The game features a water amusement park theme, incorporating two flippers, two pop bumpers, two slingshots, a three-bank drop target, a standup target, a vari-target, a kick-out hole, and a rollunder spinner.

name: Aquaman
desc: Table taken from almost scratch from Gradius. Lots of Flashers on this table... Fan of mechanical pinball, move on :) I am not a Pincab pro (only for 1 year) and even less comfortable with vpx scripts.... Thank you in advance for your tolerance. If you have any bugs or other questions about how it works, I will try to answer. I also have other interesting personal MODs but on unauthorized tables, do not hesitate to contact me. I finalized a mini PUPPACK, sharing will be available in the coming days.

name: Arena
desc:
﻿Enter the Exciting World of ARENA. Gottlieb's Newest Hit by Premier Technology® combines the Challenge of Battle with the Power and Speed of Pinball.
- Using the Plunger as a "Skill Shot" propel yourself into the PIT area to score SPECIAL, EXTRA-BALL, 1 MILLION points, or RAMP VALUE. Now you enter the Main ARENA playfield.
- Shoot through the Spinner to complete the L-O-K Lanes. Lock 1 Ball, then 2 Balls and finally RELEASE for 3 Ball Action.
- Knock down the "WALL" targets and with only seconds to spare, Battle with the "GUARD" to light up EXTRA BALL in the PIT.
- Shoot the RAMP to increase RAMP VALUE. The RAMP opens the GATE to either "Return to Flipper" or "Back to the Plunger" to face the PIT.
- Making P-I-T Lanes lights I MILLION in the PIT.
- C-Y-S Targets Increase MULTIPLIER and lights SPECIAL.

id: Asterix the Twelve Tasks 2022 (Original)/Asterix the Twelve Tasks (Original 2022) 4.0.0.vpx
name: Asterix the Twelve Tasks
desc:
Based on the popular Asterix comic book series, particularly the story of Asterix's twelve tasks.
 It's a fan-made adaptation of a different virtual pinball table, so the core mechanics might be similar to the original but with an Asterix makeover.

name: Atlantis
desc:
Single player wedgehead cabinet design. Two pop bumpers at the top of the playfield, two slingshots, two 3" flippers, a bank of 10 drop targets on the left, and on the right a dual lane of rollover switches.
This dual row of vertical rollovers was used in other games like Gottlieb Sheriff pinball and Gottlieb Lawman. In fact, Gottlieb Atlantis pinball is basically the one player version of Gottlieb's Sheriff/Lawman.
Skill shot: plunge the lit yellow lane. Note the lane changes with top slingshot hits, so allow for and count your bounces!
Note the right flipper has up-and-outlane risk. Don't make the mistake of holding the right flipper up when the ball is coming fast towards it and having the ball roll up and out the right side.
Hit drop targets in pairs [5000 vs. 500], shoot lit yellow lanes [3000 vs. 500] and targets [3000 vs. 500].

id: Attack and Revenge from Mars 2015 (Bally)/Attack and Revenge from Mars v4.3.vpx
name: Attack and Revenge from Mars
desc:
Attack and Revenge from Mars isn't actually a single, official Visual Pinball table. It's a creation for the platform that combines elements of two different Bally tables:
Attack from Mars (1995): This table features a campy theme with aliens invading Earth. Players battle flying saucers, collect Martian toys, and aim for ramps to defeat the alien attackers.
Revenge from Mars (1999): This sequel table features a darker, more intense atmosphere. Players take on the role of Earth's last defense against a renewed Martian assault.
In the world of Visual Pinball, there's a semi-original table called "Attack & Revenge from Mars"  by author JPSalas. This creation uses the playfield layout and graphics from Revenge from Mars, but applies the rule set and sound effects from Attack from Mars. This offers a unique blend of the two themes while keeping the overall gameplay familiar to Attack from Mars players.

id: Attack from Mars (Bally 1995)/Attack from Mars LE (Midway 1995) v600.vpx
name: Attack From Mars
desc: It's easy to see why Attack from Mars is one of the highest-rated pinball machines of all time. The game is a great shooter, making excellent use of the popular fan playfield layout with one of the best center playfield bash toys in the flying saucer, iconic callouts, and an approachable, easy-to-understand ruleset. Even today, it's a game that a lot of newer pins struggle to live up to. Blowing up a saucer (especially if you have a shaker motor attached) is always exciting.

name: Austin Powers (Stern 2013) VPW
desc:
Austin Powers is an arcade pinball game designed by Lonnie Ropp and John Borg, and released in 2001 by Stern Pinball. Based on the first two movies in the Austin Powers comedy series, the game has you accompany the British super-spy as he battles Dr. Evil and his forces across time.
Foil Fat Bastard behind the toilet, spin Mini-Me into submission, then use the right loop to defeat the other Henchmen. Bash Dr. Evil to restore Austin's mojo, shoot the center ramp to activate the Time Machine, and fire the Big Frickin' Laser at Washington DC when it swings out from the bottom of the playfield.
If you're groovy enough, you can stop the Subeterranian Drill, take down Virtucon, and destroy Dr. Evil's Moon Base all while Austin dances away.

name: Avatar
desc:
As one would expect, the game follows the highlights of the movie, recreating Jake Sully's encounters with the natives of Pandora and their resistance against the Unobtainium mining plans of Colonel Quaritch and the RDA. As Jake, the player will ride a giant Banshee, befriend the Na'vi, collect the seeds from the Tree of Souls, and play with the helicoradian plants.
Receive gifts from Eywa, battle the Valkyrie bomber, topple Quaritch's AMP suit, then lead the Na'vi in the Final Battle for the fate of the planet.

id: Back To The Future 1990 (Data East)/Back To The Future - The Pinball (Data East 1990) v1.05.vpx
name: Back To The Future
desc:
Back To The Future is an arcade pinball game based on the Back to the Future film trilogy.
The Back To The Future playfield is divided chronologically, with Hill Valley of 1885 on the left and the Hill Valley of 2015 on the right. While the player tries to raise his score by going between the past, the future, Biff's casino, and the clock tower, caught in the middle are the DeLorean, Doc Brown, and Marty (notably not played by Michael J. Fox).

name: Bad Cats
desc:
The game is themed around the life of a cat and the things they tend to do that annoy people. The object of the game is to spell out "BAD CATS" and accumulate the progressive jackpot that begins at 1 million points, among other things.
Unusual for its era, the table Bad Cats doesn't have a multi-ball.

id: Bad Girls (Gottlieb 1988)/Bad Girls (Gottlieb 1988) v1.6.5 ORIGINAL ART Cheese3075.vpx
name: Bad Girls (Gottlieb 1988)
desc:
The theme is a game of Pool Billiards played in the late 80's by a couple of -you guessed it- Bad Girls. The backbox shows one of Gottlieb's infamous photographic translites of the late 80's, making sure there's no mistake about when the machine was produced.

The playfield is almost a mirrored copy of Bally's Eight Ball Deluxe's playfield. With enhancements like two spinners, multiball (2) and a Vari-Target, it does have its own feel and flow to it.

The main object of the game is to sink the pool balls by dropping the drop targets, finishing with the 8-ball. After that, you can earn a big bonus by spelling RERACK by hitting the targets behind the drop targets within a certain amount of time.

The art and sound are partly influenced by Michael Jackson's 1987 album 'Bad'. The font used for both the machine and the album title is exactly the same. And one of the tunes in the machine has the exact same bass line as Jackson's song Another Part of Me.

Bad Girls - Tooned-Up (Gottlieb 1988)

this is way way more my style, these broads are TOONED-UP!!

name: Bally Game Show
desc:
The Bally Game Show pinball machine, released in 1990, isn't available as a physical machine for most people to play these days. However, it is possible to experience a digital recreation of the table through a program called Visual Pinball.
The table is designed around the excitement of a television game show.
The playfield artwork is colorful and depicts a classic game show set. There are lanes, ramps, drop targets, and other pinball elements decorated with game show motifs.

name: Banzai Run
desc:
Banzai Run was released in 1988 by Williams Electronics, and is notable for its continuous playfield, which extends vertically into the backbox. The game itself is centered on the 1988 Banzai Run Supercross race on the notorious Banzai Hill track.
As an up-and-coming racer, you are up against four rivals: Green Machine, Yellow Belly, Blue Beard, and Red Hot. Build up laps on the lower playfield, then hit the twelve color-coded targets to challenge each racer and access the hill. Once that's done, ride the Ball Lifter to the vertical playfield to defeat the challengers, then take on the King of the Hill in a light-and-sound spectacular.

name: Barb Wire
desc:
“Don't call me Babe!” Crash the tolls, battle the notorious “Big Fatso” and find the elusive contact lenses in this pinball based on the cult Pamela Anderson film Barb Wire.
This is the last pinball made by Gottlieb before they went out of business.

name: BarbWire Tooned-up
desc:
Ladies and Gentlemen I give you my rendition of the BarbWire table, New Tooned-up art, new models, new physics everything! Thanks to Aubrel for allowing me to mod his table.
Make sure to grab the Puppack by Hawkeyez88 that goes with i.
“Don't call me Babe!” Crash the tolls, battle the notorious “Big Fatso” and find the elusive contact lenses in this pinball based on the cult Pamela Anderson film Barb Wire.
This is the last pinball made by Gottlieb before they went out of business.
Thank you to Astronasty for taunting me and pushing me to finish this project. And Thanks to everyone who jumped on board to help me where my skills were lacking.

Table is 10.7

name: Barracora
desc: Barracora is a Physical Pinball Table released in 1981 by Williams Electronics. When pinball enthusiasts talk about "pinball art", Barracora is a name that frequently surfaces, as the eye-catching merwoman is the first and most memorable aspect of the game. Drawing inspiration from H. R. Giger's works (most notably the painting "Li I"), Doug Watson drew a model's facenote morphing into a predatory fish against a landscape of teeth, then dubbed her "Barracuda". Williams' President Mike Stroll loved the artwork but thought the name was too harsh, so the woman (and the game) was quickly rechristened "Barracora".

name: Baseball (Gottlieb 1970)
desc:
"Just like the Real Thing!", the flyer says. This Baseball themed pinball by Gottlieb features Vari-Targets which scores singles, doubles, triples or Home Runs depending on how hard you hit it. The six Rollovers score singles, doubles, triples and Home Runs as well. Three rollovers and six BALL targets put "Men on Base".
The Pitch rollover lanes guide the ball directly to the flippers for shots at the Vari-Targets.
The new STAR type rollover lights indicate Men on Base and score 10 points. High point scoring and total Runs-Batted-In scoring for the dual scoring, with the maximum score displayed being 9,999 points. All the action, appeal and interest a player could ask for...
According to Pinball Snapshots, this is the first American game to have the "star" rollover button.
The add-a-ball version of this game is Gottlieb's 1970 'Batter Up'.

name: Batman '66 (Original 2018)
desc:
Original table, designed by luvthecubs in 2018
This is a re-themed version of JP Salas' and Onevox's Williams The Flash (1979). This is definitely not to be confused with the Stern version. Thanks to JP and Onevox for giving me a great machine to mod and learn from.

id: Batman 1991 (Data East) VPW/Batman (Data East 1991) VPW v1.1.vpx
name: Batman (Data East 1991)
desc: As the game cabinet and backglass indicate, this is a licensed game based on the first Tim Burton movie with Michael Keaton and Jack Nicholson. The game makes no attempt to recreate the movie's plot or events, but simply takes the player on a tour of various locales from the film. Escape to the Batcave with Vicky Vale, climb the scaffolding of the Axis Chemical Factory, and hit both young Jack and old Jack for two million points. Knock down the entrance to the Flugelheim Museum to start multiball, then finish off the Joker with a one-two punch to the eyes and mouth.

id: Batman 1991 (Data East) Black & White Mod/Batman (Data East 1991)_SG1bsoN BW Mod.vpx
name: Batman (Data East 1991) B&W
desc: As the game cabinet and backglass indicate, this is a licensed game based on the first Tim Burton movie with Michael Keaton and Jack Nicholson. The game makes no attempt to recreate the movie's plot or events, but simply takes the player on a tour of various locales from the film. Escape to the Batcave with Vicky Vale, climb the scaffolding of the Axis Chemical Factory, and hit both young Jack and old Jack for two million points. Knock down the entrance to the Flugelheim Museum to start multiball, then finish off the Joker with a one-two punch to the eyes and mouth..

name: Batman 66 LE Stern Tribute
desc: Batman 66 is a crime fighting pinball adventure like no other! Based on the cheesy, yet iconic 60s TV series starring Adam West as Batman and Burt Ward as his trusty sidekick Robin, Batman 66 has been created to celebrate both the series' 50th anniversary as well as STERN Pinball's 30th anniversary.

name: Batman Dark Knight (Stern 2008)
desc:
Visual Pinball Batman Dark Knight 2008 is a virtual recreation of the physical pinball machine of the same name released by Stern in 2008. It's based on the popular movie "The Dark Knight" and features gameplay and themes inspired by the film.
Players take on the role of Batman, battling villains like the Joker and Two-Face.
Completing objectives and hitting targets awards points and activates special features.
There are multiple ramps, spinners, and drops to maneuver the ball around.
The game includes a Joker multiplier that increases your score.
Earning enough points allows you to go for the Jackpot.

name: Batman Forever
desc:
Batman Forever is a licensed arcade pinball game designed by Paul Leslie and Joe Kaminkow. It was released by Sega Pinball in 1995, shortly after the movie was released into theaters.
Like its source, this is a very brash and flamboyant game, where the goal is to take down Two-Face and The Riddler by completing various scenes from the film. Go on a Gotham City crime spree, race the Batmobile across rooftops, survive the Brain Drain, and collect the Riddler's Mystery Boxes. You'll also get to defuse the bomb at the circus, lock pinballs in the Batcave, and launch pinballs from the Batwing at playfield targets. Complete all six Gotham Events, then light up the Bat Signals and match Two-Face's two heads for a chance at FOREVER, a multiball frenzy that lasts... as long as you can manage.
The game features sound clips from the movie, as well as new custom speech recorded specifically for the machine by Tommy Lee Jones (Two-Face) and Chris O'Donnell (Robin), and supports up to six players. It even includes a "doubles mode" where two-player teams compete against each other, and a "guaranteed minimum time" mode for beginners.

name: Baywatch
desc:
Baywatch is a 1995 arcade pinball game based on the world-famous television series from The '90s. Designed by Joe Balcer and Joe Kaminkow, with artwork by Markus Rothkranz and Jeff Busch, it was the second game from the newly-formed Sega Pinball.
Set in the sun and surf of Southern California, the game casts the player as one of the Baywatch lifeguards, working with Mitch, C.J., Stephanie, Matt, and Caroline on various beachside adventures. Perform CPR on drowning victims, rescue trapped Divers, and watch out for the Tidal Wave. Visit Venice Beach and Shark Cove, go jet skiing, then activate the automatic Shark Fin Flipper to help out during Tourist Season. Lock pinballs in the Guard Tower for multiball, prove yourself in the Ironman Competition, collect all the vehicles for the Search and Rescue, then ride out the Earthquake and look great while doing so. The large DMD features near-photorealistic animated clips, while David Hasselhoff provides custom voice work. Up to six players can compete, including an option for two-on-two "doubles mode".

name: Beach Bums (Original 2018)
desc: This is a re-themed version of Hollywood Heat (Gottlieb 1986)

name: Beachboys
desc:
Hello everyone, here's another musical pinball table featuring a 1960s band, one of the best pop groups for many years. So pay tribute to them by reforming the band and completing their songs. Have fun everyone, and stay cool and surf this summer!

Pinball tables coming soon ?


Have a great holiday! Marty

id: Beat The Clock (Bally 1985)/Beat The Clock (Bally 1985) VPW v1.0.vpx
name: Beat the Clock (Bally 1985)
desc:
It's about time!

The clock pounds...the lights scramble...the sound accelerates with every tick of the timer. A stopwatch sets the pace for each player in a breathless race against time. Bally Midway introduces its most colorful new pinball challenge-a hi-gear game where the only way to win is to beat the clock!

id: Beavis and Butt-head Pinballed (Original 2024)/Beavis and Butt-head_Pinballed_1.1.4.vpx
name: Beavis and Butt-head Pinballed (Original 2024)
desc:
Thirty years ago, a cartoon show with this crazy duo aired on MTV that was so divisive that politicians were calling for it to be removed from the air. It was crass, it was filthy, but most of all, it was downright hilarious. Beavis and Butt-Head hocked a loogie into the pool of early 1990s pop culture and they've been doing it ever since with episode after episode and a few movies thrown in.

As an homage to Mike Judge, Beavis and Butt-head, and to all of the older school pinball diehards out there, watacaractr created this original table for Visual Pinball X as it might have looked, and should have been released, back in 1993. Nothing fancy, no videos, etc. Just good ol' fun retro pinball!

name: Beetlejuice (Original 2023)
desc:
Original table, designed in 2023.
This is a Reskin of JPSalas's table Iron Maiden.

Thanks to  doivelspack for his excellent table & permission to upload this & to JP Salas for his Stern Iron Maiden 1982 table which it was a Reskin from.
Added 150 Ball Drain Quotes
Added 4 Songs from the Movie & kept the epic theme as first track.
Harry Belafonte - Jump in the Line
The dinner party (Day-o)
Showtime!
The Incantation
Right Magna Save skips to the next track.
Used the Clearer Instruction Card in the original table download comments at VPU & changed it on the apron.

name: Beetlejuice Beetlejuice 2026 1.0
desc:
It's SHOW TIME!
An obnoxious, devious, and chaotic ghost who works as a freelance "bio-exorcist" in the Netherworld.
Famous for his sleazy salesman persona and striped suit, he can only be summoned from or banished back
to the afterlife by saying his name three times. Desperate to reclaim their house, the Maitlands hire
Beetlejuice, a sleazy, chaotic Netherworld spirit who specializes in scaring off the living. The new
family's goth, death-obsessed teenage daughter, Lydia, is the only one who can see the ghosts summoning
him quickly spirals out of control as he has his own dangerous agenda—which includes escaping the
Afterlife by trying to force Lydia to marry him. Years later the Deetz family returns to Winter River
following a sudden tragedy. Teenage Astrid is tricked by a local ghost and gets dragged into the Afterlife.
Desperate, Lydia summons Betelgeuse, who agrees to help in exchange for her hand in marriage.

Summon The Ghost with the most in this pinball adventure and have Beetlejuice help you spook everyone
invading this pinball game as long as you make sure you put him back in the model before you're done.

id: Big Bang Bar 1996 (Capcom)/Big Bang Bar (Capcom 1996) VPW 2.1.vpx
name: Big Bang Bar
desc: Welcome to the Big Bang Bar, the rowdiest late-night alien dive in the cosmos! Check your carapice at the door, slither up to a table, and the waitress will be with you shortly. Get your groove on with the techno-thumpin' tunes and strobing neon lights, and feast your eyes on the gorgeous gyrations of the Tube Dancer at center stage. Or you can Tour the Bar, play some Cosmic Dartz, then try to score a drink award with Ray's Ball Busters. For more excitement, stuff the Loopy Martians until they get Looped In Space, fire up the Babescanner and the Lunapalooza, or just wait for a Multibrawl Multiball to break out. Complete all fourteen tasks for a shot at the Big Bang, and see how much you can really score.

name: Big Brave (Gottlieb 1974)
desc: Big Brave is western themed the 2 player version of Gottlieb's "Big Indian"

id: Big Buck Hunter Pro (Stern 2010)/Big Buck Hunter Pro (Stern 2010)_Bigus(MOD)4.0.vpx
name: Big Buck Hunter Pro
desc: Big Buck Hunter® PRO Pinball by Stern Pinball, Inc. is a hunting game that delivers a hot new quarry of no-limit fun to players everywhere. Big Buck Hunter® PRO Pinball is based on the hugely successful Big Buck Hunter® arcade video game series by Raw Thrills and Play Mechanix. And like the video games, Big Buck Hunter® PRO Pinball is sure to challenge new hunters, as well as seasoned marksmen.nnnnBig Buck Hunter® PRO Pinball takes you on a hunting adventure. Players are in pursuit of wild game, such as elk, moose and rams, while a motorized big buck moves swiftly across the forest-like playing field. Strike the buck with the pinball and start multiple ball action.

name: Big Game (Stern 1980) v600
desc:
Big Game, released by Stern Electronics in March 1980, is a widebody pinball machine designed by Harry Williams. Known for its safari theme, and for being the first electronic pinball machine to use 7-digit score displays.
The game features four flippers, three pop bumpers, two slingshots, five star rollovers, three banks of drop targets, two spinning targets, two stand-up targets, and one kick-out hole. This was Stern's first widebody game, although its playfield was narrower than typical widebody machines of the period.
The machine features a "thumping drum beat" that increases in speed as the ball stays in play, enhancing the "hunter vs. hunted" safari atmosphere.
Stern produced approximately 2,713 units of Big Game.

name: Big Guns
desc: Big Guns is a 1987 pinball game designed by Mark Ritchie and Python Anghelo and released by Williams Electronics. Taking place in a medieval future, the King Tyrant is holding the Queen hostage. It's up to the Queen's military forces to storm the King Tyrant's castle and rescue the Queen. But to successfully storm the castle, they would have to be granted invincibility powers. Big Guns's notable features include two catapults (the cannons) that shoot the ball into the air and into the habitrail, and a taller-than-normal backbox, which houses a bagatelle mini-game (the King's Chamber).

name: Big House
desc:
Big House is a pinball machine released by Gottlieb in 1989. It isn't as well-known as some other Gottlieb games, but fans consider it underrated and enjoyable.
This recreation is highly rated and tries to capture the feel of the original machine as closely as possible, including:
Artwork replicating the original pinball machine's design
Sounds from the original machine
Lighting effects that mimic the real pinball machine, including adjustments based on the game state
Overall, if you're a fan of pinball or Gottlieb games in particular, Big House on Visual Pinball is considered a faithful and enjoyable virtual recreation.

name: Big Hurt (Gottlieb 1995)
desc:
Frank Thomas' Big Hurt is a pinball machine designed by Bill Parker and released by Gottlieb in 1995. The game features a baseball theme and is named after Frank Thomas.

The playfield of the game is laid out like a stadium with roaring crowds, a play-by-play announcer and features a moving baseball glove. The game has three flippers, two pop bumpers, two slingshots, drop targets, a captive ball, and a four-ball multi-ball.

id: Big Trouble in Little China Original 2022/Big Trouble 1.8 DOF for puppack.vpx
name: Big Trouble 1.8 DOF for puppack
desc:
This time it will be a question of reflex to play at this table...
Big Trouble in Little China. Based on the Wrath of Olympus by JP Salas. Created in collaboration with TeamTuga. Download their incredible Puppack companion.
Goal of the game is to defeat Lo Pan's World. Main features:
3 holes, 1 vuk, 2 bumpers, 6 flippers, 4 ramps, 2 spinners, 13 targets, 1 kickback, 1 captive ball and 1 elevated playfield. 3 balls per play, 20 second ball save timer on each ball, excluding any earned extra balls.
Three Skill Shots: Standard skill shot, Super skill shot, and Freaky skill shot. There are several multiballs and 1 final wizard mode. You may earn add-a-balls to your multiballs or during a single ball game, up to 6 balls at the same time.
Henchmen/Villains Battle Modes: lights are off until mode is activated, when mode is activated, it blinks intensely and if mode is completed the light will stay on for duration of game.

name: Black Belt
desc: Game play consists of collecting belts (yellow, green, blue and black) in order to achieve higher playfield bonus from 2x up to 5x. This multiplier carries over from ball to ball and the game's infectious music gets faster and faster as you progress to higher belt levels.

name: Black Hole
desc:
Black Hole is a widebody pinball machine by Gottlieb released in October 1981. It had a number of features going for it, the most striking of which were the dual playfields: a normal playfield, and the "Black Hole", a reversed playfield embedded underneath, visible through a transparent hole in the table.
It also featured speech, something of a novelty at the time, with the game memorably taunting prospective players by saying "Do you dare to enter the Black Hole?" during Attract Mode. Finally, it featured an eye-catching mirrored backglass with a rotating black hole. Both features were taken out of the export version. The game cost 50 cents to play, which was fairly extravagant at the time, but played up in marketing to promote the game's earning potential.

name: Black Jack
desc:
Black Jack is a Solid State Electronic (SS) pinball machine manufactured by Bally, whose original project date began May 6th, 1976.
It was also produced as an EM 2-Player the year before.

name: Black Knight
desc: The Black Knight is a milestone in the evolution of pinball. It introduced many of new designs to pinball. It was the first game with the patented "Magna-Save" feature. It was the first with a two-level playing field, and faceted inserts in the playfield.

id: Black Knight - Sword Of Rage (Stern 2019)/Black Knight - Sword Of Rage.vpx
name: Black Knight - Sword Of Rage
desc:
Released by Stern Pinball in 2019, Black Knight: Sword of Rage is a fast, aggressive, and challenging pinball machine designed by pinball legend Steve Ritchie. It serves as the climactic third installment in the iconic Black Knight pinball series, boasting a heavy metal aesthetic, an interactive Black Knight toy, and deep, mission-based gameplay
For the first time ever, players will explore, discover, and unlock the secrets of the Black Knight universe. Navigating through these dark, mysterious, and twisted realms, players will uncover foes, demons, riches, and secrets in their quest against the Black Knight.
Black Knight: Sword of Rage features stunning and distinctive hand-drawn art by Kevin O'Connor in homage to this pinball icon, and a custom sculpted, multi-functional Black Knight bash toy. This interactive Black Knight toy features a bi-directional motorized flail, a glowing RGB helmet with individually controllable expressive lighting to interact and taunt players with custom speech, and a sliding coil-driven shield that will bash and block your shots.
The machine was released in three tiers: Pro, Premium, and a Limited Edition of 600 units. While the Pro features the standard layout, the Premium and Limited Edition versions add a transparent upper playfield with an extra flipper and a 3-ball lock catapult mechanism, giving players the ability to achieve a chaotic 6-ball multiball.
All models include the distinctive Magna-Save, a player-controlled magnet used to prevent a ball from draining, and timed resetting drop targets. In addition, Black Knight: Sword of Rage features a legacy sound package composed and performed by Scott Ian of Anthrax with Brendon Small, adrenalizing the audio experience for players on their journey, and custom speech by Ed Robertson of Barenaked Ladies.

id: Black Knight 2000 1989 (Williams)/Black Knight 2000 (Williams 1989) w VR Room v2.0.2.vpx
name: Black Knight 2000
desc: The first sequel to 1980's original table, with software by Ed Boon and artwork by Doug Watson. The Black Knight returns, this time in a techno-feudal landscape (eschewing the more traditional, ornate look of the original game). The player must storm the Knight's castle and battle him, while a Choir of Angels provide moral support for the player. It was the first pinball game to offer a Wizard Mode, and featured a truly memorable soundtrack with Chicago singers Stephanie Rogers and Glo Van Vlack.

name: Black Pyramid
desc: Legend of Black Pyramid It all began thousands of miles beyond the mouth of the Nile River in a fertile region known today as Bally Midway. It was here that an expedition of the world's most prominent pinballologists wandered west and made a startling discovery while excavating for new plateaus in arcade adventures. Through remarkable feats of engineering, they soon uncovered a mysterious artifact said to have once amused Pharaohs, priestesses, and mummies in their final resting place. Preserved in all its monolithic glory lied the treasures of Black Pyramid. Never before had modern civilization had the chance to marvel at the rich ornamental sculpting of its cabinetry ...the majesty of its flashing lights...the gleaming opulence of its regal flippers. Now from the far corners of Bally Midway, the legend known as BLACK PYRAMID lives again.

name: Black Rose
desc:
The game focuses on the title character, a female pirate captain who commands her crew of grizzled sea dogs. Your goal is to sink as many ships as you can by lighting S-I-N-K-S-H-I-P through various means, then fire a cannonball through the broadside at the far end of the table. Along the way, you'll find the Pirate's Cove, get a random award from Polly, and play no less than three Video Modes.
Possibly the most interesting feature of the game is its cannon, which sits below the playfield just above the flippers. At certain points, the cannon will become loaded and start pivoting back and forth. The player must then press the "Fire" button on the lockbar, causing the cannon to pop up and launch the pinball at various playfield targets for different bonuses. Accurate cannon-firing is needed to hit the broadside of opposing ships and establish your reign as Queen of the seas.

name: Blackout
desc: Blackout was the first Williams machine to have a computer controlled general illumination effect. This is seen during the "Blackout" sequence. The backbox mounted GI relay would interrupt power to the playfield GI lamps. Stern's Galaxy was the first pinball title to introduce a computer controlled GI relay. It also uses the same lane change concept first introduced by Williams "Firepower." The sounds are pure 80s and the voice sounds like a computer. All in all, this is a solid state classic that will keep you coming back for more! Orbit Completed!

Bobby Orr Power Play is a digital recreation of a 1978 Bally pinball machine.

While it's a digital recreation, some versions offer options to switch between a classic and a more polished playfield look.
Bobby Orr Power Play offers a nostalgic experience for fans of classic pinball machines and hockey.  The addition of the center post and mini-flippers makes it a unique table within VPX.

name: Bon Jovi pup (Original 2024)
desc:
Bon Jovi version PUP-PACK By Laouillas

Bon Jovi is an American rock band formed in Sayreville, New Jersey in 1983.
The band consists of singer Jon Bon Jovi, keyboardist David Bryan, drummer Tico Torres, guitarists John Shanks and Phil X, percussionist Everett Bradley, and bassist Hugh McDonald. Original bassist Alec John Such left the band in 1994, and longtime guitarist and co-songwriter Richie Sambora left in 2013.
In 1984, Bon Jovi released their self-titled debut album, and its single "Runaway" managed to reach the Top 40 of the Billboard Hot 100. In 1986, the band achieved widespread success and global recognition with their third album, Slippery When Wet, which included three Top 10 singles on the Billboard Hot 100, two of which reached No. 1: "You Give Love a Bad Name" and "Livin' on a Prayer".
Their fourth album, New Jersey (1988), was also commercially successful, featuring five Top 10 singles, including the number ones "Bad Medicine" and "I'll Be There for You".
The band toured and recorded during the late 1980s, culminating in the 1988–90 New Jersey Syndicate Tour.
In 1992, the band returned with the double-platinum Keep the Faith, which included the hit “Bed of Roses”.
This was followed by their biggest-selling and longest-charting single "Always” in 1994.
The album These Days (1995), proved a bigger success in Europe than in the US, producing four Top Ten singles in the UK.
Following a second hiatus, their 2000 album Crush, particularly the lead single, "It's My Life", successfully introduced the band to a younger audience.
The platinum albums Have a Nice Day (2005) and Lost Highway (2007) saw the band incorporate elements of country music into some songs, including the 2006 single "Who Says You Can't Go Home", which won the band a Grammy Award and became the first single by a rock band to reach No. 1 on the country charts.
The Circle (2009) marked a return to the band's rock sound.
The band further success touring, with the 2005–06 Have a Nice Day Tour and 2007–08 Lost Highway Tour ranking among the Top 20 highest-grossing concert tours of the 2000s.
After releasing Because We Can in 2013, lead guitarist Richie Sambora left the band, just before a concert during the supporting tour to spend more time with family.
The band released their first studio album without Sambora, Burning Bridges, in 2015 and the follow-up album This House Is Not for Sale in 2016, touring it in 2017–19.
Their album 2020 was reworked to include songs inspired by the COVID-19 pandemic and George Floyd protests.
Bon Jov has been credited with "bridging the gap between heavy metal music, rock and pop with style and ease".
The band has released 16 studio albums, five compilations and three live albums.
They have sold more than 130 million records worldwide, making them one of the best-selling American rock bands, and performed 2,700 concerts in 50 countries for 34 million fans.
Bon Jovi was inducted into the UK Music Hall of Fame in 2006, and the US Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2018.
The band received the Award of Merit at the American Music Awards in 2004.

name: Bone Busters
desc:
Bone Busters is regarded for being a rather innovative table with an unorthodox layout and challenging gameplay. Chicago is under siege by an army of undead skeletons, and the only ones who can stop them are the brave men and women of Bone Busters, Inc.
While the disembodied head of Ol' One-Eye turns and taunts you from above the backbox, you can purge skeletons from the Jogging Path, the Fast-Food Restaurant, and the Elevated Subway and then head for Lower Wacker Drive and advance the awards. Shoot the centre fountain to collect the Water Tower Bonus, discover the secret of the Opera Bonus, and find Liz's Surprise for more points. Energize the playfield zap rods, lock three balls around town, then make the Long Jump to start multi-ball and clean up the burg.

This simple game is classic pinball at it's best.

name: Breakshot
desc:
Breakshot is a physical pinball table released by Capcom Coin-Op in 1996, designed by Greg Kmiec with artwork by Stan Fukuoka. The playfield deliberately hearkens back to the design philosophies of the electro-mechanical pinball machines of the '70s, with a single-level playfield and total ball visibility at all times. The object of the game is to complete 3 games of pool - Eight Ball, Nine Ball and Rotation - in order to start Cutthroat Countdown, a high-stakes pool game where each ball is called out in order; each ball you sink is worth 1M points times one plus the number of times Cutthroat Countdown has been successfully completed (maximum 3M) and the mode ends with a shot at a Super Jackpot worth twice the value of the balls you sank before either running out of time or sinking all the balls. Balls can be sunk in several ways; you can hit their affiliated target on the playfield, shoot an orbit with a lit Super Cue, shoot the center pockets or make the undocumented skill shot (soft plunge the ball to the upper flipper, then shoot the Bank Shot lane to score 100K and sink a ball).
The main gimmick, or "toy", of the game is the center pockets area, a set of three saucers behind a retractable post. When a ball is shot into the center pockets area, the post rises and the ball falls against it, thus making it into a captive ball; if a ball was previously locked, then it will be released from the center pockets and join the second ball on the post. You must then hit the post, which will hopefully transfer enough force to the ball(s) to send them into the center pockets, thus locking one or both of them.

name: Bumper Pool (1969)
desc:
Bumper Pool was a pinball machine manufactured by D. Gottlieb & Co. with a billiards theme in June 1969. It is the Italian "add-a-ball" export version of Gottlieb's Mini Pool, another pool-themed table from the same year. Approximately 2,150 units were made for the Italian market.

Due to strict Italian gambling laws at the time, the machine lacked the word "flipper" on the apron and flippers. It also used a turret shooter for awarding extra balls (WOWs) so that the machine, rather than the player, launched the "free" ball.

name: Bushido (Inder 1993)
desc: The Bushido pinball machine, released in 1993 by Spanish manufacturer Inder, is themed around Japanese samurai culture and the Bushido code. This solid-state machine features two flippers, three ramps, and a three-ball multiball mode, offering players a challenging gameplay experience with a mix of traditional elements and unique ramp-based shots. Bushido was among the last machines produced by Inder before the company ceased operations, making it a rare and sought-after collector's item.

name: Cactus Canyon
desc:
With less than 1,000 machines produced, the original game is notorious for being released with incomplete code. It's sort of the ultimate "rare game with promise". An expensive collector's item and pinball conversation piece until Chicago Gaming Company was able to complete the project and re-release the game in 2022.
Cactus Canyon is meant to be in the same vein as other Bally/Williams games of the era, like Attack from Mars and Medieval Madness. Fan layout, mode-based rules, mostly linear gameplay.

name: Canasta 86
desc:
Canasta 86 is a virtual pinball table based on a 1986 pinball machine by Inder.
Classic pinball mechanics with flippers, bumpers, and slingshots.
Scoring points by hitting targets and completing lanes.
Earning extra balls and special features like free games.
Three flippers (one bottom flipper and two upper flippers)
Seven lanes at the top of the playfield, each with different scoring opportunities.
Three targets on the left bank, three targets on the right bank, and a single center target.
Backglass displays point values, lit lanes, and special features.
Bonus multiplier lanes: Increase your bonus points when lit.
Extra ball lanes: Earn an extra ball for your next turn.
Special lane: Awards a free game when lit.
Three-target combos: Lighting specific combinations of left, right, and center targets activates extra balls or specials.
Bonus points awarded at certain point milestones (1.5 million and 2.5 million points).

name: Capersville
desc:
Capersville features 3-ball multiball play, used earlier on Bally's 1963 'Star-Jet'. A special version was produced for Germany with the same project number and project release date.
Inspired from 'Capersville' that was the 1965 French detective movie 'Alphaville' starring American actor-singer Eddie Constantine.

name: Captain Fantastic (Bally 1975)
desc: Capt. Fantastic was inspired by the movie 'Tommy' and includes a representation of Elton John, as his character from the movie, playing pinball on the backglass. The game name, however, is the title of Elton John's 1975 autobiographical song and album where "Captain Fantastic" was Elton and "The Brown Dirt Cowboy" was his then-lyricist Bernie Taupin. Included in the song lyrics are the words "From the end of the world to your town" which appear at the very top center of the backglass.

It is based on the book "20000 Leagues Under the Sea" by Jules Verne, and follows the adventures of Captain Nemo with his submarine the "Nautilus".

The ramps were designed with stainless steel sheets, and some pinballs were plated with gold or old cooper.

name: CARtoons RC (Nailed 2021)
desc:
This is a modification of CARtoons RC (2017) v2.3, by HauntFreaks, BorgDog, and SliderPoint - with contributions from Dark, Randr, Toxie, and Fuzzel

Major changes in Nailed: RtxBS ON, Physics, Nails, Multiball, Outlane Save Roach, Shadows, Lights, Sounds, Breakable Elements
My goal was to give it a couple more features, while staying true to its 'aged' aesthetic. I'd like to think I pulled it off!

See script for more toggle-able options
**Arachnophobe Warning** turn off spider in script, I don't want to freak anyone out (too much)

Thank you to Toxie and Fuzzel for VPX in general, and for their excellent documentation and posts clarifying all of its features.
Special thanks to JPSalas for the physics, shadows, and sounds in his excellent Arcade Physics v3 2nd edition, and for advising me to lower the max velocity of the ball - which led to fine-tuning the physics of the whole table, then tweaking the flippers to be more worn out like the original.

"My boss found this old pinball machine in his barn and stuck it in our break room, bugs and all!  I thought it was old and unfair, so I hammered some nails in...hopefully I didn't break anything...
…um, if the lights go out…...just give it a slap." – RADDOG.

name: Casino (Williams 1958)
desc: "Casino" is a card-themed electro-mechanical pinball machine released by Williams Manufacturing Company in August 1958. The game features two flippers, four pop bumpers, two kick-out holes, and a gobble hole. Primary manufacturer: Williams Electronic Games Inc.

id: Castlevania Symphony Of The Night (Original 2022)/SOTN (Mephisto Mod).vpx
name: Castlevania Symphony Of The Night (Original 2022)
desc:
This is my first completed table mod. I am just getting started with VPX and virtual pinball.

This is tribute to one of my favorite video games of all time. Castlevania: Symphony of the Night (SOTN). Originally released on Playstation 1. Filled with lots of the original sounds and artwork from SOTN.

I based this on JPSalas's amazing Mephisto table. Thanks JP for permission to mod this super fun table.

I made many little design changes and a complete reskin. Some adjustments to the rules and added features. Be sure to hit the double-jump skillshot in the plunger lane for a little bonus at the start of each ball! The ruleset is pretty easy to understand. Mostly just look for blinking lights to identify your next target!

I worked hard to iron out any bugs but I'm sure there are still some in there. Please let me know if you find anything that doesn't work properly.

Enjoy!

name: Catacomb
desc:
Everyone goes to his final reward eventually. And few ever escape. Either way. their money ALWAYS remains behind in Catacomb, the thrilling new pin game from Stern.
Having a PLAYER CONTROLLED, ACTION PACKED BACKGLASS, combined with a superfast playfield, Catacomb demands the ultimate in refined skills and cunning strategy.
What numbers should be picked ? What colors must be chosen ? Only seconds to decide as a simulated voice alerts the player to his options.

name: Centaur
desc: Centaur is a popular, highly rated pinball machine. It has a striking black and white design, with red, orange, and green accents. This makes it stand out. The playfield is also designed well, and the sounds and music are impressive. Plus, there's an extremely satisfying bonus countdown sound. This machine is fair because it offers a lot of shot variation, which helps keep players interested. Some people love it while others hate it - but that's what makes pinball interesting!

name: Cerberus (Playmatic 1983)
desc: Battle through the mythic underworld in this Spanish pinball from Playmatic. Inspired by Greek legends, Cerberus features bold artwork, multi-flipper action, and classic early-'80s gameplay with a dark fantasy twist.

name: Chance (Playmatic 1978)
desc:
Notable Features :
- High score to date adjustable to 1 or 3 replays.
- Special targets score a replay or shoot again according to adjustment..
- Shoot again, when lit, can be adjusted to collect the score or not when ball leaves playfield.
- Central bumper can be adjusted to score 10.000 or 1.000 points.
- Double Bonus dropping one bank of targets.
- Triple Bonus dropping the two banks of targets.
- Kickout Hole combined with spinning lights can multiply bonus score by 10, lit extra ball, activate up post, etc.
- Dropping targets the score on the cristal ball advances.

there is another pinball table but with the same name but completely different released in 1974 by Playmatic.

name: Charlie's Angels (Gottlieb 1979)
desc:
Charlie’s Angels was the sixth solid state game released by Gottlieb and based upon the television crime drama of the same name, which appeared on the ABC network between 1976 to 1981. The game features the likenesses of Cheryl Ladd, Kate Jackson and Jaclyn Smith, the 1977 cast of the ever-changing Angels team. The iconic Angels “silhouette” is used throughout the backglass, playfield and cabinet art. Two sets of drop targets and a stand up target work to increase bonus and advance the bonus multiplier. There is indication that this Allen Edwall design was originally used to test the limits of Gottlieb’s solid state hardware upon its implementation at Gottlieb, some years before the design was assigned to carry the Charlie’s Angels theme. An electromechanical version of this game was also made by Gottlieb in fewer numbers.

The SS Model was manufactured in late 1978, the EM Model in early 1979.

name: Check Mate (Recel - 1975)
desc:
Check Mate: 4 players, replay and/or extra ball

Options in the script Apron card in English or Spanish, 3 or 5 balls, Special or Extra Ball
As default the tables are configured like this:

Check Mate: 5 balls, English cards, Special

There are some differences in the rules:

Check & Check Mate: bumpers turn on with the central target and the upper lane
Check & Check Mate: drop targets reset after each new ball.
Check & Check Mate: tilt penalise just the ball
Check & Check Mate: the KING is a normal drop target. Special is on the upper lane (and outlines too like in Jake Mate)

This table requires B2S to play in VR.
This table Works in DT/FS/VR and MR, but specially in VR.
To change VR Room (pool/minimal) or Mixed Reality, press F12 and change Room in the menu
Virtual Desktop Settings Chromakey:
Color RGB = 255,255,255
Similarity: 2
Smoothness: 2

You can enable Ambience ROOM at the end of the script. Enable it to True.

name: Checkpoint
desc:
Checkpoint it the first pinball machine to let players choose their own music, Checkpoint is most famous as the first game to feature a Dot Matrix Display (DMD), allowing for attention-grabbing animations, status indicators, and storytelling capabilities.

The goal of the game is to drive your Porsche Carrera to victory in eight rally races around the world. Build up those RPMs for multiball, hit the Spin-N-Win, then start Fast Mode for a ten-second scoring frenzy.

Punch the Hot Nitro to get the Blue Light Special and Redline your way to the Checkered Flag. For extra glory, race through the Lasermatic Speed Gun and set a new speed record, then hit the Checkpoint for Double Bonuses.

id: Cheech & Chong Road-Trip'pin (Bally 2021)/Cheech & Chong - Road-Trip'pin nFozzy Fleep Hybrid V11.vpx
name: Cheech & Chong - Road-Trip'pin (Bally 2021)
desc:
Far out, man! Dave IS here! ...finally!

That's right, Cheech & Chong are here! It's been a long time coming, but this insanely funny duo have now made their nostalgic venture in to VPX! Kick back and enjoy the ride as you take a road-trip with these two famous stoners, doing what they do best, and explore their world from those crazy 70's and 80's. You'll encounter characters, music and sounds based from their iconic comedy albums, as well as their hilarious cult classic movies.

Traveling from "Pedro's House" to the "Battle of the Bands", and back, Cheech & Chong: Road-Trip'pin, will provide you with a "high" amount of fun and laughs that
only these two can deliver.

Dedicated to one of the best, if not, the best, laugh-out-loud comedy teams in history.

desc:
The flyer states that this is "the first pinball game ever to have the innovative "Add-a-Balls" feature giving player up to 5 extra balls on a single play." According to the manual, extra balls will stack like this only if the Special feature and the Score Thresholds are set to award an Extra Ball.
- Theme of the table : Jungle, Fantasy
- Maximum displayed point score is 9,999,990 points per player.

name: Childs Play (Original 2018)
desc:
You know what they say. You just can't keep a good guy down.

I have a lot of people to thank for contributing to this pup and table (hopefully i'm not forgetting anyone).
A big thanks to Hursty for orginally re-skinning this table. Many thanks to Joe Picasso for helping upgrade the artwork and the backglass. Thanks to JP Salas for adding the multiball option (to help spice up the table a bit:)). PinballFan2018 for adding the PuPDMD option. Hawkeyez88 for helping with some of these fun EM table pup triggers. Chucky for backglass coding. Harlan for the default backglass animation. Andrew Walsh for additional animation. Smaug for testing; and Petri Renbro for the attract intro video.

Just place the Fast_Draw_1975 folder inside your PUPVideos folder.

There are four PUP options. DMD & Topper on backglass. DMD (no topper) on backglass. FullDMD regular and FullDMD with toppers. Just run the Bat file you want inside the PupPack folder.

Also included, a sick looking b2s created by Joe Picasso and Chucky.

name: Circus
desc:
Circus 1980, released by Gottlieb.
The table features a circus theme, complete with clowns, elephants, and other classic circus imagery.
It's likely to replicate the gameplay of the original 1980 Gottlieb Circus pinball machine, which would involve using flippers to maneuver a pinball around the playfield, hitting targets, collecting points, and activating various bonuses.
VPX recreates the look and feel of a physical pinball table in a digital format. You can expect detailed graphics of the playfield, backglass, and other table elements.

id: Cirqus Voltaire 1997 (Bally)/Cirqus Voltaire (Bally 1997) VPW Mod v1.1.vpx
name: Cirqus Voltaire
desc:
The menagerie ball, a large plastic ball trapped within a cage above the left slingshot, can be hit by the ball in play and disrupts ball direction.
The Ringmaster is an animated head that elevates from the underside of the playfield and makes wise cracks at the player, who tries to defeat him by hitting him with the pinball in various modes. A stop magnet is on the top of the Ringmaster's head, holding the ball there when the head rises up.
The "Boom Balloon" pop bumper (on the lower right side of the playfield) is a disappearing bumper, dropping down until its flat plastic top is level with the playfield.
The backbox animation simulates a cannonball fired to ring a bell, although the bell is really just a piece of plastic with a bell drawn on it. This animation is mostly activated automatically by the game, but one feature allows the player to continuously fire the cannonball using the flipper buttons in a timed mini-game. Points are given if the ball takes a certain path in the fall (this path having a switch).

name: City Slicker
desc:
It's based on a rare 1987 Bally pinball machine of the same name that never went into full production.
Classic pinball mechanics with flippers, bumpers, slingshots, and targets.
Two captive balls on a raised platform that can be launched towards targets.
A center playfield kick-out hole that automatically flips the ball towards a flipper.
Replicates the design of the original Bally City Slicker pinball machine.
The playfield likely features a city theme with bright colors and detailed artwork.
You can find screenshots and gameplay videos online to get a better idea of the visuals.

name: Class of 1812
desc:
Class of 1812 is a pinball machine designed by Ray Tanzer and Joe Kaminkow and released in 1991 by Gottlieb. It features a supernatural monster theme and was advertised with the slogan "Frightful fun for all ages!"
Class of 1812 has a dark theme featuring the reunion of a long dead class. The back glass is a vacuum formed 3D image. During Multiball Madness, a large mechanical beating heart and chattering teeth are synchronized along to chickens clucking the Tchaikovsky's 1812 Overture.
The top of the playfield contains upper rollovers that advance bonus multiplier. The white target sequence advances the BAT-O-METER. Completing the left drop-targets lights the ball lock, then it is possible to lock the ball with the right ramp. Completing the C-O-F-F-I-N letters collects a 2 MILLION point jackpot. The playfield contains elements such as for example pop-bumpers, stationary targets, drop-targets, rollovers, ramps, saucer holes and spinners.

name: Cleopatra
desc:
First solid state game from Gottlieb.
This game was also produced as a 4-player EM version Gottlieb's 1977 'Cleopatra' and a 2-player EM version Gottlieb's 1978 'Pyramid' but with different backglass art.

id: Close Encounters of the Third Kind (Gottlieb 1978) LW 1.0 DT-FS-VR-MR Ext2k Conversion/Close Encounters of the Third Kind (Gottlieb 1978) LW 1.0 DT-FS-VR-MR Ext2k Conversion.vpx
name: Close Encounters of the Third Kind (Gottlieb 1978)
desc: Gottlieb’s Close Encounters of the Third Kind was based on the 1977 science-fiction film of the same name. Gottlieb had recently been purchased by Columbia Pictures, and Close Encounters represents one of the first attempts at synergy between a Columbia property and their newly acquired pinball division. An electromechanical version of this game was also made by Gottlieb in fewer numbers. The game features a spinner, a set of drop targets and Gottlieb’s trademark roto-target in the top right corner of the playfield.

name: Comet (Williams 1985)
desc:
Comet is a Physical Pinball Table produced by Williams Electronics in 1986. It was designed by Barry Oursler and illustrated by Python Anghelo, and is the first title in Williams' "rollercoaster" series of pinball games.

Named for a popular coaster at Chicago's (now closed) Riverview Amusement Park, Comet takes players for a fun time at the carnival. Visit the Shooting Galleries and knock down the ducks and rabbits, drop the Dunk Tank Dummy, and visit the Funhouse. For more thrills, shoot through the Corkscrew, race up the Cycle Jump Ramp, then light up 1-9-8-6 and Ride the Comet for a screamin' good time. End the day with a fireworks show, then try to score the One Million shot before you leave.

name: Conan
desc: This table is inspired by Conan the Barbarian, a 1982 American epic sword and sorcery film directed by John Milius and written by Milius and Oliver Stone. Based on Robert E. Howard's Conan, the film stars Arnold Schwarzenegger and James Earl Jones

name: Congo
desc:
Congo is a 1995 arcade pinball game from Williams Electronics. Based on the Michael Crichton film adaptation, it was designed by John Trudeau and illustrated by Kevin O'Connor.
As with the movie, the player is leading an expedition to Africa, and quickly runs across a lost city, a diamond mine, and lots of Killer Gorillas. Elude poisonous snakes, avoid the rabid bears, and dodge the hippo attacks on the way to Zenj. Consult the Map and decipher the hieroglyphs, then follow the lava flow around the volcano and be prepared when it erupts for multiball. For more riches, wait for the Grays to attack, then confront the giant gorilla in the lower playfield and try to collect the diamonds he guards.
