id: Guns N Roses (Data East 1994)/Guns N Roses (Data East 1994) VPW 1.2.vpx
name: Guns N' Roses (Data East 1994)
desc:
Guns N' Roses is a pinball machine based on the rock group Guns N' Roses.

The artwork features photos by Robert John from his book Guns N' Roses: The Photographic History. This game is a widebody pinball game with several unique twists. Among them, is an old fashioned revolver, which players use to start the game as opposed to the typical plunger. When a quarter is inserted, the band's famous "Welcome to the Jungle" song (recorded from a concert) plays. Also included on the soundtrack is the Use Your Illusion outtake "Ain't Going Down," which is the only official release of the song. The backdrop is illuminated with lights in the shape of the famous Guns N' Roses seal, and Axl Rose's tattoos, featured in the Appetite for Destruction album artwork.

The multi-ball can be activated when the yellow light is lit on the G ramp, this will open a trap door and send the ball into the snake pit (if the ball is shot up the ramp which is a hard shot), pulling the rose plunger will then activate the multi-ball. An "R" ramp is also featured completing the "GN'R" logo.

id: Guns N' Roses 1994 (Data East)/Guns N' Roses limited edition.vpx
name: Guns N' Roses - Limited Edition
desc:
Guns N' Roses tabletop mod from Data East remix with the JERSEY JACK PINBALL version have fun.
The Guns N' Roses Pinball Limited Edition is a visually stunning and feature-rich pinball machine designed by Jersey Jack Pinball, in collaboration with the legendary rock band Guns N' Roses, and partly designed by band member Slash. This machine offers an immersive concert experience with 22 full-length songs and extensive concert footage showcased during gameplay.
It features GNR Tour Poster Cabinet Art Packages, a Red Brick Powder Coat, and Blood Red Plastic Set. The backglass is hand-drawn, showcasing a skeletal band design.
The machine includes over 350 individually controlled RGB LEDs, two full-motion articulating RGB LED stage spotlights, and individually controllable RGB LED Hotrail Lighting, creating a vivid, concert-like atmosphere.
The playfield boasts a Gibson Headstock Upper Playfield with 6 Ball Lock, four flippers, a triple-kinetic diverter Fender Bass Head Mini Playfield, and a Triple Path 4-String Bass Ramp Wireform. Additionally, there are high hat and cymbal interactive drum kit pop bumper toys.
Other features include analog and Bluetooth headphone connectivity, a shaker motor, and Invisiglass to ensure optimal visibility and durability.
This limited edition pinball machine is individually numbered and limited to 5000 units, making it a rare and collectible item. The machine plays a significant amount of licensed video, audio, and graphical art from Guns N' Roses, thanks to Slash's involvement in the design process. It's designed for both commercial and home use, offering a high-end experience that would stand out in any collection.

name: Halloween 1978-1981
desc:
The "Halloween 1978-1981 (Original 2022) VPX" is a virtual pinball table that draws inspiration from the Halloween movies released between 1978 and 1981. This table was meticulously crafted to evoke the suspense and horror of the original films. The creators, Apophis and HiRez00, integrated a host of features to ensure a thrilling pinball experience.
Key aspects of the table include customizable sound settings like mechanical volume, ball-rolling volume, ramp-rolling, callout volumes, effects sounds, simulated ROM sounds, and music volume. Players can adjust these to their liking for a personalized gaming experience. The table also offers nine levels of LUT adjustments for visual tuning, enhancing the immersive experience of the gameplay.

name: HALO (Original 2021)
desc:
Stick with the master chief He'll know what to do!

14 march 2002 Halo came out for the xbox in europe. For our generation was this one of the best games ever made. I played this a lot with friends on a old crt televions with split screen lol! Even Halo 2 we finished in one night playing(on easy of cource). snipering with the blood gulch level, what brings this back a lot of memories for sure! I didn't saw a Halo table out there and i felt the urge to make one.

First of all the round of thanks:
Thanks to jpsals for helping me with helping troubleshoot the code and explaining how the big ufo works in attack from mars. Also his patient because of all my messages. i was in panic mode because i almost had to redo 100+ 3d objects and 3d animations, it costed me 4 hours to find my own fault and its is fixed!
Thanks to flupper for helping me out with his light code.
Thanks to terry red to inspire me because his retro flair table.

This is an original table, with everything included in the vpx file, and it doesn't need any external program to run. It can be run in desktop mode and in FS mode with flexdmd automatically(with JP code fixes). This is a 5 ball game with on 3,6 and 9 million an extra ball. This table has no ball savers, only when the ball goes in to the left outer lane it will go in cortana's station and will be shoot back to the warzone!

This table is based on attack from mars. It hasn't the jumping aliens on it but so much more. It has needler bumpers, plasma rifle slingshots, changing flashers, changing colors, explosions and 3d animations.

Play the bank away by hitting the three bank targets. Then hit the door of the blood gulch bunker to enter the bunker. When you shoot into the bunker the covenantship will fly to you and stays above the bunker(instead of the big UFO), shoot the bunker again to destroy the covenantship every wave you have to shoot the bunker one more time extra to destroy the covenant ship, six times total. then it will restart. but the total waves,kills and missions that have been completed will be shown in the gameover screen.
At the end of the wave the bonus is 100K more then the last time. the small ufo's are replaced by banshees, who doesn't love banshees(hours we flew in them!)!
collect all six jackpots for the super jackpot(50K for each jackpot and 500k for the super jackpot). Every time your assistant Cortana will help you remind the status on how much % you are for getting a jackpot. (accept for the  teleport lane, there will be only the lights).

If you shoot the ball in the teleport portal above your ball will be teleported to one of the 3 sides for extra randomness(with an extra ball it goes to the portal below).
If you shoot in the portal where Johnsen is sitting on, then 3 things can happen; teleport to three locations or missions/battles will start or the bonus level will start on the playfield below.

So every time you play it's different because you don't know where the ball teleports too!

Missions with timers:
1. collect 5 halo logo's - 60 seconds
2. collect letters C-H-I-E-F - 60 seconds
3. Skillshot low - 60 seconds
4. collect 5 frag grenades - 60 seconds
5. Skillshot high - 60 seconds
6. Collect 5 skulls - 60 seconds
7. Activate Halo Alpha - 90 seconds (bring the reactor on the left side offline)
8. Destroy Halo Alpha  - no timer (destroy the left reactor and the halo ring, Halo Beta will now be available under the missions)
9. Activate Halo Beta  - 90 seconds (bring the reactor on the right side offline)
10. Destroy Halo Beta  - no timer (destroy the right reactor and the halo ring)

The mission lights are for mission 1 till 10 and the custom lights are for the mission animated battles

This missions/ animated battles are added above the main missions and  you have change to get them also from the mission spinner(this are the other lights down the super jackpot):
11. Defeat 5 Flood carriers
12. Defeat 5 flood elites
13. Defeat 5 jackals
14. Defeat 5 grunds
15. Defeat 5 elites

After almost every mission you will get an extra ball and then the grund multiball modus will start. Kill the grunds till one ball remains on the table then the normal gameplay will be resumed.

I wanted to bring this table to the next level so i tried to do that by adding 3d annimation(wrote an tutorial for this see 1.6), so the enemies move and there is interaction with the master chief himself. Also by adding flashers which change from colors. I hope everybody enjoys this and remember we all work hard! So please rank/like the table and leave a message behind, thats the only appriciation we need and ask!

Now get back to the war soldier remdwaas out!

name: Hang Glider (Bally 1976)
desc: This is a near-twin of Hi-Deal with slightly different rules. This is a bonus plus spinner game. Bonus is advanced by the ten white mini-rollover buttons at the top when lit, by the two return lanes, by the five standup targets [three lower left, two upper right] when lit, and from the center saucer, which gives one advance and 1000 points for each drop target that you've hit so far on that ball. Bonus maxes out at 15000. If extra balls are enabled, you score it in the saucer in the center once the five targets on the right are completed.

name: Hardbody (Bally 1987)
desc: "Hardbody," a pinball machine released by Bally in 1987, features a unique fitness-themed design inspired by bodybuilding culture. It includes four flippers, two ramps, and an alphanumeric display, emphasizing precision shots and strategic gameplay. Unlike many pinball machines of its era, "Hardbody" does not have a multiball feature, making it stand out with its challenging single-ball play. The artwork and sound design, which reflect the era’s fitness craze, were crafted by Greg Freres and Bob Libbe, respectively. This machine is popular among collectors for its distinct theme and nostalgic appeal.

name: Harlem Globetrotters on Tour (Bally 1979)
desc:
Originally manufactured in 1979 by Bally, Harlem Globe Trotters on Tour is a classic pinball machine.

A really cool and entertaining pinball, Harlem Globe Trotters shows you some serious challenge. Gameplay is not fast, but still intense and with variety to the playfield. The fact that you can rip three different spinners and shoot at a tempting setup of 4 in-line-drops makes this a winner.

name: Harley Davidson
desc:
The Harley Davidson pinball machine, manufactured by Bally in February 1991, is a celebration of the iconic motorcycle brand. Designed by Barry Oursler and Mark Sprenger, with mechanics by Gerald Hedberg, and sound and music by Dan Forden, it represents a pivotal moment in pinball history. This was the first Bally game to use the Williams Pinball Controller (WPC) system and the last to feature an alphanumeric display. The artwork, also by Mark Sprenger, captures the essence of the Harley Davidson brand.
Gameplay involves various objectives like completing the U-S-A lanes to advance the bonus multiplier, hitting drop targets to light spinners for points, and navigating the "DAVIDSON" stand-ups to trigger bonuses and the potential for an extra ball. The game incorporates a multi-ball feature and rewards players for completing specific tasks with high scores and bonuses, with a "travel across America" theme adding to its allure.
Approximately 2,187 units of this game were produced, making it a rare find for collectors. The machine's estimated value varies but is considered a prized piece in any collection. Its slogan, "Live to Ride...Ride to Live," encapsulates the spirit of Harley Davidson and the adventure of riding​​​​.

name: Harley Davidson (Sega 1999) v1.12
desc: The table went through three different production runs. The first made by Sega and continued by Stern Pinball in 1999 after they bought Sega's pinball division in the same year. The second produced by Stern Pinball in 2002, and the third with an artwork change also by Stern was released in 2004. The machine features a Harley-Davidson motorcycle theme including authentic engine sound. The game enables players to lock the ball in wheelies on the playfield. The game has an up post between the flippers that is controlled by the player by an extra flipper button on the right side of the cabinet.

name: Harley Quinn (HauntFreaks 2017)
desc:
Harley Quinn (HauntFreaks 2017) supercalifragilisticexpialidocious real 4K
originally diamond lady by JPsalas
Graphics and Layout mod by HauntFreaks
RGB LED effects and F6 menu implementation by Ninuzzu
Drop Target lighting by BorgDog

I am NOT a fan at all of pins with photos, especially on the playfield…
BUT the table looked to me to have good bones, and since JP did the original I knew it was done right… also I’m not really a fan of Harley Quinn (suicide squad was terrible) BUT again she is the Queen of Diamonds and has an overabundance of artwork it was a no brainer to put two and two together… so after editing 50-80+ images for the PF, Plastics and BG… and also altering the tables layout my end of the project was good to go….
after that having Ninuzzu implement my vision of RBG LED inserts, he went above and beyond by adding f6 menu function and a bunch of other opinion goodies…
BorgDog as always bailed me out when i cant figure stuff out myself by adding droptarget lighting…

name: Harry Potter (Original 2020)
desc:
Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire (2020) by ScottyWic / OrbitalPin is one of the most ambitious original virtual pinball tables ever created for Visual Pinball X. Inspired by Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire, the table was built completely from scratch rather than based on a real-world machine.

The table features a dark cinematic atmosphere heavily inspired by the film, combining Hogwarts, the Goblet of Fire, Death Eaters, and the Triwizard Tournament into a fast-paced and highly immersive pinball experience. It makes extensive use of PuP-Pack media integration, including movie clips, music, speech, FullDMD animations, and dynamic visual effects.

Gameplay centers around progressing through major events from the movie, including:

* The Quidditch World Cup
* The Goblet of Fire
* Death Eater encounters
* The Triwizard Tournament challenges

Players can unlock several multiballs such as:

* Golden Egg Multiball
* Lake Rescue Multiball
* Maze Escape Multiball
* Wand Multiball

The ultimate goal is to reach the wizard mode, Battle Voldemort, by completing spells, tournament objectives, and story-driven missions throughout the table.

The table is also known for pushing VPX features to the limit with:

* Advanced FullDMD integration
* PuP-Pack support
* DOF and MX lighting effects
* SSF surround sound support
* VR compatibility

Within the virtual pinball community, it is widely considered one of the finest original VPX creations ever released thanks to its deep ruleset, cinematic presentation, and high production quality.

name: Haunted House
desc:
Haunted House is a Physical Pinball Table released by Gottlieb in 1982. Designed by John Osborne and illustrated by Terry Doerzaph, it is considered to be one of Pinball's iconic tables, the first game to take place across three interconnected playfields.
As the title suggests, this game takes place above, below, inside, and around a Haunted House, with the player thoroughly exploring it for points while avoiding the various traps and spirits. While lightning flashes on the backglass, start on the main floor, then take the ramp or the up-kicker into the Attic with its occupied coffin. Alternately, use the Secret Passage or the Trap Door to enter the Cellar, where the reversed playfield is filled with rats, a shackled skeleton, and grabbing ghouls. Return to the main table, knock down the cobwebs for double scoring, then tap the five targets for an Extra Ball or a Special.

id: Hawkman (Taito do Brasil - 1983)/Hawkman (Taito do Brasil - 1983) v600.vpx
name: Hawkman (Taito do Brasil - 1983)
desc: Hawkman, released in 1983 by Taito do Brasil, is a unique piece of pinball history from South America's most prolific manufacturer. It is particularly notable for being a licensed adaptation of Bally’s 1981 hit, Fathom. It shares the same core playfield layout but features a distinct theme and different technical internal components.

name: Hearts And Spades (Gottlieb 1969)
desc: "Spin-A-Card" and "Hearts and Spades" are 1969 pinball machines by D. Gottlieb & Co. with identical playfields but different reward systems. Spin-A-Card focuses on replay-based gameplay, where players aim to complete card sets to earn replays, while Hearts and Spades is an add-a-ball version designed to grant extra balls upon completing similar objectives. Both machines feature two flippers, pop bumpers, kick-out holes, and spinning backglass lights. Designed by Ed Krynski with artwork by Art Stenholm.

name: Hearts Gain (Inder 1971)
desc: Hearts Gain is a riverboat gambling-themed electro-mechanical pinball machine released by the Spanish manufacturer Inder in 1971. The game accommodates a single player and features two flippers, three pop bumpers, two slingshots, four standup targets, and two kick-out holes.

name: Heavy Metal Meltdown (Bally 1987)
desc: Heavy Metal Meltdown, released by Bally in January 1987, is a solid-state pinball machine known for its high-energy theme and music-based design. It features two flippers, one ramp, and a multiball option with a capacity for up to five balls. Designed by Dan Langlois with artwork by Tony Ramunni, the machine has an alphanumeric display and was produced in a limited run of 1,600 units.

name: Hellboy Pinball (Original)
desc: Hellboy is a fully original 2024 pinball table that plunges players into the B.P.R.D. universe. You'll face legendary foes like Baba Yaga, Rasputin, and the Ogdru Jahad across interconnected modes, alongside allies Abe Sapien and Liz Sherman. With hybrid physics, custom DOF effects, animated VR room, adjustable difficulty, and immersive styling—including voice lines, rich artwork, and cinematic audio—every shot and bumper feels as powerful as Hellboy's Right Hand of Doom.

name: Hi-Diver (Gottlieb 1959)
desc: Hi-Diver, released by D. Gottlieb & Co. in April 1959, was designed by Wayne Neyens with artwork by Roy Parker.

name: High Hand (Gottlieb 1973)
desc: Complete suits to advance bonus value; bonus is 100 for one card in a suit, 200 for two cards, 300 for three cards, then leaps to 4000 for a complete suit. Strategy – try to finish suits rather than get some of each: 12 cards total with 3 in each suit is worth 1,200 in bonus; 12 cards total in three [complete] suits is worth 12,000 in bonus. But don't finish all 16 targets if add-a-balls cannot be played! When you get all 16, the saucer changes from scoring 12,300 for 15 targets (3 times 4,000 plus 3 times 100) to adding a ball for having all 16. If add-a-balls are turned off or must be plunged, you just lost your biggest scoring opportunity. If you do happen to finish them just go for the bumper and lanes until the ball drains.

id: High Roller Casino 2001 (Stern Pinball)/High Roller Casino (Stern 2001) 1.1.vpx
name: High Roller Casino
desc:
High Roller Casino is a physical pinball table designed by Jon Norris and illustrated by Kevin O'Connor and John Youssi. Released by Stern Pinball in 2001, it stands as Jon Norris' first commercially released pin designed for a company other than Premier Technology, the last table he designed, and the last non-licensed theme table released by any iteration of Stern before they acquired the rights to mass produce Whoa Nellie! Big Juicy Melons in 2014.
The object of the game is to win six casino games: 21 (Blackjack), Craps, Hi-Lo, Poker, Roulette and Slots. The last of these will be the most frequently played of the six games, as playing the slots lights the lock for Slot Machine Multiball, while the bumpers can be reached by shooting an unlit orbit, catching the ball in a magnet at the top of the orbits, which releases the ball on top of the bumpers. The games also award you chips if you win, which increase your bonus and also factor into one of the game's Wizard Modes. If this all seems a bit overwhelming, bear in mind that repeated ramp shots will grant you a Cheat Game, turning your next loss into a big win.
The other main feature of the table is Roll 'N Win, a simple backbox-mounted circular board game that you play by shooting the ramp when Roll 'N Win is lit. The game rolls two dice and you pick one, moving that many spaces, then taking whatever effect is on the space you landed on, which include instant multiball, spotting a casino game, big points, free chips and a mystery award. Each time you complete one circuit of Roll 'N Win, you activate a Super Award, starting with Super Pops, followed by Super Loops, then Super Spinner and finally Super Surprise. Landing on the starting space increases the Super Mode's duration by 50%, so try to do so whenever possible.

name: High Speed (Williams 1986)
desc: High Speed is a pinball game designed by Steve Ritchie, with software by Larry DeMar and art by Mark Sprenger (playfield) and Python Anghelo (backglass); it was released by Williams Electronics in 1986. The game is based on a high-speed police chase between the player (in his cherry-red Lamborghini) and the long arm of the law. The player must first advance a set of traffic lights from green to yellow to red; after he runs the red light, the police will immediately follow. If the player escapes, he can start three-ball multiball for a chase at breakneck speeds, complete with flashing lights and siren.

id: Hit The Deck (Gottlieb 1978)/Hit The Deck (Gottlieb 1978) (VR Room) 1.0.0.vpx
name: Hit The Deck (Gottlieb 1978)
desc: "Hit the Deck" and "Neptune" are two closely related pinball machines produced by D. Gottlieb & Co. in 1978. "Hit the Deck" is a replay version, while "Neptune" is the Add-A-Ball variant. Both machines were designed by John Osborne with artwork by Gordon Morison. "Hit the Deck" features a low production run of 375 units, making it a rare electro-mechanical (EM) machine, with unique mechanical score reels designed to mimic solid-state displays. "Neptune" was even rarer, with only 270 units produced, and it was notable for using black score reels with red letters to give it a more modern, digital appearance despite being an EM game.

name: Hokus Pokus (Bally 1976)
desc: Mystical "Hokus Pokus" features 3 pull a rabbit out of your hat spinners 2 pop bumpers and loads of action. Our Hokus Pokus has a beautiful mint original art glass, excellent playfield and the cabinet has only a few cosmetic issues and no hero's carvings (initials carved into cabinet by vandals) or high score recorded.

name: Hollywood Heat (Gottlieb 1986)
desc:
Hollywood Heat is a Pinball Table designed by John Trudeau with art by Larry Day. It was released by Premier in 1986.

The game itself is a blatant attempt to invoke Miami Vice; the backbox translite features a white-suited Crockett wannabe posing next to a genuine Ferrari Daytona with two bikini-clad women, underneath the "Hollywood Heat" logo done in the Vice typeface. The table itself is more interesting, with a translucent red spiral and a miniature playfield nestled among neon flamingos, palm trees, and pastel-colored eighties pop art. A set of chutes sends the ball in various unorthodox directions, while the "Hot Shots" jump ramp allows players to quickly return to the upper mini-playfield.

As with other Premier pinballs of the period, the rules are not overly complex, making it suited for intermediate players looking for a fun, straightforward game. It's considered an overlooked jewel by those who managed to get past the silly theme, and is regarded as one of Premier's better games. Steve Ritchie has called it one of his favorite games of all time.

name: Hook
desc: The visual pinball version of Hook from Data East, released in 1992, is celebrated within the pinball community for its engaging gameplay and beautiful visuals. This table has undergone various modifications and improvements over the years, with notable contributions from different members of the visual pinball community to enhance its physics, lighting, and overall playability. The table, based on the popular film Hook, incorporates elements that fans of the movie will recognize and appreciate, adding to its charm and appeal.

name: Hoops
desc: Hoops is a basketball themed solid state pinball machine released by Gottlieb under the Premier label in 1991. This machine was the last of Gottlieb’s series of “Street Level” pinball machines designed to be simpler and more affordable for consumers. The game was designed by Ray Tanzer with artwork by David Moore, Constantino Mitchell, Jeanine Mitchell. Only 879 confirmed units were ever produced.

name: Horrorburg
desc: "Horrorburg" is an original table for Visual Pinball X (VPX) created by jpsalas, released in July 2023. It emerged after several months of development, inspired by a request from MaxCore to match the artwork of his cabinet. The game includes music and gameplay ideas based around horror movie killers, yet it was designed to be enjoyable for kids of all ages, avoiding explicit horror or gore. Instead, the visuals feature cartoon versions of well-known horror movie characters, aiming for a more accessible and less frightening experience.

name: Hot Hand
desc:
"Hot Hand" is a pinball machine produced by Stern Electronics in May 1979. It features a solid-state design, leveraging the Stern M-100 MPU for its electronic operations. This game was designed by Harry Williams, a notable figure in the pinball industry, emphasizing its unique place in pinball history. With a production run of 4,117 units, "Hot Hand" became a celebrated addition to the pinball world of its time.
The machine is designed for up to 4 players and includes a digital display type. Its cabinet is of the standard form, incorporating a manual plunger for ball launch. The playfield does not feature a multi-leveled layout, custom speech, a buy-in button, machine shakes, or magnets. However, it stands out with its 3 flippers, 3 bumpers, and 5 drop targets. Additionally, it includes spinners, adding a dynamic element to the gameplay, but it lacks ramps, captive balls, magnets, cannons, kickback, spinning discs, and a multiball feature.
One of the most noteworthy trivia about "Hot Hand" is its spinning flipper, a unique feature that adds an interesting twist to the gameplay. Despite its classic status, "Hot Hand" doesn't include backbox ornaments or a video mode, given its era and the technology available at the time. The latest software version for the machine remains unknown, indicating its status as a product of its time without the continuous updates seen in modern pinball machines​​​​.

name: Hot Shots (Gottlieb 1989)
desc:
Release in 1989 by Gottlieb, this carnival themed pinball is fun for all the family.

Come one, come all and experience all the fun of the fair.

Ring the bell on the PLUNGER SHOT and explode onto the playfield for carnival fun.

Aim at the shooting range targets, completing them all for big points and maybe even doubling your score.

Complete the T-E-D-D-Y and B-E-A-R targets to win an EXTRA BALL SPECIAL and aim at the elephant lane.

Enjoy the Calliope music and listen out for the bonus countdown “FREEZE” for big points.

name: Hurricane
desc: Hurricane is a pinball machine released by Williams Electronics in August 1991. It was designed by Barry Oursler as the third game in Oursler's amusement park themed pinball trilogy. The first being Comet, released in 1985, and the second being Cyclone, released in 1988.

name: Ice Fever (Gottlieb 1985) VPW 1.1
desc: The lit return lane (alternates) lights the spinner for 10K per spin instead of 1K. Shooting it dominates all other strategies on the game. Base bonus goes up to 29K, scored by any lane. Bonus multiplier goes up to 5X for 145K maximum total. Three goals (a hat trick) increases the bonus multiplier one level. Shoot the drop targets in front of the captive ball to expose it, hit the captive ball to score a goal. Completing the top three I-C-E lanes lights one of them for an extra ball which scores 100K; the lit EB lane cycles with switch hits. Basic strategy is to do whatever it takes to light the spinner, then do whatever it takes to set up shots to it on the left flipper. Shatzing either way is a good way to do these.

name: Independence Day
desc:
The Visual Pinball version of Independence Day from 1996 is a digital recreation of the original Sega pinball table, highlighting the collaboration and efforts of several enthusiasts within the Visual Pinball community. This table underwent a series of conversions and modifications, starting from VP8 and VP9 versions, and eventually being converted to the VPX format, which is known for its enhanced graphics and physics compared to older Visual Pinball versions.
Based on the blockbuster film this game bring the silver screen smash hit to life in true pinball fashion launch your ball to save the world from the invading aliens
Claim your place at the top with an truly out of this world experience
This pinball does not disappoint, featuring the voices of Jeff Goldblum, Will Smith and Bill Pullman, as well as two different multi-ball modes and stunning  visuals on the playfield and display. Its no wonder that this table was regularly featured in the industry awards for Game of the Year in the UK!

name: Indiana Jones
desc: Indiana Jones (not to be confused with the earlier Williams game Indiana Jones: The Pinball Adventure) is a pinball table made by Stern Pinball in 2008, coinciding with the release of Indiana Jones and the Kingdom of the Crystal Skull. It was designed by John Borg with artwork by Kevin O'Connor and programming by Keith Johnson. The game is all about the Indiana Jones film franchise, and there are four modes, one for each of them. It has a number of toys to further connect it to the movies, like recreations of the Ark, the Holy Grail, and the titular Crystal Skull, as well as a swordsman behind a wall. The game itself also has scenes from the movie fully recreated on the display. The game is also notable for having an eight-ball multiball mode, topped off with the infamous Ark scene from Raiders.

id: Indiana Jones The Pinball Adventure 1993 (Williams)/Indiana Jones The Pinball Adventure (Williams 1993) VPWmod v1.1.vpx
name: Indiana Jones The Pinball Adventure
desc:
Indiana Jones: The Pinball Adventure is a 1993 widebody pinball game designed by Mark Ritchie (the younger brother of acclaimed pinball designer Steve Ritchie) and released by Williams. It was based on the Indiana Jones movies. It was also part of WMS' SuperPin series of widebody games (see also The Twilight Zone and Star Trek: The Next Generation).
This game was the first game to use Williams / Midway's DCS Sound System. It features sound clips from the first three films, and actor John Rhys-Davies (reprising his role as Sallah) provided new speech for the game.
There are a total of 12 "modes" in Indiana Jones, each of them based on a scene from any of the three movies.

name: Indianapolis 500
desc:
Indianapolis 500 is a 1995 Licensed Pinball Table released by Williams Electronics under the Bally label. It was designed by Dennis Nordman, illustrated by Dan Hughes and Paul Barker, and features original voicework by motorsports broadcaster Paul Page, retired racer Bobby Unser, and legendary Indianapolis Motor Speedway track announcer Tom Carnegie.
Naturally, the game is a nonstop frenzy of speed as thirty-three racers compete to win the world-famous Indianapolis 500 auto race. As the table rumbles with the action, endure all two hundred laps, make your way past the other racers, and go for the Checkered Flag and the Victory Lap. Along the way, you'll collect spanners, complete waves, and pick up some souvenirs to boost your score. Complete the ten Speedway modes, Pass opponents to advance your Position, but watch out for Dueling Drivers or else you'll Hit The Wall. Go for the Speed Ramp and lock balls into the Turbo Boost, then make a quick in-and-out in the Pit to start two-ball multiball.

name: Iron Maiden (Stern 1982)
desc:
Iron Maiden is a Pinball Table designed by Brian Poklacki with artwork by Keith Parkinson. It was released by Stern in 1982.
Surprisingly enough, this pinball machine is not a licensed tie-in to the British heavy metal band. The title instead refers to its setting, an unspecified future where scantily-clad women use metal cables to interface with an ominous mechanical structure. There's no explanation for who they are or why they're doing this; the player is simply tasked to help them by spelling IRON MAIDEN on the two-level playfield, then load pinballs into the ball walker for three-ball multiball. Along the way, skillfully shoot the dropdown targets to earn bonus points, extra balls, and specials, and build up the Bonus Time bank for a final scoring opportunity.

desc: "JP's IT - Pinball Madness" is an original virtual pinball table created by a collaboration of talented designers, including jpsalas (who handled the VPX table, rules, and music), Joe Picasso (responsible for graphics, concept, and rules), and Unsavory (providing Pennywise voices), with Chucky contributing the directb2s. The game's layout is inspired by the Oktoberfest table, featuring unique physics designed by jpsalas to ensure it provides a compelling experience both on desktop and cabinet setups. For those interested in virtual reality (VR) gameplay, there's a version with enhancements like nFozzy flippers, Fleep sounds, and additional visual extras, alongside a video with instructions for an immersive VR experience, although it can also be played in desktop and cabinet modes. The game is designed to offer the same layout, graphics, rules, sounds, and music across versions, but differences in physics might slightly alter the gameplay experience​​​​​​.

name: Jack Bot
desc:
The Jack-Bot pinball game, released by Williams in 1995, is renowned for its engaging and complex gameplay, combining elements of traditional pinball with a futuristic casino theme. The game is a part of a series that includes Pin-Bot and The Machine: Bride of Pin-Bot, and it brings a unique twist to the pinball experience with its casino and gambling-themed elements, alongside high-tech features.
Gameplay includes a variety of objectives and modes that contribute to its depth. For instance, the Ramp and Vortex Increaser allows players to add points to the vortex value by shooting the ball up a ramp, with the potential to activate Solar Jets Mode or win random awards. The Inlane Awards feature provides opportunities for significant point gains or special conditions like lighting an extra ball. Players can engage with Casino Games by shooting the ball into a specific trap, further enriching the game's casino theme.
Jack-Bot also includes a Visor and 5x5 Grid Keno Lights, reminiscent of the original Pin-Bot, where players can unlock various bonuses and gameplay enhancements. The mechanics of locking balls for Multi-Ball mode and achieving Jack*Bots for high scores are central to the strategy and excitement of the game.
The game is noted for its challenging yet rewarding gameplay, high-quality graphics, and engaging themes, making it a beloved choice among pinball enthusiasts. Its implementation in the digital format through platforms like Visual Pinball X allows a broader audience to experience the thrill of Jack-Bot, with updates and modifications enhancing its appeal​​​​.

name: James Bond (Gottlieb 1980) 007
desc: Gottlieb's James Bond 007 is a rare solid state pinball machine released in 1980. It is based off the James Bond 007 movie franchise during Roger Moore's stint as the worlds smoothest spy. This table boasts four flippers, three pop bumpers, two slingshots, nine drop targets and three stand up targets, so there's certainly plenty to aim at whilst you get busy emulating the world's coolest secret agent.

name: James Bond (Stern 2022) LE
desc:
Stern’s James Bond 007 pinball machine uses film footage and iconic music from the films that built the 007 legend: Dr. No, From Russia With Love (1963), Goldfinger (1964), Thunderball (1965), You Only Live Twice (1967), and Diamonds Are Forever (1971). Players are immersed into the world of espionage in this action-packed pinball experience, tackling assignments, teaming up with key allies, and stopping SPECTRE’s villainous schemes.
Three versions of the machine were released in September 2022, the standard Pro Edition, a Premium Edition, and a Limited Edition (1,000 units). A special 60th Anniversary Limited Edition (500 units) was released in 2023.
Key Features:
- Based around six classic Bond films.
- Bond-themed playfield toys, targets & features.
- LCD video screen for cut-scenes & animations.
- James Bond Jetpack feature.

name: Joker Poker
desc:
"Joker Poker" is a pinball machine released in 1978 by Gottlieb. It stands out visually for its vibrant, eye-catching art that embodies the late 70s aesthetic, featuring a colorful and somewhat whimsical design centered around the card game theme. The backglass art prominently features various characters, including jesters and card figures, like kings, queens, and jokers, engaging in a lively game of poker. The playfield is equally detailed, with card suit symbols and illustrations that correspond to the poker theme, such as hearts, diamonds, spades, and clubs, alongside images of jokers and other face cards.
The machine's design includes a mix of bright reds, blues, greens, and yellows, creating a playful and inviting atmosphere. Traditional pinball features like bumpers, flippers, and targets are cleverly integrated with the poker theme, encouraging players to hit certain combinations that mimic winning poker hands. The overall visual presentation of "Joker Poker" not only highlights the fun and excitement of pinball but also pays homage to the game of poker, making it a memorable piece of entertainment from that era.

name: Jokerz!
desc:
Jokerz! is a gambling themed pinball machine released by Williams in 1988. The game was designed by Barry Oursler and Python Anghelo.
Now the deck is stacked in your favor with classic card game fun. Discover imaginative pinball as Jokerz! brings to life a timeless theme with proven play appeal. Innovative features and bring-’em-back challenges, Jokerz! has it all. There’s dynamic playfield kinetics combined with eye-catching graphics, original sounds, music and speech, and dazzling special effects for the kind of machine you’ve come to expect from the #1 pinball company in the world.
Jokerz! is a gambling themed pinball machine released by Williams in 1988. The game was designed by Barry Oursler and Python Anghelo. Popular marketing slogans for Jokerz! includes “Deal yourself in to a real winner!”, “Now the deck is stacked in your favor with classic card game fun.” and “Jokerz! IZ WILD!”
2 Flippers, 3 Pop bumpers, 3 3-bank drop targets, 2 Kick-out holes. Left and right ramps lead to small elevated playfield. Motorized center ramp raises for ball lock. Spinning wheel in backbox displays poker hand. 2 Multiball.

name: Jolly Park
desc: The visual pinball game "Jolly Park" from 1996, created by Spinball, features a table based on the original Spinball table. It includes traced and original images for all parts, 3D car objects, and a script based on an older table for the vpinmame script. The game includes unique features like activated magnets via magnasave buttons and a ROM that takes a bit longer to start. Version 4.0.0 brought updates such as VPX7 physics, cleaned-up graphics, a LUT changer for table darkness, enhanced sounds, and more​​.

Judas Priest Pinball (Original 2019)

This Judas Priest table is a theme of Skateball, built initially by JPSalas and Haunfreaks, and later modded by Siggi.

I updated the lighting, added more tunes from the Judas Priest catalog, and updated the ball to be a piece of molten metal, just like Judas Priest's music.  I also added music control to the Magna Save buttons:

Music Control:
Right Magna = Next Track
Left Magna = Stop Music

This music begins as soon as the table loads and only stops when the ball drains.  It starts again on the next song after you launch the ball.  There are also configuration settings in the script if you want to turn off the attract music and only have in-game music, or you can mute the music altogether.  You will enjoy in-game callouts by Rob Halford and some musical adornments depending on what kind of target you hit.

name: Judge Dredd
desc:
Judge Dredd is a licensed pinball machine based on the popular 2000 AD comic book character. Designed by John Trudeau, it was released by Williams Electronics under the Bally label in 1993.
In the year 2116, crime and chaos runs rampant through Mega-City One. The dips and the gumps are preying on the chumps, the heisters and joy poppers are shooting up the streets, and it's up to the player as Judge Dredd to rein in the drokkbuckets and keep the civos in line. But being a slab jock isn't just busting perps and fighting off trogs — there are suspects to shadow, crime scenes to clear, and runaway battle tanks to obliterate. Whip around the playfield on the Mega-City Super Highway, attack the Sniper Tower and hit the Subway, but watch out for Deadworld, because that's where the Dark Judges are waiting...

name: Jumanji (Original)
desc: The twelve minigames are carefully re-created based on iconic scenes from the films and feature authentic movie audio, thus making Jumanji immensely immersive, and a lot of fun. Players take on the role as one of the film's main characters to solve the entertaining and exciting games.

id: Jungle Lord 1981 (Williams)/Jungle Lord (Williams 1981) w VR Room v2.01.vpx
name: Jungle Lord
desc:
Jungle Lord is a 1981 pinball machine designed by Barry Oursler and produced by Williams Pinball. It features a Tarzan influenced theme, a multi-level playfield and a magnetic ball saver ("Magna Save"). Williams had introduced Magna Save in the Black Knight pinball game in 1980; Jungle Lord was one of four further Magna Save games produced in 1981, along with Pharaoh, Solar Fire and Grand Lizard. One difference from the Black Knight design was that Jungle Lord incorporated a "self-contained mini bagatelle style 'chamber' playfield, found on the top left-hand corner."
Jungle Lord also included an innovative scoring feature called Double Trouble, a drop target feature that engages when the player hits five special targets.

name: Junk Yard
desc:
The playfield of Junk Yard contains different toys e.g. a crane with a wrecking ball - a pinball hanging from a chain, a toilet that flushes the ball and a doghouse with an attack dog.
The player assumes the role of an inventor who is locked inside a junkyard after it has closed for the night and must find a way to escape. The goal is to collect pieces of junk and build various machines (shown on the blueprint in the center of the playfield), each of which enables a mode or mini-game when completed. Once all the modes have been played, the player can start one more mode involving a battle against the junkyard owner in outer space. A devil and angel give tips to the player on what to do. Slingshots are lit by controlled lights, so either the angel or devil can be lit. The game also contains modes featured in previous Williams pinball titles, such as the video mode from Attack from Mars.
The game uses an instrumental version of the song "Money (That's What I Want)" as its primary background music.

name: Jurassic Park
desc: The Jurassic Park pinball machine, produced by Data East in June 1993, is a solid state game designed around the theme of the iconic movie. It features a dot matrix display and accommodates up to four players. The machine includes three flippers, one ramp, and supports a six-ball multiball play. Esteemed for its engaging gameplay, the design team included Ed Cebula, Joe Kaminkow, and John Borg, with artwork by Markus Rothkranz. Sound and music contributions came from Brian Schmidt, incorporating John Williams' compositions. Approximately 9,008 units were produced, and it's currently valued between $4,160 and $4,840​​.

It has the player going through five modes, each recreating a scene from the movie, before reaching the Wizard Mode: San Diego, where the T-Rex rampages and any major shot scores an increasing value, and any target increases the value.
One of its main gimmicks is the large T-Rex egg that breaks steadily, ultimately revealing the baby T-Rex inside. It also had an optional topper replicating the film's logo, and a curvy 3D backglass.

desc: Kingpin was the last game made by Capcom and only a few were made before Capcom closed their doors. Designer Mark Ritchie was working on this game before Flipper Football was even started, but Flipper Football was rushed to production to precede it, making Kingpin the last game.

id: Kings of Steel 1984 (Bally)/Kings Of Steel (Bally 1984) v2.0.0.vpx
name: Kings Of Steel
desc: "Kings of Steel" is a pinball machine launched in March 1984 by Bally Manufacturing Co. It features a digital display, accommodates up to four players, and is known for its solid state technology. The design team included Greg Kmiec on game design, Rehman Merchant for software, Doug Watson for artwork, and the sound was created by Bob Libbe, M. Bartlow, and Neil Falconer. This machine stands out for not having any ramps or multiball features, and it supports three flippers. Approximately 2,900 units of "Kings of Steel" were produced, and its value is estimated between $1200 - $1400​​.

name: Kiss
desc:
The KISS pinball machine, produced by Bally in 1979, is a celebrated piece that captures the essence of the iconic rock band, KISS. This machine is notable for featuring all four original members of the band, with artwork inspired by their 1977 "Love Gun" era costumes. Despite the band having significantly changed their look by the time the game was launched, the side cabinet portraits echo the style of their 1978 solo album covers.
This pinball machine is equipped with 2 flippers, 4 pop-bumpers with alternating point values, 2 sling shots, a 4 target drop target bank, 8 stand-up targets, and a 4x4 grid of lights aimed at completing rows for bonuses. It also features a special AS-2518-50 sound board that plays snippets of "Rock and Roll All Night" and "Shout It Out Loud" for the game start and end tunes, respectively, maintaining the thematic connection to KISS's music.
A unique aspect of the KISS pinball machine is its distinction in the German market, which received a version with rounded 'S's in the KISS name, instead of the lightning bolt 'S's, to adhere to local sensibilities.
With a production run of 17,000 units, the KISS pinball machine stands as one of the highest production volumes for Bally's first generation of electronic sound pinball machines. Among the prototypes produced, there were 11 wooden cabinet versions and a special white fiberglass cabinet version, built to showcase at the 1979 AMOA show in Chicago, featuring a unique speech board set.
The game was designed by Jim Patla and featured artwork by Kevin O'Connor, contributing to its distinctive appearance and gameplay experience reflective of the KISS brand​​​​.

name: Knight Rider (Original)
desc: Knight Rider is a fan-made digital pinball table inspired by the iconic 1980s TV series. Step into the role of Michael Knight and join forces with KITT, the AI-powered supercar, to battle crime across high-speed missions. With voice clips, music, and visuals pulled straight from the show, the table captures the thrill of the series through fast-paced ramps, mission modes, and multi-ball action. A tribute to justice, turbo boosts, and synthwave nostalgia—one flip at a time.

name: Krull (Gottlieb 1983)
desc:
Krull is an arcade pinball machine from Gottlieb, designed by John Trudeau and illustrated by Keith Parkinson.

Based on the 1983 Cult Classic Science Fantasy movie of the same name, this game casts the player as Prince Colwyn, who must defeat The Beast and his army of Slayers to rescue Princess Lyssa and liberate their world. Venture to the lair of the Crystal Spider in the upper level and knock down the target bank to enable the extra ball, then drop to the middle playfield and defeat the Slayers to enable the Transfer. Hit the center target banks to power up the Glave, then drop down to the lower-level playfield and challenge the Beast in the bowels of the Black Fortress.

Krull's most notable trait is its lower-level playfield; while earlier games like Black Hole and Haunted House had simplified mini tables below the main level, Krull had a second, nearly full-sized playfield inside the cabinet, which the player viewed through a plexiglass lenticular window. Unfortunately, this significantly increased the cost of the game — and when the movie bombed at the box office, management canceled it just before mass-production was to begin. Only 10 completed prototypes exist.

id: Laser Cue 1984 (Williams)/Laser Cue (Williams 1984) w VR Room 2.0.0.vpx
name: Laser Cue
desc: Laser Cue is a four flipper game in 1984, and features an unusual “billiards in space”, science-fiction theme. The game is similar in layout to designer Ed Tomaszewski’s release four years earlier, Alien Poker. Despite Laser Cue being released years after speech had been perfected by Williams Electronics for their games, it features no speech chip. Instead, the game is equipped with a bell that rings when billiard balls are collected or extra balls achieved. The main bank of drop targets are individually controlled, and must be collected in the indicated order to remain dropped. Extra ball play guarantees the player twenty-five seconds of play time, serving all lost balls within that time back to the shooter lane.

id: Laser War 1987 (Data East)/Laser War (Data East 1987) w VR Room v2.0.vpx
name: Laser War
desc:
In 1985, after Stern Electronics closed its doors, the pinball factory and assets were purchased by Data East, who resurrected it as their new pinball division. Their first table was 1987's Laser War, designed by Joe Kaminkow, programmed by Lonnie Ropp, and illustrated by Margaret Hudson and Kevin O'Connor.
Like the title says, the game is centered on a futuristic firefight between three teams welding Ray Guns shooting Frickin' Laser Beams. Hit the Red, Yellow, and Blue targets, then return to the corresponding colored bases to enable multiball. Charge up the Ion Cannon, then fire it during three-ball multiball for a devastating million points. Let the 2.1 stereo sound keep your adrenaline pumping, but don't get distracted by the nonstop lightshow and dazzling flashers.

id: Last Action Hero 1993 (Data East)/Last Action Hero (Data East 1993) VPW 2.0.vpx
name: Last Action Hero
desc:
Last Action Hero is a 1993 Licensed Pinball Table from Data East. It was designed by Tim Seckel, Joe Kaminkow, Ed Cebula, and John Borg, with illustrations by Markus Rothkranz.
As one would expect, the game casts players as Jack Slater and Danny Madigan as they go through ten explosive events from the movie. Race to the Roof, Double your Bonus, chase mice with Whiskers the Cat, then Find Benedict and Save Danny to avoid the Big Mistake. Use the Super Crane to move balls around the table, and if you can endure Lt. Dekker's tirades, the quaking cabinet, and the ball-flinging magnets, you can earn your action-hero creds to attend the World Premiere for a six-ball M-ball bonanza accompanied by music from AC/DC, Queensrÿche, and Megadeth.

name: League Champ (Williams 1996)V1.1
desc:
This is a VPX recreation of a 1996 Williams League Champ Shuffle Alley Bowler. This is a complete remake by me Rascal, not a conversion. Started from scratch.
Thanks to roccodimarco for his League Champ hood panel image.
Flippers move arm left and right. Analog and digital plunger pulls the arm forwards and backwards and starts angle rotation.
Left Magna key for the game selection and to save the name.

name: Led Zeppelin
desc:
The Visual Pinball Led Zeppelin table from 2020 has garnered attention for its engaging gameplay and vibrant visuals, inspired by the iconic rock band Led Zeppelin. Users have praised the table for its balance, aesthetics, and the way it incorporates Led Zeppelin's music, creating a unique pinball experience. Notable features include the incorporation of full dynamic media displays (DMD) and a variety of lighting and color schemes that enhance the visual appeal and gameplay experience. The table also includes a "real nice color BG image" and "start light animation," alongside full DMD with all the accompanying features, making it a tribute to Led Zeppelin's legacy.
Feedback from the community highlights the table's artistic design, with original artwork by Brad Albright and mod designs by David Peck, among others. It's appreciated not just for its gameplay mechanics but also for how it captures the spirit of Led Zeppelin's music and the era it represents. The table has undergone updates to improve physics, user options, and overall fun, indicating a commitment to quality and player satisfaction​​​​​​.

id: Lethal Weapon 3 1992 (Data East)/Lethal Weapon 3 (Data East 1992) VPW 2.0.vpx
name: Lethal Weapon 3
desc:
Lethal Weapon 3 is a Licensed Pinball Table from Data East. It was designed by Joe Kaminkow and Ed Cebula, with artwork by Markus Rothkranz. The game was released in June 1992, just a month after the premiere of the third movie.
The game is somewhat misnamed, as it actually incorporates scenes and sound clips from the first three films. Hit the three LW saucers to complete various stunts like the High Fall, Joshua's helicopter, and Murtaugh's exploding toilet, then cap them off with the Super Stunt Spectacular. Alternately, shoot the outer loop to load bullets into the Uzi, then use it to shoot the villains on the display for various bonuses. Cut the correct wire to disarm the bomb, shoot the practice targets for Leo Getz, then loop the right orbit in the Getaway while Crazy Riggs racks up the score to the accompaniment of The Three Stooges. For even faster scoring, start the Lotsaballs multiball mode, then try to score the Speed, Double, and Quadruple Jackpots.

name: Lightning
desc: A fast double level game with a fantasy Norse god theme. It's got 3-ball multiball, speech and a timed bonus ball mode that you earn once you've reached a certain (adjustable) score. Extra ball is lit by shooting the drop target banks in sequence. The extra ball shot then moves between the 3 drop target banks by the hit of one of the four slingshots until you collect it. Your end of ball bonus is shown on an extra display in the playfield. It carries over between balls. It can be maxed at 99k and multiplied to a maximum of 5x. Bonus x also carries over ball to ball, unless you reach 5x. Then it resets to 1x on the next ball. Multiball enables the horseshoe for playfield multipliers to a maximum of 4x. This feature stays lit for the rest of the ball, even in one ball-play, until the maximum has been reached. Balls can be re-captured during multiball play, resulting in single ball play (without draining one of them). The spinner is lit for 1000 points via the horseshoe. It is lit for only one shot then goes back to 100 points. This means you can have 4x playfield and spinner lit for 4000/spin!

name: Lights Camera Action (Gottlieb 1989)
desc:
Lights... Camera... Action! is an arcade pinball game released by Gottlieb (under the "Premier" label) in 1989. It was designed by Jon Norris, with artwork by Brian Johnson and Constantino Mitchell. It was also one of the company's earliest System 3 tables, allowing for a more complicated game (similar to their competitors).

In this game, the player is a budding Director working on a summer action movie. Under the heat of the spotlights, travel around San Francisco, wrap up the five big Scenes, and finish the Blockbuster. Complete the Stunt Sequence, perform the Helicopter Rescue loop, then flip the ramp and film the big Shoot-Out in the backbox. Keep an eye on the countdown timer embedded in the playfield, use the Catch-Up feature to stay in the game, and collect the stars' playing cards to build up your Poker Hands.

name: Linkin Park (Original 2024)
desc:
Linkin Park Music Table with PupPack!
I plan on redoing most of my music tables so if you have the old version of Linkin Park Pup table please delete everything before installing this one.
The zip file includes the vpx table, wheel image and the pup pack.  The puppack comes with a bunch screen options to suit your cabinet needs, just choose your bat file. You can also add your favorite Linkin Park videos to the favorites folder within the LINKINPARKPUP folder.


Shout-outs!!!!  I want to thank TeamTuga and JP salas for their work on the original table. If it wasn't for these amazing guys, I wouldn't have been able to create this table. They are the best!


Hope you enjoy!

name: Lost in Space (Sega 1998)
desc:
Based on the hit movie adaptation of the classic television show Lost In Space.

Featuring three different kinds:  Robot Multi-ball, Fighter Multi-ball and Condition Red Multi-ball - all  will win you massive points!

Lost  in Space also features a spinning magnetic disc that simulates the  gravitational field of a gas giant, grabbing and tossing balls across the playfield.

Spell  W-A-R-N-I-N-G to light the robot replica for unlimited super jackpots  and slingshot around the outer planets on one of the smoothest ramps  ever created!

This machine also features detailed replicas of the Jupiter 2, Major Don West's bubble fighter and our favourite robot!

id: Lost In Space (SEGA 1998) DrJones Comic-book Edition/Lost In Space (SEGA 1998) DrJones Comic-book Edition v1.0.vpx
name: Lost In Space (SEGA 1998) DrJones Comic-book Edition
desc:
A fresh re-imagining of SEGA's Lost in Space 1998 table for Visual Pinball X. It keeps the fast flow, multiball madness, playfield layout and rule set of the 1998 table intact, but completely transforms the presentation into a comic-book celebration of Irwin Allen’s original 1960s television series.

Whereas the original table leaned on murky 1990 film stills and off-the-shelf plastic toys, this version replaces them with hand drawn character art evoking the spirit of the original show. The playfield and plastics have been redrawn, illustrating the Robinson family as well as the iconic “monsters of the week”. This gives this fast and fun John Bord table the theme treatment it always deserved. Enjoy the multiball mayhem!

name: Lost World (Bally 1979)
desc:
Lost World is a pinball machine released by Bally in 1977. The game features a fantasy theme. It should not to be confused with the pinball machine Escape from the Lost World from 1987.

Lost World is the first pinball machine that uses electronic sounds which replaces chimes. It is also the first machine that uses a photographic backglass. The game spawned a sequel - Paragon released in 1979.

The machine features a simple gameplay with the goal of hitting the A-B-C-D-E-F targets repeatedly. The playfield contains very few other feature including three pop bumpers, two kickouts, a captive ball and a spinner.

id: Lunelle (Taito do Brasil 1982)/Lunelle (Taito do Brasil - 1982) v600.vpx
name: Lunelle (Taito do Brasil - 1982)
desc: Lunelle is a rare solid-state pinball machine released around 1982 by Taito do Brasil, the Brazilian division of the Japanese company Taito. The game is widely known among enthusiasts for being a clone or heavily inspired by Williams' 1980 classic, Alien Poker.

name: Mad Race (Playmatic 1985)
desc:
Mad Race is a rare, solid-state pinball machine released in 1985 by Playmatic, a manufacturer based in Barcelona, Spain. The game is highly collectible and believed to be extremely rare, with some estimates suggesting only two or three actual machines still exist.

The artwork is widely considered to be inspired by the Mad Max films popular during that era.

name: Magic
desc: The visual pinball game "Magic" by Stern, released in 1979, has been recreated for Visual Pinball X (VPX) platforms, offering an enhanced digital pinball experience with several updates and improvements. This version of the game features new lighting and shadows for flippers and balls, improved table physics, and additional physics effects like nFozzy flippers physics. The sound has been upgraded with Fleep Sounds, and for virtual reality (VR) users, a VR room has been added. The playfield image and all images have been reworked, cleaned, and upscaled for better visual quality. Other enhancements include corrected bumper heights, repositioned bumpers, adjusted playfield lights, and many other adjustments to improve the gameplay experience. The game is available strictly for personal/home use and not for commercial sale, re-sale, or distribution, and modifications are allowed with approval​​​​.

name: Magic Pinball v1.0 (Original 2025)
desc:
Magic Pinball is an original table, so please be kind, it's my first one

I wanted to create a magical and immersive atmosphere, and I hope you enjoy it!

I would like to extend a big thank you to JP Salas and Balutito for their permission and kindness, as well as to the entire community.

If you have any comments, suggestions, or encounter any bugs, please feel free to report them in the comments so I can improve the table.

For the full DMD, loading screen, and wheel, see my other files.

Happy holidays and have fun playing Magic Pinball!

id: Mago de Oz - the pinball/Mago de Oz - the pinball v601.vpx
name: Mago de Oz
desc: The Mago de Oz pinball table, a Visual Pinball X Original from 2021, is inspired by the graphics and music of the Spanish folk rock group Mägo de Oz. The development of this table was suggested by a member named Enomao, who also facilitated contact with the band. The band kindly provided high-resolution images of their CD covers, which were used to create all the graphics for the table. This particular table draws inspiration from the layout and rules of Archer & Stern’s Iron Maiden tables and requires the latest VPX 10.7 version for the best experience. The table is recognized for its incorporation of updated physics, LUT images for different lighting options, and a set of mechanical sounds to enhance the playing experience. Additionally, it includes various improvements like fixed flashers and updated mechanical sounds for a more immersive experience​​​​​​.

id: Mars - God of War 1981 (Gottlieb)/Mars God Of War (Gottlieb 1981) Physics Sound VR MOD 1.1.vpx
name: Mars God Of War
desc: The "Mars God of War" is a pinball machine released by D. Gottlieb & Co. in March 1981. It stands out for its unique wide-body cabinet design, digital display, and capacity for up to 4 players. The game includes 4 flippers, a single ramp, and supports a 3-ball multiball play. This pinball machine was produced in a series of 5,240 units and is characterized by its solid state technology, being part of the Gottlieb System 80 generation. The estimated value of the machine ranges between $1200 and $1400. The artwork for this machine was done by David Moore, and John Buras was responsible for both the game design and software development. "Mars God of War" incorporates themes of sci-fi and mythology, with the tagline "The Power Of Mars Challenges You." It has become a sought-after collector's item, with 159 Pinsiders having it in their collections and 57 wishing to acquire it. The machine is also available to play in 13 public locations​​.

id: Mary Shelley's Frankenstein 1995 (Sega)/Mary Shelley's Frankenstein (Sega 1995) v2.0.4.vpx
name: Mary Shelley's Frankenstein
desc:
Mary Shelley's Frankenstein is a Physical Pinball Table designed by John Borg and illustrated by Paul Faris. Based on the Tri-Star film directed by Kenneth Branagh, it was released in January 1995 as the debut pin from Sega Pinball.
As expected, the game revisits key scenes from Victor Frankenstein's experiments to reverse death. Travel to Ingolstadt, collect body parts from the Graveyard, then raise the Voltage to reanimate The Creature. Lynch Justine, start Geneva Multiball, and endure the Stoning, and try to pick up an Extra Ball or Frankenstein Millions along the way. Players who can get to the Ice Cave in the North Pole might be able to complete the Creation and discover the game's final secrets — but watch out when the Creature begins throwing pinballs at you...

name: Mass Effect 1.0.6
Mata-Hari
desc:
Mata Hari is a pinball machine created by Bally Manufacturing released in 1978.
The theme of the game is based on Mata Hari who was a renown exotic dancer in Paris, she became a spy for the French during WW1 but was suspected of being a double agent and was executed by firing squad in France.
The game has chimes as it was designed before electronic sounds were used and allows up to four players. The table has a completely symmetric playfield layout and features two flippers, four pop bumpers, two slingshots, two four-bank drop targets and one kick-out hole.

name: Maverick
desc:
The Movie is an arcade pinball game based on the 1994 Western comedy film starring Mel Gibson. Designed by Tim Seckel with artwork by Morgan Weistling, this was the last game from Data East's pinball division before it was sold to Sega.
In this game, the player is a Professional Gambler riding aboard the Lauren Belle, trying to get into the All Rivers Poker Championship. After the deal, knock down the flashing drop target bank to beat the table's hand and build up your poker chips. Draw carefully to avoid needless discards, raise your bet if you're feeling lucky, or fold your hand if you're getting cold feet. Between rounds of poker, play some blackjack, collect Coop's Cash, or take a walk around the Belle, but look out for Angel's Revenge, the runaway Stagecoach, and the Bank Heist. If you can collect enough chips for the entry fee, enter the Championship, then try to keep your cool and take the Championship Pot.

name: Medieval Castle (VR ROOM) MEGA
desc:
Hello, I present to you my conversion of Medieval Castle for Future Pinball in VPX format.

I'm an amateur creator; it's a hobby. Enjoy the game!

name: Medieval Madness
desc: The centerpiece of the playfield is an animated castle with a solenoid-controlled portcullis and motorized drawbridge. One of the game's primary objectives is to "destroy" six castles by hitting the castle's entryway with the pinball. A specific number of hits will lower the drawbridge, exposing the portcullis; additional hits will cause the portcullis to rise, and shooting the ball into the castle entrance generates an explosion effect on the dot matrix display, a lightshow, and a sizable award of points. Medieval Madness also features two Trolls, animated targets that are normally concealed below the playfield, but can pop up during certain gameplay modes. Other objectives can be scored by shooting the left and right ramps, the left and right orbits, and the catapult ramp in the lower left corner of the playfield. The game's ramps introduced a patented feature that would prevent a failed ramp shot from draining straight down the middle between the flippers.

name: Medusa
desc:
The Medusa pinball machine, manufactured by Bally in September 1981, is a classic solid-state game. Designed by Wally Welch, with software by Rehman Merchant and artwork by Kevin O'Connor, it's known for its distinct theme drawn from mythology, featuring elements of monsters and mythological narratives. This game was part of the Bally MPU AS-2518-35 generation, and a total of 3,250 units were produced.
Medusa stands out for its gameplay features, including 4 flippers, but it does not include ramps or multiball, which were less common features at the time. The game supports up to 4 players and displays scores on a digital screen. It's housed in a standard cabinet with a digital display type.
Regarding its market value and collector interest, Medusa's estimated value ranges between $3,240 and $3,760. The machine's popularity is reflected in its Pinside rating of 7.784 out of 10, ranking it #125 in the Pinside Pinball Top 100 as of the last update. The game has been listed for sale numerous times, indicating a healthy interest among collectors and enthusiasts.
The marketing slogan for Medusa was "Bally MEDUSA... A Legend of Features," underscoring the game's appeal through its rich feature set and legendary theme​​.

id: Metallica Premium Monsters (Stern 2013)/Metallica Premium Monsters (Stern 2013) VPW 2.0.2.vpx
name: Metallica Premium Monsters (Stern 2013) VPW 2.0.2
desc:
The Metallica Premium Monsters pinball machine, specifically the visual pinball version modded for Visual Pinball X (VPX), is a collaborative effort that has seen several updates and improvements over the years. This digital recreation aims to closely mimic the original Stern 2013 table, focusing on aspects like playfield accuracy, physics, and sound enhancements to offer an immersive pinball experience.
One notable version is the Bigus(MOD) 2.0, which includes a variety of enhancements over its predecessors. This version boasts better lighting, physics, and sound, thanks to the efforts of creators like Hauntfreaks, Freneticamnesic, Sliderpoint, and Byancey. The table's overhaul was aimed at making the digital experience as close as possible to playing the actual physical pinball machine​​.
Another significant update came from the VPin Workshop Discord community, which undertook a comprehensive "table tune-up." This version introduced a straighter playfield, Flupper inserts, new flashers, Fleep sounds, and the latest nFozzy physics among other improvements. This mod of a mod saw contributions from a wide range of creators, including EBisLit, iaakki, and Sixtoe, who worked on various aspects like playfield alignment, physics, lighting, and 3D insert techniques​​.

id: Metallica Master Of Puppets 2013 (Stern Pinball)/Metallica Master of Puppets.vpx
name: Metallica: Master of Puppets
desc:
The Metallica Master of Puppets Table and Pup Pack (version 2.0) is a detailed visual pinball experience designed for fans of the iconic Metallica album. It requires VPX 10.7 and introduces several new features, including call-outs on the apron and fire effects on the shooting lane, thanks to contributions from Nailbuster. An interesting addition is the option for a two-screen setup with a topper, which can be turned on or off in the script, allowing users to choose the quality of the apron and shooting lane videos. The package includes an ADD_ON folder, and it's noted that if you already have the pup pack, you don't need to download it again. Just drop the files from the ADD_ON folder into the pup pack folder to replace the old ones and run the BAT file for your configuration.
The installation involves several components: a muted ROM, color ROM, the pup pack itself, and a specific VPX table file. It's designed to work with a color DMD (dot matrix display) for enhanced visual experience, and detailed instructions are provided for setting up everything correctly, including troubleshooting tips for common issues like CGamename errors​​​​.

name: Meteor
desc:
Meteor is an arcade pinball machine designed by Steve Kirk of Stern Electronics, with artwork by George Obregon. it was a tie-in to the 1979 disaster movie of the same name, and was released a month after the film's theatrical debut.
Like its namesake, Meteor requires the player to stop a five-mile-wide "meteor" from colliding with the Earth. This is done by firing three nuclear missiles at the menace; hitting a three-bank of drop targets for each missile advances it one step closer. Keeping all three missiles aligned lights WOW for all of them to increase scores, while spelling METEOR increases the bonus multiplier. Advancing all three missiles to the meteor gives the player a chance for a free game. The game also made good use of its solid-state design, resetting and remembering game states and drop targets for each player.

name: Michael
desc: Original Tribute Michael Jackson created by Marty02 June 2026. It is a modern release featuring high-end visual design and lighting that reacts dynamically to the musical beat. The table stands out for its deep integration with an advance PuP Pack that allows you to select between various music clips, synchronizing the action on the playfield with the media content. It features a custom layout with fast-flowing metal ramps and an interactive central playfield area dedicated to the King of Pop's greatest hits.

name: Michael Jordan (Data East 1992)2.0.4
desc: The "Michael Jordan" pinball machine by Data East, released in 1992, is a rare custom-built game with only seven units produced. Designed to raise money for charity, the game is based on the "Lethal Weapon 3" pinball framework and features basketball-themed elements, including a "Be Like Mike" music tie-in. The machine has two flippers, one ramp, and a three-ball multiball mode.

desc: Polo and Mini Cycle are pinball machines manufactured by D. Gottlieb & Co. in 1970. Both games share the same playfield design, with Polo being the four-player version and Mini Cycle the two-player variant. These machines feature two flippers, three pop bumpers, a vari-target, a kick-out hole, and a free ball return lane.

name: Minions
desc:
The "Minions" table for Visual Pinball X (VPX) is an updated version of the original Minions table. This table is a significant upgrade from the Future Pinball version created by ROM and Nitronimbus, with DrSandraNo undertaking the major changes to fix, implement, and complete routines so that major goals within the game could be reached​​. The game originally had issues with repetitive music and unclear progression paths, but these have been addressed in this version, allowing players to attempt a 50 million goal once all five main goals are completed. These goals include completing all targets, opening the hideout and knocking down three minion popups, performing a MultiBall run, running up all the ramps, and running down all the inner and outer lanes to hit the Collect Lanes four times and play the four narrations​​.
The table includes an Options Screen that can be activated by holding the left flipper button down for 1.5 seconds between games, allowing players to set the number of balls, switch between free play and credit, change music, and reset high scores​​. Installation involves adding the table, backglass, and Minions.UltraDMD directory to the table directory, as well as copying the contents of the Music directory to the VPX Music directory​​.

name: Miraculous
desc: The Visual Pinball version titled "Miraculous," released in 2019, is an original table inspired by the TV series Miraculous: The Adventures of Ladybug & Cat Noir. It was designed as a children's table, featuring a layout based on the Fireball home version. The game is themed around the adventures of Ladybug and Cat Noir, aiming to provide fun in the spirit of traditional pinball gameplay. Players are encouraged to score as high as possible and to earn as many extra balls as they can, with the primary goal being fun and high scores rather than mimicking the combative aspects of the TV series​​.

id: Monday Night Football 1989 (Data East)/Monday Night Football (Data East 1989)_Bigus(MOD)2.1.vpx
name: Monday Night Football
desc:
The Monday Night Football pinball machine, produced by Data East in September 1989, is a solid-state electronic game that celebrates the famous ABC TV show of the same name. The game was designed by Joe Kaminkow and Ed Cebula, with software by Lonnie D. Ropp, artwork by Kevin O'Connor, and both music and sound by David Thiel. A total of 1,492 units were manufactured between September and November 1989.
This football-themed pinball game features a playfield with goal posts that rise in the middle for an extra point opportunity, multiball, ramps, and various targets to aim for. It encourages players to score both football points and pinball points, adding a layer of fun especially when played with friends. Achieving the Extra Point is notably enjoyable, with a specific high score for it. Despite the constrained playfield making Multiball a challenge, completing it offers a high degree of satisfaction. The game also includes a skillful shot to a right scoop lock, which is difficult but rewarding when achieved.
The Monday Night Football pinball machine has an alphanumeric display, supports up to 4 players, and includes 2 flippers, 3 ramps, and a 3-ball multiball feature. Its cabinet is of the standard type used during the era, and it falls under the DataEast/Sega Version 2 generation of pinball machines. The estimated value of this machine ranges between $2,680 and $3,120, with a median asking price of around $2,850 in recent listings​​​​.

name: Monkey Island (Original)

name: Monopoly
desc:
Monopoly is a 2001 pinball machine released by Stern, designed by Pat Lawlor and his crew at Pat Lawlor Design. Based on the classic board game, it contains several elements from its source, altered to fit the new medium. The main goal is to progress around the board by shooting certain shots, stopping to buy property, while ultimately becoming rich enough to own it all.
The machine has several notable features, such as a rotating flipper on the far right that often screws with the ball’s path and a mini-dot matrix display.

name: Monster Bash
desc:
The main goal of the game is to collect the instruments of the iconic horror characters and form the Monsters of Rock band, The table includes a Phantom Flip. Players can let go of the flippers with this auto-play feature and watch the game complete the shots.
The machine has an easter egg mode called “Lyman’s Lament”. It features different music and comments of programmer Lyman Sheats while the ball is played

name: Mortal Kombat II
desc: The Mortal Kombat II Pinball Edition VPX is a tribute to the iconic game Mortal Kombat II, originally created by Ed Boon in 1993. It requires Visual Pinball 10.2 rev2830 or later to run. This pinball version introduces multiple features to emulate the Mortal Kombat II experience, including multiple ramps for combos, requirements to hit 8, 16, or 24 ramps for extra balls, defeating all characters for multiballs, and completing MK Targets for Multiball among others. This edition has been Javier's first original table, and it was submitted for download on December 15, 2016, and last updated on January 13, 2017. The file size is approximately 596.95MB, and it has garnered significant attention with over 46,851 views and 27,857 downloads. Javier allows modifications to the table without approval, showing a commitment to community involvement and adaptation​​​​​​.

name: Motörhead
desc: The Visual Pinball Motörhead 2018 table is an homage to the legendary rock band Motörhead, celebrated for their influence in the rock and heavy metal genres. This table is a Visual Pinball X Original, crafted with a design that captures the essence of Motörhead's music and legacy. It features custom sound adjustments for a more immersive experience, including the option to import mp3 files of Motörhead's songs to enhance gameplay. The default backdrop color for desktop users is green, but black & white, blue, and red options are also available for customization. This table is based on the "Blackout" table by Williams, requiring the ROM "blkou_l1". It includes 30 songs, primarily from the albums "Overkill", "Bomber", and "Ace of Spades", celebrating the band members Lemmy Kilmister, Fast Eddie Clarke, and Philthy Animal Taylor. The Motörhead table not only serves as a tribute to the band's music but also aims to introduce their rock 'n' roll legacy to both fans and newcomers alike​​.
