name: Mousin' Around!
desc: "Mousin' Around!" is a physical pinball machine released by Bally in December 1989. The theme revolves around a group of mischievous mice having a party, and the player's objective is to catch the mice. The artwork is vibrant and cartoonish, featuring a variety of mouse characters engaging in fun activities, such as skateboarding, playing instruments, and enjoying cheese. The playfield is designed with several ramps, bumpers, and targets that are adorned with illustrations of mice and cheese, emphasizing the playful and lighthearted theme. The backglass artwork prominently displays the mouse characters in a party scene, with a colorful and engaging composition that captures the essence of the game's fun atmosphere. The machine also includes digital displays and lighting effects that enhance the visual experience and provide feedback on the player's progress and achievements.

id: Mr. and Mrs. Pac-Man (Bally 1982)/Mr. and Mrs. Pac-Man (Bally 1982) Goldchicco 1.0 DT-FS-VR-MR Ext2k Conversion.vpx
name: Mr. & Mrs. Pac-Man Pinball (Bally 1982)
desc:
Mr. & Mrs. Pac-Man Pinball is a Physical Pinball Table produced by Bally/Midway in 1982. It was designed by George Christian, and was the first of two Pinball Spin-Off games Bally made for the popular Pac-Man franchise.note
This title is remarkable for being an early attempt at combining a Pinball with a Video Game. Embedded in the center of the playfield is the "Vid-Grid Pac-Maze", a five-by-five matrix of lights. The player earns Moves and extra lives by playing the pinball table, and can enter the Maze by shooting one of the two saucers after he has at least six Moves. Using the flipper buttons,note  the player makes Pac-Man (a flashing yellow light) light up all of the spaces, while avoiding the Ghost, a flashing red light. The player can escape by moving Pac-Man around the edges of the maze, or earn "Pac-Man Aggressive" on the pinball table to catch the Ghost instead.

name: Mustang
desc: The "Mustang" pinball table for Visual Pinball X, released in 2014 by Stern, is celebrated for its dynamic gameplay and exceptional visual design. It features a fast-paced gameplay experience that includes a unique turntable mechanism, rotating with a model of a Mustang car at its center. This element not only adds a visual spectacle but also integrates into the gameplay, offering players a unique challenge. The work by Dozer and the team on this table is noted for its beautiful rendition, with the lighting and visuals still regarded as top-notch. This table is a tribute to the iconic Mustang car and stands out in the virtual pinball community for its attention to detail and the immersive playing experience it provides​​.

id: Mystery Castle1993  (Alvin G)/Mystery Castle (Alvin G 1993) v.2.3.1.vpx
name: Mystery Castle
desc: "Mystery Castle," produced by Alvin G. and Company in 1993, is a rare pinball machine due to its low production volume. The machine's backglass features a spooky-looking castle, hinting at the game's objectives, while the playfield is noted for being quite vacant for the era, which possibly contributed to its poor sales. The side artwork and coin door also have distinctive designs. This pinball machine is a solid-state electronic type, with notable features including three flippers but no pop bumpers. It was designed by Wally Welch and Michael Gottlieb, with art by Dan Hughes, and only 500 units were produced​​.

name: Mystic (Bally 1980)
desc: The Mystic pinball machine, produced by Bally in June 1980, is a solid-state game. The machine features a magic theme with elements inspired by mythology and cards.

name: Nascar
desc:
NASCAR is an arcade pinball game designed by Pat Lawlor and illustrated by John Youssi. It was released in 2005 by Stern Pinball.
As one would expect, this table is based on NASCAR, the popular American autoracing sport. With accompanying commentary by NBC's Allen Bestwick, launch balls onto the magnetically-charged oval speedway around the playfield and scream into the action, then enter the Hauler truck and rack up the Miles and make the Speed Shots on the Road Course. Raise the Test Car to access the underground Garage, where you can whoop it up with the Super Fan, indulge in Happy Hour, and join the Infield Party, but watch out for the Bump 'N Run. Spell RACE to lock pinballs for multiball, collect the various Jackpot bonuses, then freeze the Super Jackpot and add more balls for bigger points. If you can make it through the rigors of the oval and take a Victory Lap, celebrate with a Super Party — and then take on the Champion Challenge.

name: NBA
desc:
The Visual Pinball - NBA from 2009, created by Stern Pinball, Inc., was launched during the 2009 NBA playoffs and featured 20 players from 20 different NBA teams. This pinball machine offers various mechanical features such as a spinning disk in the playfield center, a captive ball, drop targets, ramps, a diverter, and more. One of the highlights is its basketball backboard with a magnet in the center to assist in making shots. The game allows for three types of basketball shots: a ramp shot, a jump shot, and a free throw shot, each designed to mimic the action of shooting a basketball into a hoop.
The artwork for the NBA pinball machine was created by Pinball Hall of Fame artist Kevin O'Connor, with sound production by David Thiel and announcements by NBA video game veteran Tim Kitzrow. Players featured in the game include notable names such as Kevin Garnett, LeBron James, Kobe Bryant, Dwyane Wade, and Dwight Howard, making it a collectible item for both basketball and pinball enthusiasts​​.

name: NBA Fastbreak
desc:
NBA Fastbreak is a pinball machine released in 1997 by Williams Electronics (under its Bally label).
Designed by George Gomez, the game casts the player in the role of one of the NBA's then-29 teams, playing off against another on the court. The ultimate goal is to complete six tasks (ranging from activating every multiball to merely scoring 20 points) to win a trophy, then engage in Trophy Multiball for a shot at winning a championship ring for your team. Unsurprisingly, getting to this point heavily revolves around a plastic facsimile of a basketball hoop on the playfield. The player can shoot the ball into it from a ramp or pass it to one of four holes surrounding it (though they need to contend with a defensive player aiming to block the shot). Other features of note include a flipper, ball, and basket contained within the backglass (which can be used to rack up quite a few points when activated), high scores that are divided by teams, and the ability to link two machines together for a unique timed multiplayer mode.

id: New Wave (Bell Games 1985)/New Wave (Bell Games 1985) v2.0.0.vpx
name: New Wave (Bell Games 1985)
desc:
New Wave was a conversion kit done by Bell Games in 1985; utilizing a full reuse of Black Pyramid.  Since I just finished Black Pyramid, it was very straightforward to use that as a baseline for the New Wave conversion kit.

@redbone spent a lot of time getting the playfield, plastics, bumpers, targets, and other images just right.  He was able to utilize some prior work that  @cyberpez did as well.  I've included TONS of options in there, as it was a kit, and it appears that lots of different items could be installed.  Also Cyberpez requested I add some options he was working on years ago.  So, there are alternate plastics, bumpers, flippers, targets, rollovers, rollover lights, led edge lighting, and lots of ball choices... including a few glowballs.   All changeable in the F12 menu.  I was also able to reuse some work that was done on the cabinet for VR and the backglass.  I think Devious626 did lots of that work in the past.  And hauntfreaks did some effort in the past on the backglass.  Those images have been incorporated as well.

I implemented the latest VPW standards for physics, GI VLM, 3D inserts, AllLamps routines, shadows, updated backglass for desktop, roth drop and standup targets, a swinging target, standalone compatibility, sling corrections, default and optional DIP adjustments, updated flipper physics, VR and fully hybrid, Flupper style bumpers and lighting.  Redbone also updated the plastics, target images, and bumpers.  Lots of hours were spent studying gameplay videos to match the table skill shots and physics action.

There are options included in this table via the F12 menu including colors for balls, flippers, screws, LED plastics, rollovers and lights, bumpers, plastics, and brightness of bumpers when off and when lit.  There are also multiple VR room environments and other VR options all done via the F12 menu.  You can also change the ROM sound volume in the F12 menu.  (Note if you want to change the ROM volume, you'll need to restart the table after the change.).
Please NOTE on the ROM settings:  The default settings for the ROM options are hard coded into the script and are based on the recommended values from Bally for 3 balls.  If you want to change the ROM settings themselves, you need to change the "SetDIPSwitches to 1" in the script, and then use the F6 menu to change.

Also NOTE:  Just like Black Pyramid, Bally recommends to ensure that the self-test position settings for the ROM menu items for 16,17,18,19 are set to "03".  Here is the procedure to do this.  I've included the nvram in the zip file as well, so if you want to bypass that step and use it instead.

Here is the procedure to set the self-test positions on this Bally 35 MPU table:

1. Press 7 to enter test mode. Continue to repeatedly press 7 until you see 01 appear in the ball in play/match display
2. Press and HOLD the 1 key until it reaches the value you want to set it to (start with 16). The value will increase by 1 while you are holding in the 1 key. If you happen to go past the value you want to set it to, while holding in the 1 key press and release the 7 key. The value will then decrement by 1 while you are holding in the 1 key. When you reach the value you want, release the 1 key.  Set the value to 03.
3.  Repeat pressing 7 to scroll the remainder of the settings (17,18,19) and change values to 03 in the similar manner.
4.  Press F3 to save your changes and reset the table.

name: New York (Gottlieb 1976)
desc:
Gottlieb's New York pinball table is a 2-player add-a-ball variant of the popular Spirit of '76 (1975), released to commemorate the legalization of pinball in NYC following Roger Sharpe's famous demonstration.

Designed by Wayne Neyens, the game features high-contrast artwork highlighting American pioneers and astronaut figures, reflecting the US Bicentennial celebration. The playfield features drop targets (1776/1976) and a central saucer, offering a challenging, slow-paced EM (electromechanical) game.

While Spirit of '76 had a massive production run of over 10,000 units, New York is a much rarer variant, with only 300 units produced.

name: Night Moves
desc:
Night moves is one of 2 cocktail machines made by International Concepts, as part of a re-emergence of cocktail pinball in the late 80's.
The machine was designed and produced by Premier/Gottlieb, but sold under the International Concepts brand. The boards are System 80B and all under playfield parts are Gottlieb parts.

name: Night Rider
desc: The Night Rider pinball table, released by Bally in 1976, is notable for its era-typical design that focuses on hitting targets and spinners. It's recommended to be played in 5-ball mode, where the spinners and bumper points alternate, adding a layer of strategy to the game. Scoring the upper kicker hole while lit doubles the bonus, making bonus scoring a critical part of gameplay. The table was one of the cross-over tables where both electromechanical (EM) and solid-state (SS) versions were made. The digital recreation of Night Rider has seen enhancements in lights, scripting, table physics, and added features like nFozzy flippers, GI lighting, flippers shadows, ball shadows, and corrected mechanical sounds. A significant update in the version 2.0a addressed a ball launch issue and improved various physical elements and lighting on the table​​​​.

id: Nightmare Before Christmas (Original)/Nightmare Before Christmas(2024) v1.02_Tuga.vpx
name: Nightmare Before Christmas (2024)
desc: Nightmare Before Christmas is a fan-made digital pinball table inspired by Tim Burton's classic film. Featuring fast-paced gameplay, multiball modes, and atmospheric visuals, it captures the spooky charm of Halloween Town with vibrant animations, themed sounds, and a layout designed for thrilling combos and flow.

name: Nineball
desc: "Nine Ball" is a classic pinball game from Stern released in 1980, renowned for its angular and challenging gameplay, balanced rules, and multiple scoring strategies. As a digital version, it's available for Visual Pinball, a platform that allows pinball enthusiasts to play simulated versions of real pinball tables on their computers. The Visual Pinball version of "Nine Ball" includes options for different playing environments, such as VR rooms and cabinet modes, with settings for desktop play being the default. Additionally, it supports modifications like dynamic shadows and two VR environments to enhance the gameplay experience, ensuring that players can adjust the game according to their performance preferences and setup​​.

id: Nitro Ground Shaker 1980 (Bally)/Nitro Ground Shaker (Bally 1980) JP v6.0.0 DT-FS-VR-MR Ext2k Conversion.vpx
name: Nitro Ground Shaker
desc: The "Nitro Ground Shaker" is a pinball machine produced by Bally Manufacturing Co. in January 1980, with the original project design dating back to May 12, 1978. It stands out for its classic bottom-arch featuring a large BALLY logo in early-production games, later switching to a new-style 'Pinball-Division' design. The game was designed by George Christian, with software by Rehman Merchant and artwork by Dave Christensen. As a solid state machine from the Bally MPU AS-2518-35 generation, it boasts a production of 7,950 units. The game accommodates up to 4 players, features 2 flippers, but no ramps or multiball. Its cabinet is of a normal size, with a digital display​​.

name: No Fear (Williams 1995)
desc: The "No Fear: Dangerous Sports" pinball machine, released by Williams in 1995, themed around extreme sports, in collaboration with the No Fear clothing brand. This game features a range of adrenaline-pumping sports, including skydiving, free climbing, water skiing, and car racing.

name: No Good Gofers
desc:
The game revolves around Buzz and Bud, two gophers who are wreaking havoc on any and all golfers playing on their "turf". The gofers "pop-up" during gameplay to taunt the player, as well as provide entry ways to locks.
No Good Gofers also has a "slam-ramp" feature which if used correctly, will award the player a "hole-in-one" shot. Performing this is tricky, as the ball must travel off the ramp, into the air, and into a very small hole located on the game's upper playfield. The "hole-in-one" shot is often called one of the greatest shots in pinball history.
The game uses the DCS Sound System.

name: Nugent (Stern 1978)
desc:
There is a rollover button at the top that lights the left and right top lanes for 9k points. Smoking the spinner adds to the bonus and getting the ball in the saucer collects the bonus. This game uses the same code as Stern's Lectronamo, which is genuinely my favourite game.
Nugent is a pinball machine from November 1978, manufactured by Stern Electronics, Inc.

id: Oba Oba (Taito do Brasil - 1979)/Oba Oba (Taito do Brasil - 1979) v600.vpx
name: Oba Oba (Taito do Brasil - 1979)
desc:
The Oba Oba pinball machine, released in June 1979 by Taito do Brasil, is a solid-state table and a prominent example of the "cloning" era in Brazilian pinball history.

The playfield layout is nearly identical to Playboy, featuring 2 flippers, 5 drop targets, and 3 pop bumpers. While the rules and sounds are largely the same as the original, Oba Oba uses a standard rollover switch in the extra ball lane instead of the star rollover found on Playboy.

The artwork was completely reimagined. Instead of the Playboy brand, it is themed after the Oba Oba playhouse, a famous nightclub in Rio de Janeiro.

desc: "Odin Deluxe," released by Segasa under the Sonic brand in 1985, is a solid-state pinball machine with a Norse mythology theme. The game accommodates up to four players and features two flippers, three pop bumpers, and five drop targets, providing engaging gameplay. Notably, "Odin Deluxe" is a rebranded version of the Spanish manufacturer Peyper's "Odin" pinball machine, with differences primarily in the backglass artwork, pop bumper cap images, and drop target colors.

name: Odisea Paris-Dakar (Peyper 1987)
desc: Odisea Paris-Dakar is a solid-state pinball machine released by the Spanish manufacturer Peyper in 1987. The game draws inspiration from the renowned Paris-Dakar Rally, featuring thematic artwork and playfield elements that reflect the adventurous spirit of the race. The playfield is equipped with two flippers, three pop bumpers, and two slingshots.

name: Olympics (Chicago Coin 1975)
desc: "Olympics" and "Super Star" are electro-mechanical pinball machines released by Chicago Coin. Both games share a sports theme, with "Super Star" accommodating up to four players and "Olympics" designed for two players. The playfields feature two flippers, three pop bumpers, two slingshots, two standup targets, and two spinning targets.

name: Olympus (Juegos Populares 1986)
desc: Olympus is a Spanish solid-state pinball machine manufactured by Juegos Populares. It is themed around the Greek Pantheon, featuring artwork of Olympian gods and mythological figures across its backglass and playfield.

name: Operation Thunder
desc:
Operation: Thunder is a Physical Pinball Table released by Gottlieb (under the "Premier" label) in 1992. Developed by Ray Tanzer with artwork by David Moore and Constantino and Jeanine Mitchell, it was Gottlieb's last game to use an alphanumeric score display.
The game puts the player in charge of a squadron of F-15 Eagles and Stealth Fighters, waging an unyielding air attack on the enemy such as destroying radar installations, strafing tank columns, and attacking the domed power plant. Light up the mountainous terrain with a barrage of bombs and missiles, but make sure you don't run out of fuel lest you crash and burn. Only the best pilots will make it through all eleven missions, and those who survive the Final Assault will be rewarded with a hero's welcome and a well-earned promotion.

name: Panthera (Gottlieb 1980) v600
desc: "Panthera" is a pinball machine released by D. Gottlieb & Co. in June 1980. It features a solid-state design with two flippers, no ramps, and no multiball mode. The game is part of the Gottlieb System 80 series. A total of 5,220 units were produced.

id: Papa Smurf 2015 (Original)/Papa Smurf v4 by JP.vpx
name: Papa Smurf
desc:
JP's Papa Smurf, a digital pinball table from 2015, is a homage to the beloved Smurfs, particularly Papa Smurf. This table was designed for Visual Pinball X (VPX), showcasing several technological advancements in the platform. The table is an electromechanical (EM) simulation based on the 1976 Surfer pinball table by Gottlieb. It features a variety of new objects and mechanics available in VP10, such as bumpers, rubber objects, new lighting effects, bulb lights, transparent walls, and a cool rotating ball mechanism​​.
The table has been updated several times since its initial release, with version 4.0.2 bringing enhancements like extra Direct Output Framework (DOF) commands and directb2s commands to work with BorgDog's db2s, among other fixes and improvements. These updates have focused on refining gameplay and integrating modern pinball table features, including music by Father Abraham & the Smurfs (which can be disabled), improved physics, scripting techniques, and UltraDMD support for a dynamic display experience​​​​.

name: Paragon
desc:
Paragon is a Physical Pinball Table released by Bally in 1979. It was designed by Greg Kmiec, and features artwork by Paul Faris.
The game is set in Paragon, a Heroic Fantasy world of muscular Barbarian Heroes, maidens wearing Chainmail Bikinis, lush landscapes, and Everything Trying to Kill You. In his quest for a high score, the player must scale the Golden Cliffs, ride the Waterfall, and fight through the Valley of Demons to the Treasure Chamber beyond. Climb Paragon Tower to reach the saucer above, but beware of the Beast's Lair, where death is but a hair's breath away.

name: Party Zone
desc:
The Party Zone is a pinball table designed by Dennis Nordman, with artwork by Greg Freres and music and sound effects by Dan Forden. It was released in 1991 by Williams Electronics under the Bally label.
The Party Zone is centered on an interdimensional party under the watchful eyes of the wildly enigmatic Captain B. Zarr. Win the Door Prize, enter the Dance Contest with the Dancing Dummy, shoot the Rocket Ramp for the Ozone Bonus, and make sure to Eat, Drink, & B. Merry. Start up the Super Sonic Robotic Comic for a Laff Attack, and don't hesitate to Make a Request from the DJ. After all that, get the Party Animals, Party Monsters, and Party Dudes into the Cosmic Cottage, then start Happy Hour Multiball and try to collect enough Rock-It Fuel for the Big Bang jackpot — or get booted into the End Zone and out of the Party.

name: Pharaoh
desc:
Who DARES to enter the tomb of the mighty Pharaoh.
The Pharaoh pinball machine, created by Williams in 1981, is celebrated for being part of a unique group of double playfield machines, a design approach that was particularly innovative at the time. Other notable machines in this category include Black Knight, Jungle Lord, and Solar Fire. Pharaoh distinguishes itself with features like magna saves, an abundance of drop targets, and challenging shots like the captive ball and various "tombs" to aim for. This design complexity is meant to provide an engaging and challenging experience for players, encouraging strategic gameplay to navigate its richly themed Egyptian playfield.
A significant aspect of Pharaoh is its use of speech, making it the last two-level game from Williams to incorporate this feature. The machine has a range of phrases for different moments in the game, from inviting players to "enter the tomb of the mighty PHARAOH" to reactions like "Beware of cobras!" upon certain actions or achievements within the game. These audio snippets add a layer of immersion and personality to the game, enhancing the overall experience.
The playfield itself is a mirror image of Black Knight's layout, with the unique twist of the upper playfield being larger than the lower one, a rare choice among two-level games. This design choice impacts gameplay strategy, especially in how players aim to keep the ball in play on the different levels of the machine. Features like magna-saves allow players to save the ball from draining, adding a strategic resource management aspect to the game. The game's detailed design, from its thematic elements to its mechanical intricacies, makes it a noteworthy piece of pinball history​​​​.

name: Phoenix
desc: The "Phoenix" pinball machine, produced by Williams Electronic Games, Inc. in November 1978, is a solid-state type with a normal cabinet and digital display. It accommodates up to 4 players, featuring 2 flippers but no ramps or multiball option. The game was designed by Barry Oursler, with artwork by Constantino and Jeanine Mitchell, and sound and software by Paul Dussault. Approximately 6,198 units were produced​​.

name: Pinball (Stern 1977)
desc: The game concept comes from a Chicago Coin advertisement from the mid 70's with the ball coming down a big city street. It features four players and saves high scores to date!

name: Pinball Magic
desc:
Pinball Magic is a 1995 arcade pinball game, the first table from Capcom's pinball division. It was designed by Bryan Hansen and Rob Hurtado, with art by Hugh Van Zanten and Jeff Busch.
In Pinball Magic, the player is an aspiring magician who must prove his skills before a group of seven famous mystics, all under the leadership of the mysterious Matra Magna. As she waves her wand over the playfield, impress the Masters by performing the linking rings, transforming beasts in the Morph Chamber, riding the magic carpet, escaping from a locked trunk, and numerous other acts. When it's time, take the Stage and Silence the Critics by levitating the pinball. If you manage to complete all three rounds of the magicians' trials, you might discover the secret of Matra Magna's eternal youth...

name: Pinball Pool
desc:
The "Pinball Pool" pinball machine, manufactured by Gottlieb in June 1979, is a solid-state device known for its engaging gameplay and classic design. With artwork by Gordon Morison and game design by Ed Krynski, this machine was part of the Gottlieb System 1 generation. A notable feature of this game is its unique drop target mechanism: hitting a drop target on one side causes the corresponding target on the opposite side to drop as well, adding a strategic element to the gameplay. This feature varies with the number of balls in play, with all drop targets responding in 3-ball play, while only the even-numbered ones do so in 5-ball play.
The digital recreation of "Pinball Pool" has seen considerable updates, enhancing its visual and gameplay elements. These updates include new lighting and table physics, reworked images cleaned and upscaled, added flipper and ball shadows, improved mechanical sounds, and tuned slingshots and bumpers force. The digital version offers three gameplay scripts based on the number of balls in play, ranging from easy to hard, catering to different skill levels and preferences.
"Pinball Pool" enjoys a place in pinball history for its straightforward yet captivating gameplay mechanics, including shooting drop targets, clearing A-B-C sequences, and utilizing kick holes to increase bonuses. The game was produced in a quantity of 7,200 units and has an estimated value of $1660 - $1940, reflecting its collectible status among pinball enthusiasts​​​​​​.
Featuring Gottlieb’s innovative “Remotrip” drop targets, this pool themed pinball would make a fantastic addition to any games room.

name: Pinbot
desc:
The Pinbot pinball machine, produced by Williams in October 1986, is a celebrated example of classic pinball design, brought to life by the creative minds of Barry Oursler and Python Anghelo, among others. This game was notable for being the first to credit its entire development team, a decision driven by Python Anghelo. The machine features two flippers, three pop bumpers, a five-target dropping bank, a 3-bank drop targets, and three kick-out holes. A unique element is its opening skill shot that propels the ball up a conical ramp, leading to a playfield adorned with a vibrant array of lights that track the player's progress in hitting targets. When a player hits a dropping bank of 5 standup targets, it reveals two kick-out holes, adding to the challenge and excitement. Additionally, the game has an upper-level bagatelle mini-playfield and offers a 2-ball multiball feature. The game runs on the Williams System 11A MPU and includes a flashing light topper bar, although this feature was often removed or disabled by operators. The voice of Pin•Bot was provided by Barry Oursler​​.
The primary goal in Pin-Bot is to progress through the planets of the Solar System, starting from Pluto and aiming to reach the Sun. Players advance by hitting specially marked targets, earning bonuses along the way. A central grid of lights, situated just below the Pin•Bot, can be filled by hitting targets, leading to the opening of the visor and the chance to lock two balls in the robot's eye sockets. This action triggers a two-ball multiball mode. Additionally, there's a spiral ramp for skill shots and a bagatelle-style mini-playfield, enhancing the gameplay's complexity and appeal​​.

id: Pink Panther 1981 (Gottleb)/Pink Panther (Gottlieb 1981) Sound MOD v3.0.vpx
name: Pink Panther
desc:
Pink Panther is a pinball game based on the popular comedy film series and cartoon character. It was designed by John Buras, illustrated by Jerry Simkus, and released by Gottlieb in 1981.
The game's premise is a very loose adaptation of The Return of the Pink Panther; the Panther is pursuing an attractive female jewel thief through a dimly-lit mansion as she pilfers its collection of gems. Get the black diamonds to enable the Secret Passage, then light the flashlight and enter the Hidden Staircase. Lock two pinballs to explore them, then start three-ball multiball for a frantic chase to collect the blue diamonds scattered around the playfield. Players who can collect the most diamonds are rewarded with a free game.
Pink Panther is noteworthy for being Gottlieb's first multi-ball pinball game.

name: Pirate Gold
desc: "Pirate Gold" is a pinball machine manufactured by Chicago Coin in 1969. This table features artwork by Christian Marche, showcasing awesome designs that contribute to the overall pirate-themed aesthetic of the game. It includes distinctive play features such as a horseshoe lane and two-inch flippers. The restoration and artwork for the Visual Pinball X (VPX) version of "Pirate Gold" were derived from an actual machine that was saved from being scrapped, fully restored, and then digitized, indicating a meticulous process to preserve the game's original charm in a virtual format​​.

name: Pirates Life (Original)
desc: Pirates Life - The Revenge of Cecil Hoggleston is an original, story-driven pinball table. Set in a richly imagined pirate universe, it follows the journey of young Cecil Hoggleston as he transforms into a fearsome pirate captain. The table features immersive visuals, pirate-themed voiceovers, and dynamic gameplay with eight unique modes, including ship battles, sea monster encounters, and treasure hunts. Designed as a hybrid experience, it supports desktop, cabinet, and full VR play, offering players a deeply interactive and cinematic pinball adventure.

id: Pirates Of The Caribbien 2006 (Stern Pinball)/Pirates of the Caribbean (Stern 2006)_Bigus(MOD)1.1.vpx
name: Pirates Of The Caribbean
desc:
Pirates of the Caribbean is an arcade pinball game designed by Dennis Nordman and illustrated by Kevin O'Connor. It was released in 2006 by Stern Pinball, coinciding with the release of the second Pirates of the Caribbean movie, Dead Man's Chest.
The game puts the player in the boots of Captain Jack Sparrow as he stumbles through various misadventures. Engage in sword fights, fire on Port Royal, collect your pirates, then play Liar's Dice and assemble a crew of 100 souls. Prove your mettle by shooting the pirate ship on the playfield and sinking it, then Fight Davy Jones, Destroy the Kraken, and use the Key to open the Dead Man's Chest. Along the way, you'll Catch the Wind and collect various bits of Treasure, but only the Pirate King will be able to complete the eight tasks and four points of the Compass to invoke Four Winds Multiball and come out on top of the Gauntlet of Pirates.

id: Pistol Poker (Alvin G. and Company 1993)/Pistol Poker (Alvin G. and Company 1993)_V1.3.vpx
name: Pistol Poker (Alvin G. and Company 1993)_V1.3
desc: Pistol Poker is a solid-state pinball machine with a unique Western and gambling theme. It combines traditional pinball mechanics with elements of poker, where players aim to create the best poker hand using the backglass display. It features three flippers, a ramp, and multiball functionality.

name: Playboy (Bally 1978)
desc: In 1978, Bally released the first Playboy pinball machine. According to Pinside, this particular pinball has a production run of 18.250, making it the #4 most successful Flipper-Game of all time. The start-up and bonus score countdown music for the Playboy pinball machine is similar to the “Playboy's Theme” from the 1969 “Playboy After Dark” television show. This game's artwork was created by Paul Faris and the backglass features an illustration of Hugh Hefner with Playmates Patti McGuire and Sondra Theodore. Special Features on the Flyer: 5 Playboy Keys They open the door to specials, bonuses and giant Grotto scores. New Playmate Targets Hit all 5 and win specials, bonus advances, extra balls, games. Action Drop Targets Key to 25,000 outlane score when all are down. New Playboy Grotto Unique kickback lane advances bonus up to 30,000 depending on the number of Keys lit. New Memory Super Bonus Once a 20,000 bonus score is achieved, 20,000 points are recalled and added with every ball.

name: Playboy (Stern 2002)
desc: "Visual Pinball - Playboy" from 2002 is a digital pinball simulation featuring a Playboy theme. It incorporates the Playboy brand, known for its adult entertainment magazine founded by Hugh Hefner. The game's visual elements likely include iconic Playboy imagery such as the Playboy bunny logo, images of Playboy models, and other related graphics that evoke the luxury and sensuality associated with the brand. The gameplay mechanics follow traditional pinball rules, where players control flippers to keep a ball in play on the table, aiming to hit various targets and rack up points. Given the Playboy theme, the table and its components are probably designed with a lavish, adult-oriented aesthetic, possibly including digital representations of photoshoots, parties, and other aspects typical of the Playboy lifestyle. The game is part of the larger Visual Pinball community project, which allows users to create and play custom pinball simulations on their computers, combining realistic physics with imaginative table designs.

id: Playboy 35th Anniversary (Data East 1989)/Playboy 35th Anniversary (Data East 1989) Physics Sound Hybrid MOD 1.1.vpx
name: Playboy 35th Anniversary (Data East 1989)
desc:
Playboy 35th Anniversary is a pinball machine released by Data East in 1989. It was designed by Joe Kaminkow and Ed Cebula, with artwork by Kevin O'Connor.

This game commemorates the 35th anniversary of Playboy magazine with a poolside party at Hugh Hefner's Playboy mansion. Shoot up the ramps to enter the Mansion, then play with the animals in the Mansion Zoo for a score multiplier. When you're ready, head on over to the pool patio, where you can take the 35th anniversary playmates to the Photo Shoot and earn a Special. While 1989 Playmate of the Year Kimberley Conrad watches from the playfield, lock two balls into the Grotto for multiball, and try to shoot the ramps for the Jackpot.

name: Pokemon Pinball
desc:
JP's Pokémon Pinball, released in 2016, is an original Visual Pinball X table inspired by the world of Pokémon. The layout of this table is designed to resemble that of Stern's Kiss table. Players aim to achieve high scores primarily through catching Pokémon and hatching eggs, activities that offer the highest points. The game is enriched with various extra modes, including multiballs, combos, jackpots, and coins to upgrade your ball, adding depth and excitement to the gameplay. This version also includes FlexDMD code for cabinet play and has been updated to include JP's latest physics for an enhanced playing experience​​.
Additionally, a distinct but related table, inspired by Pokémon Pinball for the Gameboy and drawing elements from Pokémon Pinball Ruby and Pokémon Red & Blue, focuses on capturing the nostalgia of the original games. Players embark on adventures similar to the core Pokémon series, including catching Pokémon, battling trainers, and winning gym badges. This table, however, opts for a more traditional pinball experience by excluding multiball features to maintain the nostalgic feel of the original Pokémon Pinball Gameboy game. The gameplay involves more than 1100 custom DMD images, extensive scripting, and a variety of interactive 3D Pokémon models to engage players in the Pokémon-catching experience​​.

name: PokemonDungeonv3-FleepNfozzy

This is a re-theme MOD of JP Salas’ original Pokémon table, inspired by Pokémon Mystery Dungeon.
The core table layout and some gameplay elements remain the same, but the presentation has been reworked to better fit the Mystery Dungeon style.

name: Polar Explorer (Taito 1983) v600
desc: Polar Explorer is a solid-state pinball machine designed for up to four players. The game features an arctic exploration theme, challenging players to navigate treacherous ice and snow. Its playfield design is similar to Zaccaria's "Pinball Champ" from the same year.

name: Pole Position (Sonic 1987)
desc: Pole Position is a solid state pinball table. It is unrelated to the popular arcade Namco game of the same name.

name: Police Force
desc:
Police Force is a 1989 arcade pinball machine from Williams Electronics. It was designed by Barry Oursler and Mark Ritchie, with art by Python Anghelo and John Youssi.
In a World of Funny Animals, a Bank Robbery is underway at the First Animal Bank, and it's up to the player to stop the wrongdoers. Hit the Drug Rat, Diamond Weasel, Machine-Gun Croc, and Loan Shark targets to put them in jail, then shoot the right ramp and bring down the Mafiosaurus Rex for the Jackpot. Spell POLICE to light the Bullseye for the Top Cop bonus, then load up the Patrol Car and roll it out to start multiball. Use your sharpshooting skills to repeatedly hit the center ramp for Unlimited Millions, or be a Cowboy Cop and Take the Highest Score from the other players.

name: Pool Sharks (Midway 1990) v600
desc: This solid-state table features a billiards theme and includes two flippers, three pop bumpers, multiple drop targets, and a unique 8-ball or 9-ball game option.

id: Popeye Saves The Earth 1994 (Bally)/Popeye Saves the Earth (Bally 1994) v1.25.vpx
name: Popeye Saves the Earth
desc:
Popeye Saves the Earth is a Physical Pinball Table designed by Barry Oursler and themed and illustrated by Python Anghelo, with additional artwork by John Youssi and Pat McMahon. It was released by Williams Electronics under the "Bally" label in 1994.
As is evident from the title, this is a game based on the long-running Popeye comic strip. Popeye's long-time nemesis Bluto is now a planet-polluting profiteer; his companies' toxic activities have endangered five species of wildlife, while Bluto himself has kidnapped Olive Oyl, and Swee'pea has gotten lost in a maze of corridors. It therefore falls on Popeye to rescue the endangered animals, find Swee'Pea, defeat the Sea Hag, and demolish Bluto's cartel of corrupt companies. Only then can Popeye find his spinach and Rescue Olive in a six-ball multiball frenzy.

name: Primordial Quarry
desc:
You’re our last hope to restore humanity. You’ve been sent to an alien planet far from Earth that’s rich in magical resources powerful enough to revitalize our dying farms, dwindling fuel, diminishing health, and withering economy. Extract rare crystals with miraculous properties from deep in the extraterrestrial mines and ship them back home. You may never see a sunny day again, but with enough hard work in the mines, everyone back home just might.

FREE TO PLAY. Just launch the ball.

This one took me awhile to finish! A 100% original table by me. I designed the layout, wrote the rules, scripted the code, modeled the primitives, and composed and performed the music. The art was mostly created with Co-Pilot, then collaged together by me. I tried to keep the grittier sci-fi elements of my Raygun Runner table that people liked but add a little bit more of the whimsy and magic that I like.

[TO PLAY THE RAR FILES, DOWNLOAD ALL TO ONE FOLDER AND EXTRACT PART1 WITH WINRAR, THAT SHOULD AUTOMATICALLY COMBINE THE REST]

OBJECTIVE:

Complete six major work tasks to deplete the mine, then drill at a new location to find new resources. Meanwhile, select which of the six supernatural minerals to mine and try to fill orders.

-----WORK: (6 Work quests. Only one can be played at a time. Once one is complete, it is unavailable until you complete all six)

EXCAVATE:

Shoot the left or right orbit five times to start Excavate Work. This will light the captive ball on the upper playfield. Access it via the Expedition Ramp, then shoot the captive ball to ignite the explosives. This will drop a load of rubble on the worksite. Shoot the Stone Crusher machinery in the orbit to clear it away and complete the Work.

SMELT:

Mined resources must be melted down into ingots. Shoot the SMELT ramp five times to start Smelt Work to smelt minerals down for processing. Once the smelting furnace is ready, travel down to the lower playfield via the Expedition Ramp. Then turn the red valve to increase the heat until the molten pit on the right is lit. Shoot the pit to complete the Work.

HAUL:

Much of mining is moving minerals around, both valuable gems and useless rocks. Shoot the HAUL ramp five times to begin Haul Work. This will light one of three ramps randomly. Shoot this track to haul minerals out of the mine. You will see the mine cart on the plunger lane move forward. Shoot the wrong track and the minecart will fall back a bit. Get it to the Headquarters building to complete Haul Work.

PROCESS:

These minerals have to be refined to a usable state. Shoot the PROCESS ramp five times to begin Process Work. Two control panel drop targets will appear. One on the main playfield, and one underground. Shoot both to light one ramp each. Shoot both ramps, then the Smelt ramp to complete Process Work.

EXTRACT:

To get the good stuff, you have to drill deeper. Shoot the drill in the center loop to start Extract Work. This will activate the stone cutter on the upper playfield. Shoot the violet ore six times to carve precious metals from the caverns. While this mode is active, you can shoot the drill again to raise your Gem Cut Value, which is awarded upon completing Extract Work.

EXPEDITION:

On top of mining, you must also explore the alien planet for new mining locations. Shoot the EXPEDITION ramp five times to begin the search. This will light the crane above the Haul ramp. Shoot it accurately and the crane will snatch your ball. Shoot the crane again with a new ball to dislodge it and begin Expedition Multiball. Now shoot all green lit shots without losing a ball, and then shoot the Headquarters on the far right OR the hidden kicker via the Expedition Ramp for the final jackpot that completes Expedition Work.

-----MINERALS: (6 Minerals to mine. Only one can be played at a time. Shoot the Headquarters building on the far right to select your mineral with the flippers and plunger key. This mode will stay active indefinitely until you switch to a new mineral. There are no time limits when mining.)

SANGUINE QUARTZ:

A mystical red gem that can heal human disease and injury. Three quartz veins will appear on wire return ramps. Smash all three to locate the big red quartz crystal on the right orbit. Hit the Excavation Hammer to mine one piece of Sanguine Quartz. (Award: Mine four or more to increase your chances of having your ball randomly saved.)

PYROCLAX:

A rare volcanic stone that seems to have almost unlimited combustion power for fuel. Shoot the volcano on the left orbit to flood the mine with lava. When it cools, Pyroclax will appear beneath the drill. Shoot the drill loop to extract it, then the Smelt ramp to mine one Pyroclax. (Award: Mine four or more to unlock a radar dish bonus round and increase its value.)

STARDUST TOPAZ:

A celestial crystal that seems to grant incredibly good fortune to those who possess it. Shoot the three left ramps to find Stardust Topaz. It will appear on the upper playfield. Smash five pieces with the ball to collect one Stardust Topaz. You will have to alternate shooting ramps and shooting crystals. (Award: Mine four or more to increase the value of filling mineral orders.)

PRIMORDIAL MUD:

The namesake of the mine, this planet is famous for its radioactive primordial goo. But far from deadly, this ooze has been shown to spawn growth in plants even in the harshest conditions. This could save the agricultural crisis! Shoot the hidden cave in the right orbit to locate pools of primordial mud around the mine. Roll over all three to collect one piece of Primordial Mud. (Award: Mine four or more to permanently increase the value of the ramps.)

ETERNOULINE:

Perfect for building machines, homes, and even human armor, Eternouline is 100% indestructible. But mining it is tricky. Descend into the lower playfield to turn the blue water valve. This will release the flood gates and fill the mine with water. When it drains, Eternouline is left to be retrieved. Hit both flipper bumpers to grab the crystals, then shoot the Process ramp to mine one Eternouline. (Award: Mine four or more to increase your multiball jackpot.)

PHANTAMATHYST:

The most valuable of all the crystals, Phantamathyst has unknowable, almost god-like powers. Who knows what miracles can be achieved with this amazing stone? Shoot the moving purple shards above the three left ramps to try to snag one. Catch four shards and the Fusion Machine will appear by the drill. Shoot your ball into this narrow shot to fuse the four shards together and mine one Phantamathyst. (Award: Mine four or more to increase the value of the Work completion bonus round and the Video Mode.)

-----MINOR FEATURES:

Orders: Shoot the right kicker in the lower playfield to light the order. Now shoot the kicker in the right of the upper playfield to obtain your Order Requisition. The "Balls Left" reel will show you what minerals are requested back on Earth. Usually it will be 1-3 of a 1-2 minerals. As you mine these minerals, lights will appear in the lower left of the table showing how much is available. When you have enough to fill the order, shoot the Order kicker again to send them to Earth. You do not have to fill orders if you don't want to, but they're worth big points and give you a mineral to aim for!

Mountain Multiball: Every time you complete Work, you can lock one ball on the right orbit. Lock three on the three primordial peaks to start Mountain Multiball. Then shoot the orbit for jackpots.

Video Mode: Every time you mine a mineral, video mode will be lit in the lower playfield. Use the plunger key to mine stones but avoid bombs.

Damaged Machinery: Shooting the right orbit runs the risk of colliding with the rotating fan blade. If you do, your mining machinery is damaged, but don’t worry! Malfunctions often lead to improved efficiency. Shoot the haywire grinder in the lower playfield to restore its function, then shoot the captive ball to reboot the system in safe mode. This will increase the value of completing Work and Mining.

Treasure Trove: Every five million points, the violet ore on the upper playfield will begin to flash rainbow color. Shoot it to find a secret treasure trove and earn a random award.

Multiplier Minigame: When you shoot the Expedition Ramp, before entering the lower playfield, you have a brief bonus chance to shoot the moving target. Every shot gives you rare Rainbow Crystal and increases your multiplier (up to 10).

name: Pro Pool (Gottlieb 1973)
desc:
An electro-mechanical game features a billiards theme, challenging players with two sets of seven drop targets that represent the solids and stripes in pool, along with a critical eight ball target. This game was exported to Italy as Gottlieb's 1972 'Play Pool'.

The replay versions of this game are the 2-player Gottlieb's 1974 'Big Shot' and the 4-player Gottlieb's 1973 'Hot Shot'.

name: Pulp Fiction
desc:
Pulp Fiction is a retro-inspired full-featured modern pinball machine. Developed at the request of Quentin Tarantino who wanted an 1980’s style Pulp Fiction themed pinball machine for his home. Tarantino’s continued involvement throughout the project shaped the final game. Tarantino rarely licenses his intellectual property, it is a unique privilege to produce a game which pays tribute to this masterpiece.
Pinball designer Mark Ritchie masterfully crafted a playfield which on its surface appears comparable to games from this era but outside of initial perception features more mechanisms and greater depth than most games produced today. David Thiel forcefully pulls the player into this world utilizing over 250 iconic lines from Pulp Fiction’s legendary cast, five licensed songs from the original movie soundtrack, and a number of original compositions. Josh Sharpe developed an approachable rule set that is both intuitive and deep enough to engage even the most skilled player.
o 250+ Iconic Lines of Pulp Fiction Dialogue Featuring 19 Movie Characters
o 5 Licensed Songs from the Pulp Fiction Soundtrack – Comanche, Jungle Boogie, Misirlou, Son of a Preacher Man & You Never Can Tell
o Mirrored Backglass with Custom Hand-Drawn Artwork from Pulp Fiction’s Legendary Jack Rabbit Slim’s Dance Scene
o RGB LED General Illumination Lighting, 15 RGB LED Featured Inserts, RGB LED Lower Arch Lighting
o Vintage Stainless Steel Coin Door with LED Pulp Fiction Logo & Start Button on Door (Non-Coin Operated Models ONLY)
o 4 Memory Drop Targets, 3 Drop Targets, Pawn Shop 3-Ball Subway Lock, Briefcase 3-Ball Lock; Knocker AssemblyHere is the last of the three tables started since January after Godzilla vs Kong, The Untouchables here is Pulp Fiction I think it's the most fun of the three. here it is over for me so have fun. have a nice weekend.

Today I go back to 1994, the release date of the cult film Pulp Fiction. I was inspired by the new Pulp Fiction pinball machine, which has some similarities to Stern's Bond 60 TH. Have fun. Many thanks to JPsalas for his help

name: Punchout (Original)
desc:
Are you ready to rumble?

There is a separate mediapack for the weels and other stuff. This table plays in 10.7 only you have to save it in 10.7 and then reopen it, but if you want to play VR then you need 10.8 version revision 1.

Last year Joe Picasso came to show the Punch-Out table to me, but people where already coding it. The table is based on a homebrew by Craig Evans. The project got on hold and i asked to look at it. I coded the table in 5 days and did 1 week bug solving. There is so much love in this table because of Joe Picasso, he wanted everything as authentic as possible regarding to the NES game. I think I redid the b2s 50 times and every time I thought I was finished with coding then Joe came with a new idea and I had to rewrite pretty much everything. But all the hard work paid off because its a super fun table to play.

First a round of thanks:
Oqqsan: Thank you for helping with the getup bugs we had and other bugs aswell.
Dardog: VR room
Flupper + Zandysarcade: 3d models
Outhere: DOF
JoePicasso: Design table,art,POV,keeping remdwaas1986 sane.
Remdwaas1986: Rules,coding,some art,3d modifications,3d animations.

RULES:
This is a 3 ball game(I know normally I only make 5 ball games), but like the real punchout game you have 3 chances to get up in each ball you play! After fight 3/7/11 you will get an extra ball.

You start at training level 0. To train for the fight, hit 4 times the reps scoop or 4 times the spar scoop to get a higher training level. After that you will get an extra ball and you have to hit the targets F-I-G-H-T N-I-G-H-T to get ready for the fight. Play then in the top scoop and the fight will start with a 3 ball multiball. Hit 8 times the knockout(KO) gate or 5 gut punches en 4 star gates(TKO) to win the fight. Every next fight will get harder because for every next fight you have to do an extra gut punch before you can start the KO or TKO sequence. After fight 11 the wizard point mode starts and the scoops/targets/inlanes will give 1 million points, the bumper 10k,the spinners 100k and the outlanes 2 million.

how many fights did you won?

name: Q*Bert's Quest
desc:
Q*Bert's Quest is a Pinball Spinoff of Gottlieb's popular Q*Bert video game. It was designed by John Trudeau and released in 1983.
Q*Bert's Quest is memorable for its unconventional playfield layout, dominated by a massive figure eight design and two pairs of cross-over flippers at the bottom. Just as in the arcade game, the player had to light up all of the surfaces on a pyramid of six cubes by hitting various rollovers and dropdown targets. As he does this, the enemies Coily, Ugg, and Wrong Way would advance towards the pyramid, resetting one of the cubes if they reach it. The player could hit the enemies' targets to make them retreat, and clearing six pyramids awarded a free game. Of course, Q*Bert would be jabbering away incomprehensibly during all of this.

id: Queen The Game Hits 1 (Original 2022)/Queen The Game Hits 1 (Original 2021) ReMod v1_4_1.vpx
name: Queen The Game Hits 1 (Original 2021)
desc:
This is my mod of Mark Paulik's table "Queen - The Game", which in turn is a mod of my own table Watchmen. All artwork and non-mechanical sound effects are by Mark Paulik. Moving post models, textures, and animation by Lumigado. My mod adds:
Music imported in the sound manager for lag free playback and hassle free installation
Cabinet support, including DOF
Optional FlexDMD (enable by changing line 22 of the script to const bUseFlexDMD = True )
Fleep's mechanical sounds
NFozzy physics
Playfield mesh for the center saucer
Other than that, it's Queen! A band so great one table cannot contain it. This download includes two versions, Hits 1 and Hits 2, with different artwork and song lists, but identical gameplay. Each table has a playlist of 21 songs, spread out over 15 modes, three wizard modes, and other features.

RULES
THE GAME: Hit the left drop targets to light The Game modes. Hit the center saucer to start The Game modes. During The Game modes, hit orange lights.
MAGIC: Hit the left ramp to light and start Magic modes. During Magic modes, hit white lights.
MIRACLE: Hit the spinner to light and start Miracle modes. During Miracle modes, hit purple lights.
OPERA: Hit the right ramp to light and start Opera modes. During Opera modes, hit yellow lights.
CLASSIC QUEEN: Hit the right saucer behind the right drop targets to light and start Classic Queen modes. During Classic Queen modes, hit blue lights.
WIZARD MODES: Complete modes for all album banner names to light wizard modes.
MULTIBALL: Hit loops lit with green lights to light lock. Hit ramps to lock balls. During multiball, hit green lights.
MUSIC NOTES; Collect music notes to light extra ball, light mystery, and light "X" at the inlanes.
"X": Roll over the lit X inlane to multiply the value of your next shot.
MYSTERY: Hit red arrows on the upper playfield to light a mystery award at the center saucer.
DOUBLE SCORING: Hit teal targets on the upper playfield to light double scoring at the upper playfield hole.

name: Quicksilver
desc:
Quicksilver is a celebrated pinball machine released by Stern Electronics in June 1980. It's a solid-state machine, known for its sci-fi theme, designed by Joe Joos Jr. with artwork by Doug Watson. The software was handled by Bill Pfutzenreuter. Notably, Quicksilver does not feature ramps or multiball, sticking to a more classic pinball experience with two flippers and digital display. The production run was relatively limited, with only 1,201 units made.
The Visual Pinball X (VPX) version of Quicksilver, a digital recreation, offers enhanced features including new lighting, updated table physics, improved flipper mechanics, and high-quality sound effects. This version also incorporates a new script, reworked images for better clarity, and physical adjustments to improve gameplay realism. Enthusiasts appreciate these updates, especially the modifications to the table's physics and the addition of contemporary pinball mechanics like nFozzy flippers and Fleep sound effects​​​​.
Pinside, a comprehensive resource for pinball enthusiasts, lists Quicksilver with an estimated value between $5,360 and $6,240, reflecting its status as a collector's item and its demand in the market. It also boasts a rating of 7.978 out of 10 based on Pinsider reviews, ranking #86 in the Pinside Pinball Top 100. The machine is celebrated for its fast-paced gameplay, underscored by its marketing slogan, "It Ain't Just Any Plain Old Silver Ball.It's the Fastest Moving Pinball Ever!"​​.

id: Rack Em Up (Gottlieb 1983)/Rack Em Up (Gottlieb 1983)_1.0.9 Hybrid.vpx
name: Rack 'Em Up! (Gottlieb 1983)
desc: "Rack 'Em Up" has a pool and billiards theme, featuring two flippers, no ramps, and no multiball. It is part of the Gottlieb System 80A series. A total of 1,762 units were produced.

name: Radical
desc: The Visual Pinball X recreation of "Radical!" by Bally from 1990 is a highly detailed digital version of the original pinball table, emphasizing the skateboarding culture of the time. It features improvements and enhancements such as Fleep sounds, nFozzy Physics, 3D inserts, updated ramp textures, lighting updates, Flupper domes and bumpers, and an integrated VR room by Sixtoe, among others. This mod was made possible thanks to the efforts of the VPinWorkshop team and JP Salas, who originally worked on this table. The recreation is designed to provide a nostalgic yet fresh experience of the "Radical!" table, capturing its essence and bringing it to the modern digital pinball community​​​​.

name: Ramones BW (Original 2024)
desc:
This Original table is a brilliant, high-contrast tribute to the kings of punk rock, designed entirely around a striking black and white (B&W) aesthetic. Based on the classic layout of Bally’s 1972 Fireball, this mod perfectly fuses vintage electromechanical gameplay with the raw, underground spirit of the band.
The Monochromatic Look: The entire playfield, plastics, and cabinet artwork abandon traditional arcade colors for deep blacks, sharp whites, and grays. This minimalist, high-contrast styling beautifully mirrors the iconic 1970s rock photography of the Ramones.
The Dynamic PuP-Pack: The backglass comes alive with a custom "PuP-Pack" video display. It triggers real live performance footage, rare concert clips, and animations of Joey, Johnny, Dee Dee, and Tommy rocking out on your secondary monitor in perfect sync with the gameplay.
Classic Chaotic Mechanics: True to its Fireball roots, the gameplay is notoriously fast, chaotic, and physical. It features the famous Zipper-Flippers (which physically slide together to close the drain gap) and a central Disc Spinner that rapidly whips the ball in random directions across the monochrome playfield.
Audio-Driven Spirit: The machine’s fast tempo matches the 2-minute rush of a punk song. With the band's actual music tracks loaded, the gameplay is completely driven by high-tempo rhythms. Targets clank like heavy snare drums, and the audio syncs perfectly with the frantic action of the ball.

id: Red and Ted's Road Show 1994 (Williams)/Red and Ted's Road Show (Williams 1994) VPW 1.5.4.vpx
name: Red & Ted's Road Show
desc:
Red & Ted's Road Show (also known as Road Show) is a 1994 widebody pinball game designed by Pat Lawlor and released by Williams. It is part of WMS' SuperPin line of widebody games.
Country singer Carlene Carter provided the voice of Red, and her song, "Every Little Thing", is featured in the game. The game is considered an unofficial successor of FunHouse, as both were designed by Pat Lawlor and feature animated talking head(s) along with some similar playfield layout ideas. It is equipped with a shaker motor to make the machine vibrate. It was the first pinball machine to feature an additional daily highscore list.

name: Rescue 911
desc:
From Gottlieb comes the official Rescue 911 pinball game based on the TV show of the same name. Released in 1994, it incorporates a rescue crew motif, complete with a little helicopter that electromagnetically carries the ball to another location. It was designed by Bill Parker, with art by Jeanine and Constantino Mitchell and David Moore.
It does not include host William Shatner's likeness. Instead, what the game offers are six emergency missions, ranging from an Emergency Room baby delivery and a Cave-In, to rescuing people from Flash Floods and Wildfires. Use the Helicopter to fly pinballs to critical areas, collect the Medi-Alert bonuses at the ramp, and try to save enough lives to reach the pulse-pounding "Life Force" Wizard Mode.

"Ripley's Believe It or Not!" is a pinball machine released in 2004 by Stern Pinball, designed by Pat Lawlor. While I can't access the specific visual details of the Visual Pinball version at this moment, the physical table itself features artwork and themes based on the Ripley's Believe It or Not! franchise, known for its bizarre and fascinating facts, artifacts, and stories from around the world.
The pinball machine is designed to capture the essence of Ripley's adventurous and exploratory spirit, incorporating various elements and locations from the "Ripley's" universe. Players can expect to see references to different continents and cultures, with missions and modes that reflect the theme of discovery and surprise. The playfield is decorated with vibrant artwork, showcasing exotic and unusual items, and is filled with ramps, targets, and obstacles that offer a challenging and entertaining gameplay experience. The game is also known for its engaging sound effects and voiceovers, which contribute to its immersive and quirky atmosphere.

name: Riverboat Gambler
desc:
Riverboat Gambler is a gambling themed pinball machine produced by Williams. Pinball machine designer Mark Ritchie reportedly sings the song that plays during the game, whose gravel-voiced, New Orleans-style male voice sounds similar to Louis Armstrong.
In the center of the head of the machine, a vertical roulette wheel operates more like the Wheel of Fortune than an actual roulette wheel and does not have a ball. 7 of 16 sections are black, 7 are red, which alternate, with two green spaces that have stars on opposite sides. Located directly above the roulette wheel, a four digit display keeps track of virtual chips. The player uses chips earned on the playfield to bet on the roulette wheel.

name: Robo-War (Premier 1988)
desc: Robo-War features a sci-fi robot theme with two flippers, one ramp, and a two-ball multiball mode. Part of the Gottlieb System 80B series. A total of 2,130 units were produced.

name: Robocop
desc:
RoboCop is a licensed pinball machine designed by Joe Kaminkow and Ed Cebula, with illustrations by Kevin O'Connor. It was released by Data East Pinball in 1989, just a few months before the premiere of RoboCop 2.
As one would expect, the game is a tie-in to the 1987 smash movie featuring the titular cyborg super-cop. As RoboCop, the player must patrol the streets of Detroit, enforcing his Prime Directives while arresting lawbreakers of all types. Capture Emil Antonowsky, Clarence Boddicker, and Dick Jones, then jump the Entry Ramp to start multiball. Spell ROBOCOP for random rewards and an extra ball, then get some target practice and confront ED-209 for a million-point bonus, all while the game plays memorable quotes from the film.

name: Robot (Zaccaria 1985)
desc:
Robot is a Physical Pinball Table released in 1985 by Italian arcade game maker Zaccaria.

The game depicts a Robot War in an unspecified future, with the player as part of a human resistance fighting against the mechanical menace. Hit the five dropdown targets to enable the Orange Special, then knock down the three Z-Targets and enter the Tunnel to raise the bonus multiplier. Run across the Robot Bridge and five robots will rise from the playfield; knock them all down to advance the Red Special and collect the jackpot.

name: Rocky (Gottlieb 1982)
desc:
Rocky is a Pinball Table designed by John Trudeau with art by David Moore. It was an indirect tie-in to Rocky III, and was released by Gottlieb in 1982.

Not surprisingly, the Rocky pinball pits the player in a ten-round boxing match; knock down the drop target corresponding to the current round to advance to the next. More surprisingly is the unconventional table layout, which has two pairs of flippers at the bottom of the playfield. Extra balls and specials are available for going through seven or more rounds, and an "Instant Win" button gives beginners a fighting chance. Cheering crowds and the "Rocky" theme music round out the package.

Sharp-eyed filmgoers will notice that the Rocky pinball machine is not the one that appears in Rocky III; that was a prop backglass installed on an existing pinball table. Only three of the prop backglasses were made. One was destroyed on-camera, and the surviving two are in possession of private collectors.

name: RockyLegends
desc:
I present to you my new table,
**ROCKY LEGENDS**

The result of over six months of work, I poured my heart and soul into it.
I hope you enjoy it as much as I enjoyed creating it.
First, I want to thank two people. The first is **JPSalas**, for the base I used with his permission. The second is **Philip Mationi**, for his incredible graphics. He fulfilled my desire for a polished table.
It includes some new features: 3D objects that appear based on achievements, as well as rules that can be viewed in video format during gameplay and explained by Rocky himself. It contains numerous tasks to complete, along with the associated multiballs.
For this occasion, I created an entry in the **DOF** for the toys and LED lighting.
It comes with a **PUP-PACK** that retraces the world of the *Rocky* films.

Feel free to leave your comments and opinions!

VPX Version: I tested in VPX 10.8 64 Bit.
Have fun playing, and good luck !

Special thanks for their help and pre-launch testing of the table to:  Philip Mationi (Graphics and testing), Micki, Kimiko (testing and 3D help), Fabrizio NT, Gwen Lizard, Victoria LF and Virgil Angus..

name: Roller Coaster Tycoon
desc:
The Visual Pinball version of RollerCoaster Tycoon, produced by Stern in 2002, is a modded table that includes numerous enhancements over the original. These improvements consist of advanced physics (nFozzy Physics), improved sounds (Fleep Sounds), a LUT Selector, dynamic ball shadows, high-resolution textures (up to 4k), fully rendered GI textures for various table components, and gameplay fixes among many other adjustments. The table also features new drop targets by Rothbauerw, Flupper Domes, and new plastic and metal ramps. This version of RollerCoaster Tycoon pinball table has received praise for its quality and the depth of its modifications, making it a favorite among players​​.
The original Stern's RollerCoaster Tycoon pinball machine itself is known for its roller coaster theme, with the playfield featuring ramps named after roller coasters ("The Flying Ghost", "The Flying Turns", "Chicago Loop", and "The Rocket"), various themed obstacles, and targets such as "Scrambled Eggs", "Bumper Cars", and "Dunk the Dummy". The main objective is to open rides by hitting them to change their status lights from red to yellow and then green, drawing in guests for bonus points and extra balls. It also features a multi-ball mode initiated by locking balls in the "Chicago Loop" and then hitting "The Flying Turns". Successful gameplay can lead to jackpots and even a "Super Jackpot" of 1 million points with hits on "The Rocket" during active multi-ball. Completing all food stalls grants an extra ball, adding to the strategic elements of play​​.

name: Roller Disco
desc: The "Roller Disco" pinball machine, created by Gottlieb in January 1980, is a solid-state, widebody game designed by Ed Krynski with artwork by Gordon Morison. It supports up to 4 players, features 4 flippers but no ramps or multiball. A total of 2,400 units were produced, with an estimated value between $1,110 and $1,290. The game is part of Gottlieb's System 1 generation and is recognized for its vibrant theme and design reflective of the era​​.

name: Rollergames
desc:
Rollergames is a 1990 pinball game designed by Steve Ritchie, with artwork by Pat McMahon and released by Williams Electronics. It is based on the short-lived roller derby "sports entertainment" television show of the same name from 1989.
Its most notable features include the Deep Freeze Magna-Flip, which, when lit, magnetically freezes the ball next to the upper right flipper, for an easy shot to the Wall ramp, and the multiball launching loop, which, during normal gameplay, kick the balls out of (and back into) the lock at random times.

name: Royal-Flush-Deluxe (Gottlieb 1983)
desc: Royal Flush Deluxe, released by Gottlieb in June 1983, is a solid-state pinball machine featuring a card game theme. Designed by Ed Krynski with artwork by David Moore and Terry Doerzaph, the machine includes two flippers, no ramps, and no multiball. It uses the Gottlieb System 80A hardware and has a digital display.

name: Safe Cracker
desc:
Safe Cracker is a 1996 pinball machine by Pat Lawlor and Williams Electronics (under the Bally label), with art by John Youssi. The game revolves around a bank heist, where you must avoid guards and sneak into the vault to crack the safe and get rich.
It is very different from most pinball machines — the playfield is noticeably smaller, allowing it to fit in places a conventional pinball machine couldn't go, and the backglass is rather large. Players do not have a finite amount of balls, but instead have a set time limit to get into the Vault, whereupon a board game begins on the backglass. The player (and the computer, playing the security guards) rolls the dice in hopes of getting a good space. Making it to the safe in the center ends the game, and the player is rewarded with a Magic Token that rolls out of the backglass.
Players could keep playing to collect the twenty different token designs available. Alternately, players could use the tokens to play "Assault on the Vault", where they have 90 seconds and four balls to hit as many targets and shots as possible in order to break into the vault once again. A third use — intended in the design but never actually promoted — was for adult-oriented venues to let players redeem tokens for free drinks or other rewards.

name: Scared Stiff
desc:
The game features a B-movie horror theme. Players have to go through the Six Tales Of Terror to level up the Stiff-o-meter. These are: Eyes Of The Bony Beast, Terror From The Crate, the Stiff In The Coffin, the Monster's Lab, Night Of The Leapers, and the Return Of The Deadheads. The interactive backbox contains a player controlled spinning spider. It is used to collect unique features and start special modes. Scared Stiff uses the DCS Sound System.
Scared Stiff was exhibited at the 1996 AMOA show in Dallas, with Cassandra Peterson present in her Elvira identity to promote the game.
When Scared Stiff was introduced in 1996, it was designed to have moving rubber boogieman figures mounted over the slingshots. These were designed to move forward with the kicker each time the ball hit the slingshot. The game's ROM also allowed for the boogiemen to 'dance' to the music during the Boogie Man Boogie mode by kicking with the music. Very late in production, this feature was removed because the figures' arms were thought to eventually break off. An opening between the feet of the slingshot plastics is still present on all production machines, as well as an entry in the game's manual about the feature. Additionally, the code in the machine's ROM supports the feature. Because of this, many hobbyists have added the boogiemen figure modifications to their machines.

name: Scooby Doo
desc:
The "Scooby Doo, 2022" is a custom table for Visual Pinball X (VPX), an original creation that modernizes the classic VP9 Scooby Doo pinball table. This version includes a complete overhaul with better code, streamlined gameplay, and a fully re-mastered audio track. It's built on top of JP Salas's January 2022 release of "Wrath of Olympus," retaining all the original code from that table. If you're familiar with the "Wrath of Olympus" rules, you'll have a good understanding of how to play this table. The table also includes additional features like a choice of six different desktop backgrounds, user switches for DOF Testing and "Beer Mode," a "JUKEBOX" mode for playing favorite Scooby TV songs, and enhanced DMD screens and messaging. Various bugs reported in the initial release have been addressed in version 1.0.1, including fixes for audio tracks, gameplay enhancements, and a streamlined script​​​​.
Additionally, for those interested in visual modifications, there are four "Scooby-Doo (Original 2022) Full DMDs" available, including one static and three animated versions. These were created with artwork from "rkd.zone" and include creative solutions to avoid copyright issues, like featuring "The Mustard Machine." This add-on demonstrates the community's creativity in enhancing the digital pinball experience with visually appealing and thematic elements that complement the gameplay​​.

name: Scorpion
desc:
The "Scorpion" is a pinball machine released in July 1980 by Williams Electronic Games, Inc. It's designed by Barry Oursler, with software by Larry DeMar and artwork by Constantino Mitchell and Tony Ramunni. Randy Pfeiffer contributed to the sound design. This machine is a solid state, wide-body cabinet that can accommodate up to 4 players. It features 4 flippers, no ramps, and offers a 2-ball multiball play. Notably, "Scorpion" doesn't include any ramps, emphasizing its classic play style. It's part of the Williams System 6 generation and had a production run of 2,000 units. The estimated value ranges from $1,850 to $2,150.
The playfield layout of "Scorpion" is intricate, with a focus on keeping the ball in play and navigating through various targets, locks, and bonuses. It has two lower flippers for standard play, with additional upper flippers in the upper left quadrant to facilitate play in the mini-playfield area. The game is known for its wide body, which allows for a spacious playfield filled with a variety of play elements. Players can score points through inlanes, outlanes, drop targets, and standup targets, among other features. Completing certain target sequences lights up pop bumpers and spinners for additional scoring opportunities. The machine also includes a manual plunger, allowing for skilled shots right from the start.
One of the main goals in "Scorpion" is to initiate and sustain two-ball multiball play as long as possible, a task involving locking balls in both left and right saucers and managing a variety of playfield features to maximize scoring. The machine's detailed and thematic artwork, combined with its challenging playfield layout, make it a memorable piece for pinball enthusiasts.
The marketing slogan for "Scorpion" captures the adventurous spirit of the game: "Come aboard the SCORPION - There's no time to lose!" This encapsulates the dynamic and thrilling experience of playing the game, inviting players to dive into the action.

name: Seawitch
desc:
Seawitch is an arcade pinball game designed by Mike Kubin and illustrated by Bob Timm. It was released in May 1980 by Stern Electronics.
Before an ominous storm-tossed shoreline, two Seawitches engage in a no-holds-barred battle for supremacy while a school of mermaids watch from the sidelines. Launch the ball to loop around the upper playfield and down to the flippers, then sweep the three banks of drop targets to advance the bonus and increase the multiplier. Against the sounds of crashing waves, raise the value of the spinner, then use the two upper flippers to fling the ball around the Rip Tide and quickly build up your score.

name: Secret Agent (Original 2024) v1.0
desc: Secret Agent is a fast-paced, cartoon-style spy-themed pinball table full of action and personality. Players step into the shoes of a secret agent, battling colorful villains across dynamic missions. With stackable multiballs, varied modes, vibrant visuals, and energetic voiceovers, it delivers a thrilling and playful pinball experience inspired by classic animated spy adventures.

name: Secret Service
desc:
Secret Service is a 1988 Pinball Table from Data East. It was designed by Joe Kaminkow, with art by Kevin O'Connor and Margaret Hudson.
The player is Agent 001 of the United States Secret Service, with one simple mission — protect Washington, D.C. from the evil Soviets who are targeting the nation's leaders. Patrol the streets of D.C. in your service-issued Ferrari, gun down enemy agents in front of the Capitol Building, then curve around the Beltway and lock your ball in the White House. Infiltrate the Soviet spy headquarters via the underground passage, then start a three-ball multiball for a chance at the Special.
Secret Service is memorable for its post-game karaoke mode; after each game, the table would play the chorus from "Nobody Does It Better" (from The Spy Who Loved Me), while displaying the lyrics on the alphanumeric score display. It also featured a Digital Stereo soundsystem, a point played up in advertisements.

id: Serious Sam Pinball 2017 (Original)/Serious Sam Pinball v600.vpx
name: Serious Sam Pinball
desc:
The "Serious Sam Pinball" from 2017 is an original table created for Visual Pinball X (VPX), inspired by Croteam's game "Serious Sam: The Second Encounter". The creator, jpsalas, decided to use graphics not directly from the game itself but from various Maya images and models to craft a unique visual experience. This pinball table stands out because it solely relies on VPX, excluding the need for any external programs, and includes all necessary sounds and music within the table itself.
Significant updates and improvements have been made to the table since its initial release, including updated physics for more realistic gameplay, a new set of mechanical sounds for enhanced audio experience, and fixes to flashers for better visual effects. Moreover, the latest version introduced LUT images adjustments for varied visual tones and warmer shades, offering players the ability to customize their visual experience further.
The table design is deeply integrated with elements and characters from "Serious Sam: The Second Encounter", providing a thematic adventure as players navigate the pinball gameplay. Despite the rich content and complexity, the creator assures that the rules are straightforward and easy to grasp, with a document available for those who wish to understand the gameplay mechanics in depth.
