name: Shaq Attaq
desc:
This 1995 basketball themed pinball from Gottlieb is “A real slam dunk!”
An actual moving basket located under the dome challenges players to sink baskets, timing is essential as the ball sails airborne.

id: Sharkey's Shootout 2000 (Stern Pinball)/Sharkey's Shootout (Stern 2000) Burger LW VR.vpx
name: Sharkey's Shootout
desc:
Sharkey's Shootout is a Pinball Table released by Stern Pinball in 2000. Designed by John Borg with art by veteran pinball artist John Youssi, this is a game with an unconventionally tumultuous origin.
Sharkey's is about an exclusive, invitation-only pool tournament in Sharkey's Pool Hall, where a motley cast of characters — including Sharkey himself, Tex the cowboy, and a space alien — attempt to dethrone the current champion, Real Life pool expert Jeanette "The Black Widow" Lee. The player must first defeat five other players at 8-ball or 9-ball, then take on The Black Widow herself to win the generous cash prize. And the challenge extends beyond the playfield, as Sharkey's is Stern's first tournament pinball, allowing players worldwide to compete with each other.

name: Sharpshooter
desc: The Sharpshooter pinball machine, produced by Game Plan, Inc. in May 1979, features a Western theme. Designed by Ed Cebula, Joe Joos Jr., and Roger Sharpe, with artwork by George Molentin, it is a solid state type with a digital display. It supports up to 4 players, has 2 flippers, but no ramps or multiball feature. Approximately 4,200 units were produced, and its estimated value ranges between $1,390 and $1,610​​.

name: Sheriff (Gottlieb 1971)
desc: Sheriff from September 1971 was the first Gottlieb-machine to use a "Dummy-Zero" and the first multi-player with a large drop-target-bank, which soon became some kind of Gottlieb-trademark.

name: Shovel Knight (Original)
desc: Original table, designed in 2017. It is based on Shovel Knight, the retro-styled platform game released in 2014 by Yacht Club Games.

name: Shrek
desc:
The "Shrek" pinball machine from Stern Pinball, released in August 2008, is a fascinating piece that shares its playfield design with "The Family Guy" pinball machine but features different artwork and programming to immerse players in the world of Shrek. The game incorporates voice acting approved by major actors through their contracts with DreamWorks, making for an authentic experience. Notably, the game faced challenges, including licensing issues with Smash Mouth's "All Star" for the opening music, eventually leading to the use of the original recording for the game's start. The game also uniquely utilizes music directly from the three Shrek movie soundtracks, adding depth and authenticity to the gameplay experience.
Designed by Pat Lawlor with software development by Lonnie D. Ropp and Mike Kyzivat, the artwork was created by John Youssi. The animations were managed by Mark Galvez and Tom Kyzivat, with sound design by Jeff Powell. The pinball machine features a solid-state design, capable of entertaining up to 4 players, with 5 flippers, 1 ramp, and a 5-ball multiball feature. The display type is Dot Matrix, and the game was part of the Stern SAM System generation, with only 600 units produced. Its estimated value ranges between $5730 and $6670, reflecting its collectibility and the enjoyment it brings to players and collectors alike​​.
DreamWorks Animation's SHREK is the best animated movie franchise of all time and now has an officially licensed pinball machine!
One of the SHREK pinball machine's main features is the Donkey's mini-playfield. This is situated in the upper right hand corner of the game board.
It has mini-flippers that the player controls with the regular flipper buttons when the game is in ‘Donkey mini-playfield' mode.
The mini-playfield has ramps and targets to shoot at while an actual Donkey figurine spins in front of the mini-playfield.
Game features:
Figurines of five SHREK characters, including Shrek, Donkey, Puss in Boots, Princess Fiona and Gingy
A mirror sculpture of Prince Charming sits in the centre of the playfield and can be struck by the pinball
Two captive pinballs spell out P-I-N-B-A-L-L when hit
SHREK also includes plenty of exciting multi-ball action

name: Silverball Mania
desc:
Silverball Mania is a Pinball Table designed by Jim Patla and illustrated by Kevin O'Connor. It was released in 1980 by Bally.
In the annals of pinball, Silverball Mania stands out for its mesmerizing art; the mirrored backglass is a stunning combination of black and silver, an eye-catching attraction in any sort of light. The playfield itself depicts an abstract mercurial landscape of chrome, where muscular men and lithe women spring forth from a gigantic silver ball under the watchful tutelage of a silver wizard. Among all this activity, the player's goal is to hit the various targets and spell SILVERBALL MANIA; loop the central horseshoe to raise the Disappearing Kicker, then let it kick drained balls back onto the table and try for the Carry-Over Special.

name: Sinbad
desc:
Sinbad is a 1978 solid-state pinball table by Gottlieb, designed by Ed Krynski and illustrated by Gordon Morison.
 It draws inspiration from the 1977 Columbia Pictures film "Sinbad and the Eye of the Tiger." This game is notable for its integration of four banks of drop targets with the bonus ladder, bonus multipliers, and top rollover lanes. Both two- and four-player versions were produced, with slight differences in artwork and rules to accommodate electromechanical (EM) limitations. For more details, you can visit Pinside's page on the Sinbad pinball machine​​.
The game is a licensed tie-in to the Ray Harryhausen movie, Sinbad and the Eye of the Tiger .

name: Skateball
desc: The "Skateball" pinball machine, produced by Bally Manufacturing Co. in September 1980, features a design centered around skateboarding and outdoor themes. It was created by a team including Claude Fernandez (game design), Rehman Merchant (software), and artists Greg Freres, Kevin O'Connor, and Margaret Hudson. This solid-state machine, part of the Bally MPU AS-2518-35 generation, was released with a production run of 4,150 units. It supports up to 4 players, has 4 flippers, but does not feature ramps or multiball. The estimated value of "Skateball" ranges between $3,050 and $3,550​​.

name: Snow Derby (Gottlieb 1970)
desc: Snow Derby and Snow Queen are two pinball machines released by Gottlieb in 1970. Both machines share the same gameplay design but differ in the number of players—Snow Queen accommodates four players, while Snow Derby is for two players, these machines feature a winter sports theme with skiing and snowmobiles.

name: Solar Fire
desc: "Solar Fire" is a pinball machine produced by Williams Electronic Games, Inc. in July 1981. This solid state machine features artwork by Constantino and Jeanine Mitchell, with game design by Barry Oursler and software by Ed Suchocki. It supports up to four players, includes four flippers, two ramps, and offers a multiball feature for up to three balls. A total of 782 units were produced, and it belongs to the Williams System 7 generation​​.

name: Solar Ride
desc:
This 1979 pinball is a classic Gottlieb solid state electronic system 1 machine.
It has 3 flippers and the simple gameplay includes pop bumpers, kick-out holes a 5-bank drop target and a roll-under in the upper right hand.

id: Sonic The Hedgehog (Original)/Sonic The Hedgehog (Brendan Bailey 2005) VPX MOD 1.33.vpx
name: Sonic The Hedgehog (Brendan Bailey 2005) VPX MOD 1.33
desc:
The original is "The Hedgehog 2"  for Future Pinball created by Brendan Bailey in 2005.
AND Converted for VPX by javier1515
AND Ultra DMD added by DCrosby
AND VR ROOM support by DaRdog
I made some bug fixes for the above
The attached directb2s file is required for VR.
There are two types of VR ROOM.
VR_ROOM = 1 : Minimal
VR_ROOM = 2 : Mixed Reality
Mixed Reality supports chromakey on Virtual Desktop.
       Virtual Desktop settings
       Chromakey color is blue  RGB = 0 : 0 : 255
       Similarity=5, Smoothness=5
----------------------------
Rules:
Multiball - Shoot the bottom and top 3 banks of drop targets to light the middle and side eject holes for ball lock. After locking two balls, the upper left side hole will be lit for multiball. During multiball, shoot the upper left side hole for a 250,000 point jackpot! When two balls have drained, normal play resumes, only now you must complete the drop targets twice in order to light lock.

Hurry Up - Completing the 5 stand up targets along the upper and lower playfields starts the "Hurry Up" feature. You have 10 seconds to shoot any hole (or the drop target in front of the lower eject hole) before complete the targets again. If a ball is locked the left side eject hole, you cannot score a hurry up award there.

Savers - The game begins with the kickback and the save gate active. They only save the ball once and then shut off. However, they can be reacttivated by shooting either of the lower stand up targets when the purple sheild light is flashing (they are lit when the ball passes through one of the inlanes). The Center post is activated by shooting the top center loop shot when lit. You light this shot by having the ball pass through the left side lane. Once activated, the Gate and kickback will remain so until used. The center post, however, only lasts for 15 seconds.

Invincibility - Making the right side loop shot 3 times starts invincibility. This causes all 3 savers to be active consistantly for 20 seconds.

Bonus X - completing the top 3 lanes advances the bonus multiplier from 1X, 2X, 3X, 4X, and 5X. The multiplier is reset for each ball.

Extra Ball - Extra Balls are awarded when you reach the score of 750,000 and 1,500,000

name: Sorcerer (Williams 1985)
desc:
Sorcerer is a 1985 Pinball game designed by Mark Ritchie and released by Williams Electronics. With the Sorcerer's flashing eyes and numerous taunts, it became the second-best-selling pinball game of the year, and is fondly remembered for its straightforward but challenging gameplay, fast action, and ornate art by Pam Erickson.

The table itself is the named Sorcerer, who is being challenged in a magic duel by the player. Invoke his title to build your magic power, then use it to summon demons, earn extra balls and light the special. But move quickly with the upper flipper, or else the magic will dissipate and leave you powerless. For more points, lock two balls to start multiball, then repeatedly shoot the ramp to build the multiball multiplier up to 5x.

id: South Park (Sega 1999)/South Park (Sega 1999) Physics Sound Hybrid MOD_1.1.2.vpx
name: South Park
desc: South Park is an arcade pinball game produced by Sega Pinball in 1999. It proved to be the last pinball game relased by Sega before the pinball division was sold to Gary Stern and reformed as Stern Pinball. As one would expect, the game is based on the infamous animated show from Trey Parker and Matt Stone, and brings with it the show's notorious Toilet Humor, foul language, and obscene attitudes. Help Stan kiss Wendy, retrieve Mr. Hankey for Kyle, give Cartman an anal probe, recruit the kids for Chef's fotball team, and kill Kenny repeatedly. Hit Mr. Hankey to start multiball, then flush pinballs down the toilet for the jackpot - and be prepared to save the townsfolk in case of unexpected volcano eruptions.

name: Space Cadet
desc:
The Visual Pinball version of Space Cadet from 2021, known as JP's Space Cadet, is an interpretation based on the original game by Cinematronics/Maxis from 1996. Created by jpsalas, this table for VPX 10.7 features graphics and layout that are the author's own take on the classic game. The table aims to closely follow the original game's rules, with missions and gameplay designed to progress the player's rank from Space Cadet to Fleet Admiral through the completion of a series of tasks. However, it introduces some changes and additions, such as multiball functionality which wasn't present in the Microsoft version and variations in how replays and extra balls are handled.
The table is described as being not as easy as the original game, with shots being more difficult, but it's still considered an easy game overall, offering plenty of extra balls and replays. It might not be challenging enough for seasoned pinball enthusiasts, but it's expected to be enjoyable for kids and those who fondly remember playing Space Cadet in the 1990s. The creator also mentioned adding modern elements to the table while retaining the essence of the old game. It's designed to be played with VPX 7 or newer versions, marking a significant contribution by jpsalas after 18 years of creating tables​​​​.

id: Space Cadet Galaxy Edition/JPs Space Cadet (GE)V1-2.vpx
name: Space Cadet Galaxy Edition
desc: Space Cadet is a retro-futuristic pinball game where the player takes on the role of a young pilot at the Space Academy, completing missions to rise through the ranks of the space fleet. Popularized through its inclusion in Windows XP as 3D Pinball for Windows – Space Cadet, this cult classic captivated millions of players with its immersive space-themed atmosphere and dynamic gameplay mechanics.

name: Space Gambler (playmatic 1978)
desc:
Theme: Outer Space - Fantasy
Notable Features: Flippers (2), Pop bumpers (2), Mushroom bumpers (4), Slingshots (2), Drop targets (4), Standup targets (3), Rollover buttons (3), Spinning target (1). 3 or 5 ball play.
Toys: Flashing lights on 3D 'Tunnel' on the backglass.
Notes: Probably the first SS game by Playmatic.

The backglass artwork depicts elements from the Star Wars movies: the droids R2-D2 and C-3PO, and TIE fighter spacecraft. Also depicted is a lady with an unusual helmet seen previously on the backglass of Gottlieb's 1976 'Target Alpha'.

name: Space Invaders
desc:
Space Invaders is an arcade pinball machine designed by Jim Patla and released by Bally in 1979. As Bally's Video Game division Midway was the Western distributor of the arcade video game at the time, that makes this the Ur-Example of the Pinball Spinoff.
As with most other pinball games at the time, there wasn't much of a story to the game — the player would simply shoot pinballs at various alien targets to repel the invaders. To flesh things out, Bally distributed an eight-page Comic Book/Advertisement to arcade operators that provided a backstory: the invaders were a race of Giger-esque aliens who have infiltrated Earth as sprites in the Video Game cabinets. Now the second phase of their plan has begun, as the aliens exit the arcade games and combine to form incredibly addictive pinball machines that completely steal the minds (and quarters) of unsuspecting humans.
The art for the game (by Paul Faris) was heavily "borrowed" from the designs used in the movie Alien. Naturally, 20th Century Fox sued Bally over the resemblance, stopping production after 11,000 machines were manufactured. Bally eventually reached a settlement with Fox, paying royalties for each pinball sold.

name: Space Jam
desc:
Space Jam is a Licensed Pinball Table released by Sega Pinball in 1996, illustrated by Morgan Weistling and designed by Joe Kaminkow, Orin Day, and Lonnie Ropp.
Based on the Warner Bros. movie of the same name, this is a lighthearted romp where Basketball superstar Michael Jordan teams up with Bugs Bunny and the Looney Tunes stable to play ball against the evil alien Monstars. Make baskets into the magnetic hoop for multiball and extra balls, race with the Road Runner and the Tasmanian Devil for the Fast Break, then get on Fire and score some ten-pointers. Get the Rebound, complete the Slam, and get In Yer Face, then light all seven planets and start the Final Jam with Number 23 himself.

name: Space Race (Recel 1977)
desc:
Step into the cockpit of a 1970s classic. Space Race is a quintessential vintage pinball machine released by Recel in 1977. It captures the era's fascination with the cosmos, blending "Space Age" aesthetics with the tactile, clattery charm of electro-mechanical (EM) gaming.

The Vibe

The machine is a time capsule of 70s sci-fi art. The backglass features vibrant, stylized illustrations of astronauts and futuristic spacecraft, heavy on the oranges, blues, and purples that defined the decade's color palette.

Gameplay Features

Space Race is known for its relatively fast-paced flow and a layout that rewards precision. Key features include:

Four Flippers: It utilizes two standard flippers at the bottom and two smaller flippers further up the playfield, allowing for complex "cross-court" shots.

The "Kick-Out" Holes: Aiming for these pockets is essential for high scores and activating multipliers.

Pop Bumpers: Three central bumpers keep the ball zipping through the upper playfield, mimicking the chaotic energy of an asteroid field.

Target Striking: Features a mix of drop targets and stationary targets that, when hit in sequence, light up the "Space Race" bonus.

Technical Snapshot

Feature	Details
Manufacturer	Recel (Spain)
Release Year	1977
Type	Electro-mechanical (EM)
Players	Up to 4 players (alternating turns)
Theme	Outer Space / Exploration

name: Space Shuttle
desc:
In Space Shuttle the main goal is to acquire the shuttle score value from spelling out "S H U T T L E" by hitting six stand up targets and one drop target - or by using the lit inlanes (if available).
The reward for the shuttle score value is assigned randomly with each new ball, or by hitting a stand up target, at the top of a short ramp. It will be one of the following:
50,000 points plus a bonus holdover,
an extra ball (a score award is given if 5 extra balls are earned during game),
a special,
100,000 points,
50,000 points,
20,000 points, or
100,000 points plus lite outlanes, which will give another shuttle score value if the ball goes down one of the outlanes
Additionally three lights labeled U, S and A are lit when a ball rolls over them. They are worth 2,000 points each. Spelling USA increases the end of ball bonus multiplier (a multiplication factor for points earned and awarded when the ball in play drains), up to 7X. There are three jet bumpers that are worth 100 points when unlit and 1,000 points when lit. Two or three ball multiball is started by hitting one ball up a ball lock or two balls up two different ball locks and then shooting a ball up the center ramp when the drop target is down.

name: Space Station
desc:
Space Station is a Physical Pinball Table released by Williams Electronics in 1987. It was designed by Barry Oursler, with artwork by Tim Elliott, sounds by Brian Schmidt, and software by Ed Boon.
Space Station is widely considered to be an unofficial sequel to Space Shuttle. It features a second set of "STATION" spot targets that scores its own independently-cycling value and builds upon the Stop-N-Score feature. Station also features a mini upper playfield above the pop bumpers and a rotating space station toy used to direct balls towards the locks on either side of the playfield.

name: Special Force (Bally 1986)
desc: Special Force features a military theme with two flippers, three ramps, and a three-ball multiball mode and produced 2,750 units.

name: Spectrum (Bally 1981)
desc: Spectrum is a Physical Pinball Table designed by Claude Fernandez with art by Margaret Hudson. Released by Bally in 1982, it's based on— of all things— the game Mastermind! Players have to deduce the 4-color code provided by the "Computor" by shooting the ball into the colored saucers (to obtain clues), comparing them to the light display on the playfield, and then shooting banks of colored targets to place the colors in the order of your guess.

id: Spider-Man VE (Stern 2016) Classic Edition/Spider-Man VE (Stern 2016) Classic VPW Mod 2.1.vpx
name: Spider-Man
desc:
In 2016, Stern Pinball released the Vault Edition, an updated version of the 2007 game. Unlike other Vault Editions, the game's aesthetics were completely overhauled: the playfield and backglass art were updated with comic book-style illustrations by Mark Bagley from Ultimate Spider-Man, with the dot-matrix animations, audio, and game modes updated to match. The actual playfield layout and rules remain the same, however.
Based on Sam Raimi's Spider-Man Trilogy starring Tobey Maguire, the game pits the players against the villains of all three movies. Rock the Green Goblin by shooting his pumpkin bombs, build speed by whipping around Venom, then use the webslingers to launch balls across the playfield. Hit Sandman as he rises and falls, but make sure Doctor Octopus doesn't catch you in his tentacles. The game features video and voice clips from the films, and J. K. Simmons reprises his role as J. Jonah Jameson to give player instructions.

name: Spirit
desc: The "Spirit" pinball machine, manufactured by D. Gottlieb & Co. in October 1982, is a solid state machine featuring a wide body design. It's known for its unique game design by John Trudeau and artwork by Terry Doerzaph. The machine supports up to 4 players, has 6 flippers, 2 ramps, and offers a 3-ball multiball play. A total of 1,230 units were produced, and it operates on the Gottlieb System 80A generation. This pinball machine is a part of Gottlieb's legacy, with an estimated value between $8,320 and $9,680​​.

id: Spirit of 76 (Gottlieb 1975)/Spirit of 76 (Gottlieb 1975) FS-DT-VR SoundMOD v1.0.vpx
name: Spirit of 76 (Gottlieb 1975)
desc:
Spirit of 76 is a pinball game designed by Ed Krynski and Wayne Neyens and released in 1975 by Gottlieb. The pinball machine should not be confused with the pinball machine The Spirit of '76 by Mirco Games, Inc.

Two other versions of this pinball machine were released in 1976: Pioneer - a two-player version and New York - a special 2-player Add-a-ball version in celebration of the 1976 lifting of the ban of pinball in New York City.

Spirit of 76 was made to celebrate the 200th birthday of the United States. The backbox of the machine has art from America's heroes. The red white and blue theme dominates the game. Minutemen, covered wagons and rockets are displayed on the playfield. Stars and stripes, representing the flag of the United States, are on the side of the table.

id: Split Second 1981 (Stern Pinball)/Split Second (Stern 1981) Physics Sound VR MOD 1.1.vpx
name: Split Second
desc: The "Split Second" pinball machine, created by Stern Electronics in August 1981, features a wide body cabinet, digital display, and supports up to 4 players. It includes 4 flippers, 1 ramp, and offers a 3-ball multiball play. The game was designed by Harry Williams, with artwork by Doug Watson and Gerry Simkus. It's known for its solid state technology and is part of the Stern M-200 MPU generation. The estimated value of this machine ranges between $2,770 and $3,230​​.

name: SpongeBob's Bikini Bottom Pinball
desc: Introducing VPW's latest creation, SpongeBob's Bikini Bottom Pinball by the original table author, Skillshot! Dive into the deep sea fun with your favorite sponge and friends in this exciting new table. Immerse yourself in Bikini Bottom's quirky world with innovative gameplay and stunning graphics. Get ready for a pinball adventure like no other!

id: Spy Hunter 1984 (Bally)/Spy Hunter (Bally 1984) Physics Sound Hybrid MOD 1.1.vpx
name: Spy Hunter
desc:
Spy Hunter is a Pinball Spin-Off of the hit arcade racing game of the same name. Designed by Greg Kmiec with art by Tony Ramunni, it was released by Bally/Midway in 1984.
In this game, the player must help Agent GK and his partner as they battle enemy agents on land, sea, and air. Make the Skill Shot to open the safety gate, then take to the air with missiles and a one-man jet to double and triple the playfield targets. Drive through the Weapons Warehouse for armament, then drop out to engage the target in a deadly battle over the drain. Knock down the drop targets to build the score towards a Special, hit the SHOT targets to light the spinner, then enter the saucer hideout and collect the Hunter bonus.

name: Star Action (Williams 1973)
desc:
Notable Features: Flippers (2), Pop bumpers (3), Slingshots (2), Drop targets (4), Spinning posts. End-of-ball bonus. 3 or 5 balls.

Backglass has five silkscreened stars above the word 'STAR'. They are not visible to the player unless illuminated from behind.

The small print on the backglass showing the manufacturer name and copyright date also shows the name 'Triple Action' which is the replay version of this game. The small print on the playfield shows the correct name 'Star Action'.

Maximum displayed point score: 1,999,990 points.

Sounds: 3 chimes, knocker. The knocker operates once for each added ball.

name: Star Gazer
desc: Star Gazer is a 1980 pinball table designed by Brian Poklacki and released by Stern. The gazer in question is a Hot Gypsy Woman who uses her powers of prognostication to guide players to a high score. Hit the lower drop target banks to raise the bonus multiplier, then collect the twelve signs of the Zodiac to advance the Star Bonus and get a chance at the Extra Ball. Collect the various Stars on the playfield to lock the Spinner values, but beware of the semicircle scoops feeding each flipper, as they are capricious and unpredictable.

name: Star God (Zaccaria 1980)
desc: Star God is a sci-fi themed solid-state pinball machine by Zaccaria, featuring two flippers, drop targets, pop bumpers, and colorful futuristic artwork. It's known for its fast gameplay and distinctive Italian design.

name: Star Light (Williams 1984)
desc: Star Light is a solid-state pinball machine featuring a space theme, it includes two flippers and offers a two-ball multiball feature. Only 100 units were produced, making it a rare collectible. Compare this playfield layout to that of Williams' 1979 wide-body game, Laser Ball.

id: Star Race (Gottlieb 1980)/Star Race (Gottlieb 1980) w VR Room v2.0.0.vpx
name: Star Race (Gottlieb 1980)
desc:
Gottlieb's Race Thru Space!  Another extended wide-body machine like Circus.  Lots of fun to play, two Varitargets, a hard to hit bonus saucer, and fast loops.

Game objectives summary: Spell out S-T-A-R or R-A-C-E on the vari-targets to scoop the Special. Make the top rollover lanes to increase the multiplier bonus value of the central drop-targets. Look to make the top loop or drop the top left drop-target bank a couple of times to set up the Extra Ball chance.

name: Star Trek
desc:
The Star Trek pinball machine from 1979, manufactured by Bally, is a classic game that holds the distinction of being the first officially licensed Star Trek pinball game. A total of 16,842 units were produced. The machine featured several iterations of backglass designs, one with colorful TV series uniforms and another modified to align with the Star Trek movie's aesthetics, shifting characters into gray, single-color clothing. This change occurred early in the production to match the release of the Star Trek movie at the time.
The gameplay includes two flippers, three pop bumpers, two slingshots, a four-bank of drop targets, five standup targets, two star rollovers, a kick-out hole (saucer), and a free-ball return to the shooter lane. It's designed for up to four players and does not feature ramps or multiball, characteristic of many solid-state pinball machines from that era. The artwork was done by Kevin O'Connor, with game design by Gary Gayton.
An interesting aspect of this machine is its sound system, which utilized the AS-2518-32 sound board, marking Bally's first generation of electronic sound boards. The sounds were primarily based around the 10, 100, and 1000 point chimes and did not specifically pay homage to the Star Trek theme. However, the designers managed to string together various sounds to create tunes for the start of the game, saucer exit, Bally bonus, and game end.

id: Star Trek 25th Anniversary (Data East 1991)/Star Trek 25th Anniversary (Data East 1991) Hanibals 4k Mod.vpx
name: Star Trek 25th Anniversary (Data East 1991)
desc: The Star Trek 25th Anniversary pinball machine, produced by Data East in 1991, is a celebration of the original Star Trek series. This game features side art of the original Enterprise NCC-1701, along with head artwork and phrases iconic to the Star Trek universe, like "To boldly go where no man has gone before." The playfield is adorned with images of Captain Kirk, Spock, and other characters, emphasizing the rich narrative of the Star Trek series. The game includes a variety of mechanical features such as multiball, an automatic plunger, swinging targets, 4-bank drop targets, and a kickout saucer. One of the standout features is the patented "Transporter Effect" backglass animation, offering a unique visual experience. The design team includes Joe Kaminkow and Ed Cebula, with artwork by Margaret Hudson and Kevin O'Connor, and sound and music by Brian Schmidt. Kristina Donofrio contributed to the software, rounding out a team that created a game filled with the spirit of exploration and adventure that defines Star Trek​​​​​​.

id: Star Trek LE (Stern 2013)/Star Trek LE (Stern 2013) LW.vpx
name: Star Trek LE (Stern 2013)
desc:
Stern Star Trek pinball machine, released in 2013, is based on the 2009 "Star Trek" film and its sequel "Star Trek Into Darkness." Designed by Steve Ritchie, this machine puts players in the role of Captain James T. Kirk, leading the crew of the USS Enterprise on various missions to protect the Federation.

Related machines: Star Trek (Premium), Star Trek (Pro), Star Trek (LE), Star Trek (Vault), Star Trek (Premium Vault), Star Trek (Enterprise Limited Edition)

name: Star Trek The Next Generation
desc:
The Star Trek: The Next Generation pinball machine, created by Williams Electronic Games in November 1993, is celebrated for its engaging gameplay and strong thematic integration. Designed by Steve Ritchie, it features mechanics by Carl Biagi, software by Dwight Sullivan and Matt Coriale, artwork by Greg Freres, animations by Eugene Geer and Scott Slomiany, with sound and music by Dan Forden​​.
The game is a widebody pinball adventure, part of the SuperPin series, and incorporates a rich array of missions that reflect episodes from the TV series, such as Time Rift, Worm Hole, Search The Galaxy, Battle Simulation, Q's Challenge, Rescue, and Asteroid Threat. Completing these missions advances players towards the ultimate challenge, The Final Frontier, a wizard mode that offers significant point scoring opportunities​​.
Players can earn various "Artifacts" that increase the value of The Final Frontier mission, with gameplay features like a unique three-flipper setup, kickbacks to save the ball from draining, and shuttle launches that contribute to game progression. Special modes like Holodeck adventures add depth, along with video modes triggered in unique ways, such as "Riker's Poker Night"​​.

id: Star Wars 1992 (Data East)/Star Wars (Data East 1992) VPW v1.2.2.vpx
name: Star Wars
desc: Join the Rebel Alliance for death defying action in your quest to destroy the Empire's ultimate weapon, the evil Death Star. Make the universe safe again while collecting tri-ball and double jackpots as you and Luke Skywalker save the day.

name: Star Wars Bounty Hunter (Original)
desc:
The Star Wars Bounty Hunter (2021) table by Tartzani (also known as Oqqsan) is one of the most polished "Original" tables in the VPX world. It’s not a recreation of an old physical machine; it’s a high-end, modern digital tribute that heavily leans into The Mandalorian and the broader bounty hunter lore.

The Table Vibe

This isn't a clunky EM machine. It’s a "Next Gen" VPX experience. It uses the VPW (Visual Pinball Workshop) physics and lighting standards, meaning it feels heavy, fast, and incredibly realistic. The aesthetic is "Dark Gritty Sci-Fi"—think heavy bass, neon highlights, and high-fidelity sound clips from the Disney+ series.

Key Gameplay Features

The Mission System: The table is objective-driven. You’re not just hitting bumpers; you’re completing bounties. You’ll recognize missions and callouts directly from the show (e.g., hunting down targets for the Guild).

Dynamic Lighting & Shadows: It utilizes the "VPW Example Table" features, meaning you get real-time ball reflections and shadows that move across the playfield as the ball zips around.

Orbital Scoreboard: It supports the Orbital framework, giving you a sleek, integrated look for your scores and mission progress.

The Wizard Mode (Dark Troopers): The ultimate goal is a brutal multi-ball battle against Dark Troopers. It’s high-stakes, high-score, and visually chaotic in the best way possible.

Audio Immersion: It features a deep, cinematic soundtrack (often paired with the Mandalorian theme) and high-quality "pew-pew" laser sound effects and mechanical "clunks" that make it feel like a physical machine.

Technical Breakdown (VPX Specs)

Feature	Details
Author	Tartzani / Oqqsan
Year	2021 (v3.0 released May 2021)
Physics	VPW (Visual Pinball Workshop) standards
ROM Required	None (It's an "Original" script-based table)
Special Tech	FlexDMD support, VR Room mode, and 23 different ball skin options

name: Star Wars Episode 1
desc:
"Star Wars Episode I" from 1999 is a notable entry in the realm of visual pinball games, celebrated for its innovative integration of pinball mechanics with digital technology. This game, released by Williams Electronics under the Pinball 2000 platform, represents a significant evolution in pinball design, melding traditional physical pinball elements with an overlay of computer-generated imagery (CGI).
The game's cabinet is a standard upright pinball machine body, but with a distinct technological twist. At its core, it features a full-sized pinball playfield, complete with flippers, bumpers, ramps, and various targets. However, what sets it apart is the use of a reflection-based display system that projects CGI animations onto the playfield's surface. This system creates an illusion of depth and interaction between the physical ball and digital characters or objects. The result is a dynamic and immersive gameplay experience that extends the narrative and visual excitement beyond traditional pinball boundaries.
The artwork and thematic elements are deeply rooted in the "Star Wars Episode I: The Phantom Menace" movie, showcasing key characters such as Qui-Gon Jinn, Obi-Wan Kenobi, Anakin Skywalker, and the villainous Darth Maul. The cabinet and backglass are adorned with high-quality graphics depicting these characters, drawing players into the Star Wars universe.
Gameplay involves completing various missions aligned with the movie's plot, aiming to progress through the story while achieving high scores. Players can engage in battles with Darth Maul, participate in pod races, or undertake Jedi training, all through the pinball mechanisms. The integration of sound effects, voice clips from the movie, and John Williams' iconic score adds to the game's allure, providing an audio-visual experience that complements the physical gameplay.
"Star Wars Episode I" pinball game stands as a memorable example of how technology can enhance traditional arcade games, offering fans of the franchise and pinball enthusiasts alike a unique and engaging way to experience the galaxy far, far away.

name: Star Wars Redux (BorGlieb 2019)
desc: Inspired by the original Star Wars trilogy, this Pinball reimagines the classic saga in a fast, retro style. Players battle through iconic space and ground combat—deflecting TIE fighters, destroying Imperial wall targets, and powering up the Death Star trench run. With nostalgic 8-bit Star Wars music, crisp artwork by BorgDog, and enhanced spinner and sound effects, it offers a solid-state pinball feel infused with galactic charm.

name: Star Wars The Bad Batch
desc:
Here's a little Star Wars Bad Batch retheme I did of JP's Gamatron. Thanks to JP for all that he gives to the community including making his tables available for modification. He also gave me a few tips when I was trying to work a few scripting issues out. Many, many thanks.

Be sure to put the theme song mp3 in your VisualPinball/music folder.

id: Star Wars Trilogy 1997 (Sega)/Star Wars Trilogy (Sega 1997) Physics Sound Hybrid MOD 1.1.vpx
name: Star Wars Trilogy
desc:
Five years after Data East's own table, Sega Pinball returned to the galaxy far, far away with Star Wars Trilogy, released at the same time as the Special Edition of the original films. Designed by Joe Kaminkow and Joe Balcer with artwork by Morgan Weistling, the game came out in March 1997 just as the Special Editions finished playing in theaters.
The most prominent features of the playfield are the spaceships, with the player's X-Wing facing off against Vader's TIE Advanced; a turbolaser turret fires between them, while a frozen Han Solo sits on the lower-right side. There are six tasks that the player must complete, such as scoring various jackpots, performing heroic deeds, and thawing Han from the carbonite. Only then can the player confront Darth Vader by loading a pinball into the X-Wing, knocking down his phalanx of TIE fighters, then scoring a direct hit on his ship. Use the Force to light the jackpot and try for the Millenium Falcon's multiball, but be prepared to test your knowledge of Star Wars trivia. Operators could add extra visual appeal by choosing a 3D lenticular backbox print instead of the standard one.

name: Stargate
desc:
Stargate is a Licensed Pinball Table released in 1995 by Gottlieb (under the Premier label). It was designed by Ray Tanzer and Jon Norris, with artwork by David Moore and Constantino and Jeanine Mitchell.
Based on the 1994 sci-fi action movie starring James Spader and Kurt Russell, this pinball has players recreate the events of the film. Activate the Transporter, trade Quartz for various awards, then make it through the Sandstorm and attack Ra's Temple. Collect the White Pyramids, lead the miners in a rebellion, use the Sarcophagus to raise the dead, then slip under the floating Guardian statues. Levitate the Pyramid and attack the flying Glidercraft, collect the seven Segments to activate the Stargate, then activate the Eye of Ra and prove yourself the master of Abydan.

name: Stars
desc: The "Stars" pinball machine, produced in March 1978 by Stern Electronics, Inc., is a solid-state game designed by Steve Kirk with artwork by Jorge Obregon. It features a digital display, accommodates up to 4 players, and includes 2 flippers but no ramps or multiball. An estimated 5,127 units were produced, and it's valued between $2500 and $2900. The game is tagged as sci-fi and space-themed​​.

id: Startship Troopers 1997 (Sega)/Starship Troopers (Sega 1997) VPW Mod v2.0.vpx
name: Starship Troopers
desc:
Starship Troopers is an arcade pinball game based on Paul Verhoeven's film adaptation of Robert A. Heinlein's sci-fi novel. It was designed by Joe Kaminkow and Joe Balcer, illustrated by Morgan Weistling, and released by Sega Pinball in 1997.
The pinball table casts the player as a member of the Mobile Infantry, who must visit six planets and kill all of the Arachnids in the Federation's Bug War. Blast the Warriors, Plasma Bugs, Hoppers and Tankers to secure a planet, then try to capture the Brain Bug before it escapes. Secure the planet and then advance to the next, or Arm the Nukes and Nuke 'em instead. Practice your gunnery skills on the Live Fire Assault Range, perform Recons for various awards, then use the right Mini-Flipper to score Double Kills and Advance In Rank. Survive long enough to make your way to Klendathu, then kill all the Bugs and Double Nuke them all to extinction.

name: Stellar Wars
desc:
Stellar Wars is a pinball game designed by Steve Ritchie and illustrated by Constantino and Jeanine Mitchell. It was released by Williams Electronics in 1979, and is noted for being the first game Ritchie created for Williams.
Riding the popularity of science-fiction media in The '70s, Stellar Wars depicts a space battle between two sides over an unspecified planet. From the cockpit of your Space Fighter, shoot the various targets and repel the invading fleet. Hit the center targets to increases the Eject Hole value for an Extra Ball, hit the right targets to raise the values of the Spinner and the Captive ball, then shoot the left targets and go after the bumpers. Nudge the table to roll over the WARS inlanes, then spell STELLAR WARS and watch the Battlescope explode in a frenzy of firepower.

name: Stingray
desc:
Roger Sharpe tells us that he and Sam Stern designed this game, and Mike Kubin did the build-up of the whitewood.
'Stingray' is one of two 4-player games made by Stern Electronics that has a switch setting to convert the game to 2-player operation. This is accomplished by setting CPU Switch 25 to its OFF position. Designer Mike Kubin tells us that there were certain markets that wanted only 2-player games, although he could not recall which countries they were. Because the 3rd and 4th player score displays would be disabled for this, and likely were not even installed, Stern made a special 2-player backglass for these games. Included in this listing is one of these backglasses along with its backbox missing the 3rd and 4th displays. We do not know how many games were shipped with the 2-player backglass.
The game that followed this one in production, Stars, is the other game that has this 2-player CPU option. Stern discontinued the option in subsequent games.

name: Strange Science
desc:
Strange Science is a Physical Pinball Table designed by Dan Langlois and illustrated by Greg Freres. It was released by Bally/Midway in 1986.
On a dark and stormy night, frisky teens Jodi and Todd venture into an abandoned old house, only to get separated by a Mad Scientist living within. Dr. Shock introduces Jodi to Gertrude the chimpanzee, then announces his wild experiment to swap their bodies. While Todd rushes to save her, the player must use the Particle Accelerator and the Atom Smasher to power up the experiment, and activate the Anti-Gravity machine to move balls up the playfield. Trigger the Power Saver to prevent drains down the outlane, fill up the test tube, then start a five-ball multiball spree and start some Strange Science!

id: Street Fighter II 1993 (Gottlieb)/Street Fighter II (Gottlieb 1993) VPW 2.0.1.vpx
name: Street Fighter 2
desc: The Visual Pinball version of Street Fighter II, based on the Premier/Gottlieb table from 1993, has been recreated to closely mimic the original table's layout and gameplay. The table incorporates custom graphics and has undergone several updates to improve its graphics, physics, and overall gameplay experience. It features enhanced images, updated scripts, and improved physics to provide a more realistic pinball experience. Additionally, the recreation includes 3D figures to replace pictures, bringing more depth and visual appeal to the game. The updates have focused on details such as the neon FIGHTER lights visibility, environmental image enhancements for better shadow effects, and sound adjustments for a more immersive experience​​​​.

name: Strikes And Spares
desc:
"Strikes and Spares" is a classic pinball machine released in 1978 by Bally Manufacturing Co. It is themed around the sport of bowling and is well-known for its vibrant artwork and engaging gameplay. The visual design of the playfield features a lively and colorful representation of a bowling scene, complete with illustrations of male and female bowlers in action. The artwork often reflects the fashion and style of the late 1970s, showcasing characters in the attire typical of the era.
The playfield is dotted with various targets, bumpers, and lanes that resemble bowling pins and alleys, encouraging players to "knock down" pins by hitting these targets with the pinball. The machine's backglass is particularly notable for its striking design, often featuring a prominent image of a female bowler in a dynamic pose, adding to the machine's eye-catching appeal.
"Strikes and Spares" includes features typical of pinball machines of its time, such as score reels, mechanical bells, and chimes for sound effects, enhancing the tactile and auditory experience of the game. The objective is to score points by hitting targets and completing certain combinations, with the ultimate goal of achieving a high score, much like achieving a high score in an actual game of bowling.
This pinball machine has been celebrated for its blend of challenging gameplay and distinctive artwork, making it a favorite among collectors and enthusiasts of vintage pinball machines. Its theme, tied closely to bowling, offers a unique twist on the traditional pinball experience, further solidifying its place in the history of classic arcade games.

id: Strikes N' Spares (Premier 1995)/Strikes N' Spares(Premier 1995) Lebowski Mod1.1.vpx
name: Strikes N' Spares
desc: Strikes N' Spares brings bowling to the pinball world with fast-paced, casual gameplay. Players compete in a full 10-frame game, using 1 or 2 balls per frame just like real bowling. The machine features two DMD displays: the upper one tracks frame and game progress, while the lower provides play information. Designed as a novelty game, it offers simplified rules, humorous callouts, and a single flipper layout, perfect for quick fun and lighthearted competition.

name: Super Mario Bros.
desc:
The Visual Pinball version of "Super Mario Bros." is a digital recreation of the original physical pinball machine themed around the iconic Nintendo video game series. This version is designed to emulate the look, feel, and gameplay of the original pinball machine, which was originally released by Gottlieb in 1992. The game features artwork, themes, and characters from the "Super Mario Bros." universe, including Mario, Luigi, Princess Peach, and various enemies like Goombas and Koopa Troopas.
The table layout includes ramps, bumpers, and targets themed after the game's world, offering players various missions and objectives to complete, reminiscent of the platformer's levels and challenges. Players can trigger special modes and bonuses by hitting specific targets, simulating the adventure and exploration aspects of "Super Mario Bros." games.
Visual Pinball's digital rendition allows for enhancements such as improved graphics and sound effects, while also providing the tactile feedback and physics that pinball enthusiasts appreciate. This makes it a beloved choice for fans of pinball and the Super Mario series, offering a nostalgic blend of two classic gaming experiences.

id: Super Mario Bros. Mushroom World 1992 (Gottlieb)/Super Mario Bros. Mushroom World (Premier 1992) v1.0.4i.vpx
name: Super Mario Bros. Mushroom World
desc:
Super Mario Bros. Mushroom World is a Pinball Table based on the popular video game franchise, designed by Ray Tanzer and released by Gottlieb in 1992. Unlike Gottlieb's earlier Super Mario Bros. pinball, Mushroom World is expressly designed for younger players. The playfield cabinet is not as long as a conventional pinball machine, and the game could be equipped with shorter legs to lower its height. Operators could set the game to one of two difficulty modes, and it could be configured to reward redemption tickets.
The game itself is a simplified version of Super Mario Bros. 3. Mario must travel through seven lands of Mushroom World and clear each one. Doing so opens up the eighth world, Dark Land, with lots of opportunities for players to score points (or tickets). Powerups provide Mario with fire, frog, and raccoon powers, while the Warp Whistle opens a ramp for hidden secrets.

name: Super Orbit (Gottlieb 1983)
desc: Super Orbit is a streamlined, space-themed solid-state pinball machine. It features two flippers, three pop bumpers, a spinner, spinning and vari-target shots, and rewards skillful orbit loops and bonus collection through the upper-right gate. It shares the same playfield layout as the EM games Orbit (1971) and Outer Space (1972), and is possibly the first Gottlieb game to produce a sound effect by pressing the flipper buttons during attract mode.

name: Super Spin (Gottlieb 1977)
desc:
1977 Gottlieb's "Super Spin" 2 player pinball fun from the premier manufacture of vintage pinball. Highly collectable and considered by some to be the king of the EM (electromechanical) pinball machines. Family friendly futuristic surfing ride theme hop on board the Super Spin.
 Super Spin is a great game from the last full year of electromechanical pinball from Gottlieb the King of EM pinball manufactures. Super Spin is the rarer 2 player version of the 4 player Jet Spin

Feature packed action for two players:

Old school Roto target spins for different scoring values
Old school vari-target the harder you hit it the higher the scoring
Two ways to win Specials
Two ways to win extra balls
Two rebuilt pop bumpers
One kick out hole
100,000 scoring for over the top pinball fun

name: Super-Flite (Williams 1974)
desc: Super-Flite features an outer space theme, prominently displaying a 1960s military jet against a starry background on the backglass. The 4-player version of this game is Williams' 1974 'Strato-Flite'.

name: Superman
desc:
Superman is an arcade pinball game designed by Steve Ritchie, with artwork by George Opperman and programmed by Eugene Jarvis. It was released by Atari in 1979.
As with other Pinball games of The '70s, Superman has a series of objectives but no overarching plot or goal beyond a high score. Light the top rollovers to raise the bonus multiplier, then hit the Metropolis dropdown targets to enable various bonuses. Shoot through the Fortress of Solitude or Luthor's Lair to return to the top of the board, and spell SUPERMAN to get extra points and light the Special.

name: Superman and The Justice League (Original 2024)
desc:
Hello everyone, I'm sharing the Superman and The Justice League table with the community.

We start with thanks to
Mr JPSalas for his help, thank you JP.
Mr James VPG for tests and videos

Goal of the game help Superman to reform the Justice League
 you must complete 12 missions and 3 Boss missions plus 3 bonus missions.
Table contains 4 multiball modes, 12 music from films or series and a bonus,
voices from Superman films, multiple jackpot, extra ball, multiplier bonus, etc.
Change lighting ambiance with the Lmagna and Rmagna buttons
There is the DOF to achieve
 good fun

name: Supersonic
desc:
The playfield is identical in design to Bally's 1976 'Star Ship'.
The first Concorde, the 001, flew its maiden flight on March 2, 1969 over France. The first commercial passenger flights took place on January 21, 1976 when a British Airways flight traveled from Heathrow to Bahrain at the same time that an Air France jet flew from Paris to Rio de Janeiro. But for a quarter, you could fly supersonic in 1979 and have the best seat in the house.

name: Surf'n Safari
desc:
Surf'n Safari isn't a visual pinball program itself, but a digital recreation of a 1991 pinball machine  made by Gottlieb that can be played on some visual pinball programs like Visual Pinball X (VPX)  or Visual Pinball 8 (VP8). These programs are pinball simulators that allow you to play digital versions of classic pinball tables on your computer.
As the name suggests, the table has a jungle and surfing theme, with artwork depicting beaches, waves, and jungle animals.
The objective is to score points by hitting targets, ramps, and loops, and completing certain tasks like getting the ball to lock into specific locations.
The table likely has various features that replicate the original pinball machine, such as working flippers, a digital scoring display, and sound effects. Some recreations may even include realistic physics that simulate the ball's movement.

id: Swamp Thing - Bayou Edition (Original)/Swamp Thing 2.1.1 Bayou Edition (LTek 2024).vpx
name: Swamp Thing - Bayou Edition (Original)
desc:
The "Serious Sam Pinball" from 2017 is an original table created for Visual Pinball X (VPX), inspired by Croteam's game "Serious Sam: The Second Encounter". The creator, jpsalas, decided to use graphics not directly from the game itself but from various Maya images and models to craft a unique visual experience. This pinball table stands out because it solely relies on VPX, excluding the need for any external programs, and includes all necessary sounds and music within the table itself.
Significant updates and improvements have been made to the table since its initial release, including updated physics for more realistic gameplay, a new set of mechanical sounds for enhanced audio experience, and fixes to flashers for better visual effects. Moreover, the latest version introduced LUT images adjustments for varied visual tones and warmer shades, offering players the ability to customize their visual experience further.
The table design is deeply integrated with elements and characters from "Serious Sam: The Second Encounter", providing a thematic adventure as players navigate the pinball gameplay. Despite the rich content and complexity, the creator assures that the rules are straightforward and easy to grasp, with a document available for those who wish to understand the gameplay mechanics in depth.

name: Swords Of Fury
desc:
"Swords of Fury" is a pinball machine released in June 1988 by Williams Electronic Games, Inc. This game falls within the fantasy-knights-wizard/magic theme and was designed by Steve Kirk, Tony Kraemer, and Doug Watson, with music by Brian Schmidt. It's a solid-state electronic pinball machine, identified as part of the Williams System 11B generation. The production run for "Swords of Fury" was relatively limited, with only 2,705 units produced​​​​.
The gameplay features include the opportunity to adventure through the Ogres Alley, where caution is advised as it may come at a cost. Players are encouraged to collect the AVENGER targets and then shoot the ramp for high scores and an extra ball. Additionally, braving the Titan Tunnel to lock balls and start multiball is a key aspect of the game. Once a player reaches 2 million points, the table increases in difficulty, testing the player's pinball skills further. Engaging in battles on the mini-playfield can lead to significant jackpots, complemented by one of the most acclaimed soundtracks in pinball history​​.

id: Tales From The Crypt 1993 (Data East)/Tales from the Crypt (Data East 1993) VPW v1.22.vpx
name: Tales From The Crypt
desc:
Tales from the Crypt is a licensed pinball machine based on the 1950s horror comic books and the horror anthology television series on HBO. The game was designed by John Borg, with art by Kurt Andersen and Markus Rothkranz, and released by Data East in 1993.
Similar to its namesakes, the Crypt game is centered on twelve frightful "Creature Features". As the cabinet shakes with the souls of previous players, Crack some Skulls, rob the Crypt, dodge the Guillotines, then try to select a Door Prize (but avoid the hangman!). Hit the Keeper's eyeballs, pound on the Tombstone, then confront the Werewolf and Play the Organ. Complete all twelve Features, then sit in the Electric Chair and fire it up for the Crypt Jam — all while the Crypt Keeper cackles away with his nonstop barrage of horror(-ble) puns...

id: Tales Of The Arabian Nights 1996 (Williams)/Tales of the Arabian Nights (Williams 1996) v600.vpx
name: Tales of the Arabian Nights
desc:
This is another great game by John Popadiuk Jr. It is clearly inspired by his earlier success, Theatre of Magic. The difficulty level is about the same; even though it is much easier to progress through the modes and reach the final mode, the playfield is more difficult. The game is based on the Arabian Nights, of course, with a Lamp, a Genie, and a flying carpet ramp. It has a beautiful and detailed backglass, which reminds me of a Magic card - can you guess which expansion it would be from? :-)
Surprisingly, it is a very low scoring game. Williams seems to have done what Mexico did a few year ago, and chop three zeroes off their "currency". Scores are about one thousand times less than Attack from Mars. Replay is usually around 10-20 million, high scores around 40 million or so, anything over 100 million is a world-class score. Highest score I've ever seen is over one billion! The font for the high scores is the same as AFM, there's a lot of empty space where the billions would have been. The game rolls over at one billion, good luck getting there...
Another unique thing about Tales from the Arabian Nights (TOTAN) is that it goes out of its way to tell players free games are available. Instead of "Replay at..." it flashes "Free game at..." at the start of the last ball. During Match, it tells the players that a free game is possible if they match. This is a good feature for people new to pinball, who might not know about the Match feature.
I would like to thank the people who helped me with this. Their names and email addresses are listed at the end of this Rule Sheet.

name: Target Alpha (Gottlieb 1976)
desc: Target Alpha is a four-player reimagining of Gottlieb's classic one-player wedgehead El Dorado. Contrary to El Dorado's old west theme, Target Alpha features a science fiction theme complete with flying machines, laser guns and space helmets. A few features are stripped away from the original El Dorado ruleset, and a few are added to compliment the multi-player operation. The game features fifteen drop targets, including a massive row of ten that runs across the top of the playfield. Gottlieb also released Solar City, the same design with new art and two player operation, the same year.

name: Taxi
desc:
Taxi is a Physical Pinball Table designed by Mark Ritchie with art by Python Anghelo. It was released in 1988 by Williams Electronics.
Compared to other Pinball games of the time, Taxi is deceptively simple. As a taxi driver, pick up a crazy cast of characters — including former Soviet Leader Mikhail Gorbachev (Gorbie), Dracula, and Santa Claus — then take them to the airport and collect the jackpot. The longer you play, the more tips you'll put on the meter, so take the Express Lane and loop the airport for an even bigger score.

name: Team One (Gottlieb 1977)
desc: Team One features a magic and sorcery theme and includes two flippers, five pop bumpers, ten drop targets, and a unique center target mechanism that increases bonus value. The replay version of this game is Gottlieb's 1975 'Abra Ca Dabra' but with different artwork. The Add-a-ball version for export to Italy is Gottlieb's 1977 'Kicker'.

name: Teed Off
desc: "Tee'd Off," created by Gottlieb in May 1993, is a pinball machine known for its unique theme centered around golf, drawing comparisons to the popular "Caddyshack" movie. It features a design by Ray Tanzer and Jon Norris. The game is distinguished by its fun and engaging golf theme, which has made it a memorable piece for both arcade goers and collectors. Although comparisons are often made with Williams' "No Good Gofers," "Tee'd Off" holds its own with distinct gameplay and thematic elements​​.

id: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (Data East 1991)/Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (Data East 1991) v1.2.3f.vpx
name: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (Data East 1991)
desc:
Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles is a 1991 pinball machine based off the multi-media franchise of the same name (more specifically the 80's cartoon), made by Data East. It was designed by Ed Cebula and Joe Kaminkow, with artwork by Kevin O'Connor and Paul Faris.

It has a number of somewhat interesting features, such as a spinning pizza ala Whirlwind, two prominent ramps, and a sewer shot that caused the ball to momentarily disappear under the playfield.

name: Terminator 2: Judgment Day
desc:
Terminator 2: Judgment Day is a 1991 arcade pinball game designed by Steve Ritchie and released by Williams Electronics. It is based on the movie of the same name, and Arnold Schwarzenegger reprised his role as The Terminator. Unsurprisingly, the game rode the movie's popularity to become the best-selling pinball machine of 1991 by a landslide.
Instead of trying to replicate the plot of the film, the pinball instead opts to recreate the emotional highlights with a whirlwind of nonstop action. Shoot the two Cyberdyne ramps to raise the Security Levels, repeatedly hit the Chase Loop for progressive bonuses, then fire the ball over the left loop and Escape into the saucer to collect more rewards. Hit the dropdown target below the T-800's skull, then load the swinging cannon and shoot the HK-Aerial across the playfield to start multiball. But to score the Super Jackpot among all the chaos will require the cool demeanor of a robot...
Terminator 2 was one of the first pinball games to use a dot-matrix display, and the first pinball game to feature a Video Mode. It also eschews the traditional plunger for an automatic plunger (in the form of a gun), and features a ball-firing cannon on the right side of the playfield.

id: Terminator 3 Rise Of The Machines 2003 (Stern Pinball)/Terminator 3 (Stern 2003) Siggi-TW VLM mod.vpx
name: Terminator 3: Rise of the Machines
desc:
Eight years after No Fear: Dangerous Sports, Steve Ritchie returned to arcade pinball with Terminator 3: Rise of the Machines. Released by Stern Pinball in 2003, this table features art by Kevin O'Connor, original voice clips by Arnold Schwarzenegger, and a ball-launching RPG in the backbox itself.
As one would expect, this pinball game follows the plot of the movie, with the player as the T-850 Terminator fighting against the T-X. Since her Plasma Cannon easily outclasses the T-850, the player must first travel around the playfield, collecting weapons and BFGs. Look for opportunities for multiball, Quick Fire, and Payback Time, but don't hesitate to Escape if necessary. Avoid getting distracted when the Command Center initiates a Red Alert, and be ready to use the backglass RPG at the T-X when the time comes. Survive long enough for the Final Battle, and try to Finish Her before she does the same to you.

name: Terrifier Sensative Stomach (Original)
desc: Can you escape the wrath of art the clown? Battle through 15+ mos, and discover what lurks in the shadows of this grotesque pinball experience. Sharpen your skills to defeat the wizard modes that await you in this terrifying thrill ride. Dou have the stomach to face hell in its circus? Let's see your guts.

name: The Addams Family (Bally 1992)
desc: The Addams Family, released in March 1992, is the best selling pinball machine of all time. Manufactured by Midway (under the Bally name), it is a solid state electronic pinball arcade game. It was based on the 1991 film of the same name, and features custom speech (mostly derived from the motion picture) by the stars of the film, Raul Julia and Anjelica Huston. More than 20,000 units have been sold thus far.

id: Amazing Spider-Man 1980 (Gottlieb)/Amazing Spiderman (Gottlieb 1980) Sinister Six Edition v1.1.vpx
name: The Amazing Spideman
desc: The Amazing Spiderman is a wide-body pinball, release in 1980 by Gottlieb. Based on the Marvel character it features character poses taken directly from Marvel comics and style guides including Aunt May, Kingpin, Lizard, Scorpion, Vulture, Black Widow, Kraven the Hunter and the Green Goblin. It was the first of Gottlieb's System 80 design pinball machines. It also was the first Gottlieb pinball, with an "attract mode" lighting. In which various playfield lights, alternate between off an on. It was also the first solid state pinball with the speaker in the backbox instead of the bottom cabinet.

name: The Avengers Pro (Stern 2012)
desc:
The Avengers (Stern, 2012) is a fast-paced pinball machine featuring Marvel's superhero team. With vibrant comic-style artwork, multiball action, and unique features like the spinning Tesseract cube and Hulk bash toy, it delivers an intense, action-packed experience.

Related machines: The Avengers, The Avengers (LE), The Avengers (Premium), The Avengers Hulk (LE)

name: The Beatles
desc:
The Beatles pinball machine will immerse players in 1960’s Beatlemania and feature nine timeless hit songs from that era:

A Hard Day’s Night
Can’t Buy Me Love
Ticket to Ride
All My Loving
Help
Drive My Car
It Won’t Be Long
I Should Have Known Better
Taxman

The game also features iconic introductions by Ed Sullivan along with custom speech and callouts by Hall of Fame disk jockey, Cousin Brucie.  Cousin Brucie introduced The Beatles at New York’s Shea Stadium in 1965.

The retro-themed playfield features four flippers, eleven drop targets, eight stand-up targets, multiple skill shots, two opto-spinners, a ball-catching magnet and a magnetic spinning record disc in the center of the playfield.  Players, friends and family will enjoy full screen animations as well as simulated reel scoring on the game’s high definition video screen.

All models feature unique art packages and custom powder-coated armor.  The 100 Diamond Editions are numbered, certified collectible and include a mirrored backglass.  The 250 Platinum Editions are numbered and certified collectible.

name: The Champion Pub
desc:
The Champion Pub is a 1998 pinball machine made by Williams Electronics (under the Bally label).
It's centered around the concept of boxing matches held in bars - the player, as a newcomer named "The Kid", must work his way up through the circuit, training to get his health up, before eventually beating the final man, getting the Pub Champion belt, and fending off five more foes in "Ultimate Challenge".
The game's design departs from the norm - there are health meters for the player and his opponent, and there are a number of toys in the machine, the most prominent of which is a large, revolving target that can present either a heavy bag or a boxer figurine. Two others are a small speed bag with a pair of fists and a rotating metal bar styled as a jump rope; each of these is a separate Mini-Game that the player must complete in order to train for the fights, using the flipper buttons to knock the ball against the bag or make it hop over the turning rope.

name: The Exorcist (Original 2023)PUP version
desc: Original table, designed in 2023. This is a tribute to The Exorcist, a 1973 American supernatural horror film directed by William Friedkin. The film stars Ellen Burstyn, Max von Sydow, Jason Miller, and Linda Blair, and follows the demonic possession of a young girl and the attempt to rescue her through an exorcism by two Catholic priests.

name: The Flintstones
desc:
The Flintstones is a Licensed Pinball Table designed by John Trudeau and illustrated by Kevin O'Connor. It was released by Williams Electronics in the summer of 1994, a month after the live-action movie starring John Goodman and Rick Moranis.
The game combines key events from the film with additional animated antics from the prehistoric town of Bedrock. Make Fred's Bronto-Crane spit out various awards, find a job for Barney, then Go Bowling at the Bowl-O-Rama. Use the Smart Ramps to loop pinballs around the flippers for the 1-2-3 Combo, visit Joe's Diner and the Bedrock Water Buffalo Lodge, and make Fred's Choice for a chance at the Mystery Award. Build up more Machine Time to power up the Rock Cutter, then help Fred invent Concrete and collect both the Jackpot and Super Jackpot awards. This is all accompanied with numerous animated displays and original dialog from Goodman, Moranis, and Harvey Korman.

name: The Fog (Gottlieb 1979)
desc:
Original table, designed in 2020. It is based on BorgDog's Space Walk from Gottlieb in 1979.

The Fog is a 1980 American supernatural horror film directed by John Carpenter, who also co-wrote the screenplay and created the music for the film. It stars Adrienne Barbeau, Jamie Lee Curtis, Tom Atkins, Janet Leigh and Hal Holbrook.

name: The Games (Gottlieb 1984)
desc: Simple but hard to master. The goal: collect five medals in one ball and it consists of five shots.  Including captive balls, Vari-target, saucer, and a spinner.  The shots are really fulfilling despite the simple guidelines.  The captive ball, the spinner, and the vari target are examples of critical shots that pay off if you make them, but the ultimate payout an Olympic gold medal—comes from making them properly.

name: The Getaway High Speed 2 (Williams 1992)
desc:
The sequel to Steve Ritchie's game from 1986, The Getaway: High Speed II, is similar to the original game. In both games, you drive your car as fast as you can and avoid the cops.
But the execution on this one is just amazing. Right off the bat you'll notice the supercharger feature at the center of the playfield, which when activated, triggers a magnetic ball accelerator which whips your ball around the metal track quickly for a large point payout.
This game is fast-paced, like most Ritchie games. It also has a lot of flow and is easy to learn and play multiple times. If you're a fan of High Speed, you'll love this game too.

name: The Incredible Hulk (Gottlieb 1979)
desc:
The "Incredible Hulk" pinball table, released by Gottlieb in 1979, is a notable addition to the world of digital pinball, especially within the Visual Pinball 10 (VPX) platform. The table is highly appreciated for its adaptation of the classic pinball experience into a digital format, offering a blend of nostalgic gameplay with modern technology. The VPX version of the table has been developed based on scans of an actual "Incredible Hulk" machine, ensuring a faithful recreation of the original design and play experience. It includes detailed playfield meshes and updates to several primitives, including the apron and gate, enhancing the visual and gameplay fidelity​​.
For enthusiasts looking to delve into the specifics or modify the table, the Visual Pinball X (VPX) version provides flexibility and support for modifications, although the details of these modifications and the process for implementing them would require consultation within the VPX community or resources provided by the developers. The table also supports adjustments such as the number of balls and volume settings, among others, indicating a degree of customization for players to tailor the gameplay experience to their liking​​.

name: The Last Dragon (Original)
desc: Step into “The Last Dragon” Pinball, an electrifying fusion of martial-arts mastery and pinball adrenaline. Join Bruce Leroy Green on his quest to reach the Sublime Glow — battling through six action-packed modes, unleashing Sho'nuff Multiball, and facing the ultimate showdown with the Shogun of Harlem himself!

name: The Lord of the Rings (Stern 2003)
desc: Lord of the Rings – Valinor Edition is a high-end Visual Pinball remake of Stern's 2003 classic, faithfully reimagined by the VPW team. Featuring hand-drawn artwork, 3D-scanned figurines, and advanced lighting effects, the table captures the epic journey across Middle-earth. Players battle through major story arcs like Fellowship, Two Towers, and Return of the King, aiming to unlock the ultimate challenge: the Valinor Wizard Mode. With cinematic visuals and refined gameplay physics, this edition stands as one of the most immersive and faithful virtual pinball recreations to date.

id: The Machine - Bride Of Pinbot (Williams 1991)/The Machine-Bride Of Pinbot (Williams 1991)_VPW_1.0.4.vpx
name: The Machine: Bride of Pin•Bot (Williams 1991)
desc:
The Machine: Bride of Pin•Bot is a pinball game designed by Python Anghelo and John Trudeau. It was released in 1991 by Williams Electronics, and is the sequel to Williams' earlier Pin•Bot.

In the game, the player must assist in the construction of "The Machine", a massive female humanoid robot. The player does this by first shooting a ball into her mouth (enabling her to speak), then shooting two balls into her eye sockets (so she can see). With the Machine complete and fully operational, the job would be done, except an influx of human DNA causes the Bride to undergo an unexpected metamorphosis...

A sequel, Jack•Bot, was released in 1995.

name: The Mandalorian
desc: The history of The Mandalorian is set after the fall of the Galactic Empire and before the emergence of the First Order. The series follows the travails of a lone gunfighter in the outer reaches of the galaxy, far from the authority of the New Republic. In this action-packed pinbal quest, players are transported to a galaxy far, far away as they play as The Mandalorian, teaming up with key allies and protecting Grogu, while battling dangerous enemies and forces across journey. There are Pro, Premium and Limited Edition variants of this table.

name: The Matrix (Original)
desc:
Intro:
Wake up, Neo.
Welcome to The Matrix Pinball, by Pincredibles. Prepare for a pinball adventure like no other.
You are stationed aboard The Nebuchadnezzar aided by Tank, your operator. Tank will help you as you guide the crew; Neo, Trinity, Niobe and Morpheus as they try to free the minds of the human race and free them from the imprisonment of the Matrix.
It won’t be smooth sailing. Agent Smith, Brown and Jones will attempt to stop you at all costs. Cypher is sneaking about, waiting to betray Morpheus and the crew. Sentinels will attack the ship and the Zion outpost.
Visiting the Oracle could bring you some answers and perks to help. Do not forget to go through the training programs to gain perks and increase your Matrix mode score.
Good luck. Maybe Morpheus was right. Maybe you are The One.

****************************************************************

How it came to be: The goal of the Pincredible tables has always been to push things to the next level. All of the work done up to this point has been about building a strong foundation that would allow us to create our own original table.
We began this project on February 27, 2022. By December 2024, I thought we were getting close to the finish line—but there was still so much more to add and improve.
A tremendous amount of work has gone into this from many different people, and the entire process has been an incredible experience.

id: Pabst Can Crusher (Stern 2016)/Pabst Can Crusher (Stern 2016) v2.5.5_d.vpx
name: The Pabst Can Crusher (Stern 2016)
desc:
The Pabst Can Crusher game is themed on the iconic Pabst Blue Ribbon (PBR) beer, and Pabst will be promoting the game at a number of their merchandising and sponsored events.
The game features all-new artwork by Dirty Donny Gillies featuring a typically highly-stylised design and many cameos, such as the band Red Fang who provide the music for the new game.
The Pabst Can Crusher also eschews the weathered wooden cabinet and legs in favour of a more modern design. However, it retains the score reels, backglass light indicators and the electromechanical essence of Big Juicy Melons.
The cabinet shape is also retained from the WhizBang game.

id: The Phantom Of The Opera (Data East 1990)/Phantom Of The Opera (Data East 1990) v1.25.vpx
name: The Phantom Of The Opera (Data East 1990)
desc: The Phantom of the Opera is a 1990 Physical Pinball Table released by Data East. It was designed by Ed Cebula and Joe Kaminkow, with artwork by Paul Faris. Though released during the Broadway musical's runaway success, the game is not based from it. It is instead based on the original 1911 novel by Gaston Leroux. As the Phantom, scurry across the Catwalk, walk behind the Magic Mirror, then arise from the Trap Door behind the stage. Choose between the Scorpion and the Grasshopper, play the Organ and activate its secret passage, then start the three-ball multiball and steel yourself against the sight of the Phantom's disfigured face.
